544309|2026-09.headline: IKS Q2 FY27 revenue INR1,592 crore (+104% YoY, +78% QoQ, TruBridge consolidated for 82 days) with ~28% EBITDA margin; TruBridge treated as flat FY27.
544309|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 is the first full call after the TruBridge acquisition, with 82 days of TruBridge consolidated. Revenue was about INR1,592 crore and EBITDA about INR442 crore (~28%), including roughly INR25 crore of one-time acquisition/integration expenses. Legacy IKS constant-currency revenue grew a little over 13% YoY to about $101 million, and legacy IKS margins held at about 34.5-35%. Management said TruBridge is a year of stabilisation with no significant growth modelled for FY27, with synergies expected to start in the second half of Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +104% YoY in INR; +78% QoQ in INR

financial_highlights.value: INR442 crore (~28%); ~INR459 crore before ESOP cost of ~INR17.5 crore

financial_highlights.change: a little over 13% YoY in USD

financial_highlights.value: ~$68 million for 82 days (run rate ~$75 million per quarter / ~$300 million per year)
INR217 crore; adjusted PAT INR273 crore (~17% of revenue)

financial_highlights.change: reported OCF lower by ~INR96 crore for TruBridge acquisition payment (non-recurring)

financial_highlights.value: INR101 crore (~$9 million interest for part-period)

segments.name: Legacy IKS (ambulatory / physician groups)
segments.commentary: Constant-currency revenue ~$101 million, +a little over 13% YoY; underlying EBITDA margin ~34.5-35%, maintained despite acquisition costs. Four wins in the quarter: a cross-sell into Augusta Health (Mayo Clinic network) and new logos White-Wilson, Evolve and UMass Memorial.

segments.name: Legacy TruBridge (rural/community hospitals, acute)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~$68 million for 82 days, against a ~$75 million quarterly run rate (~$300 million annualised). Pre-synergy EBITDA in line with the ~$68 million annual run-rate expectation; adjusted margin on the call was about 17.5% by an analyst's math, which management said understates the figure. About 2/3 is system of action and 1/3 system of record (~$100 million EHR).

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given. FY27: legacy IKS to keep growing above the ~12% industry growth in constant currency; TruBridge to be flat with no significant growth modelled for the year.
FY28: early signs of TruBridge system-of-action growth; management aspiration of 10-12% growth in the TruBridge system-of-action book from late FY28, with the EHR (system of record) book kept flat.

Synergies: management said nothing material realised yet, with the bulk ahead; restructuring of the financial health RCM operating model and G&A integration to play out from the second half of Q3 FY27.
Margin: management reiterated a return to early-to-mid 30s EBITDA margin by FY30 across both books; no FY28/FY29 margin guidance.

Long-term True North: INR3,000 crore (~$320 million) EBITDA target for FY30 and net leverage taken to near zero by end FY30. Net debt roughly INR5,280 crore; interest ~$10 million per quarter; loan has an 18-month principal moratorium, pricing SOFR+2.75% falling to SOFR+1.75% at 1.7x leverage.
ESOP: a grant to about 60-65 leaders of ~4% of equity, with ~80% tied to the FY30 EBITDA target; P&L impact from the second half of Q3 FY27, with disclosure on approval.
capex_capacity: TruBridge's three legacy IKS features (denial prediction and prevention, medical coding, clinical documentation/virtual care assistant) are to be integrated into the legacy COBOL-based TruBridge EHR and released to its customers by Q1 FY28.
Project Endeavor: a ground-up AI-native operating system for the rural and community market, launched in parallel, likely meaningful from FY29.
Two TruBridge customers have begun assessments to take the full IKS system-of-action platform.

System-of-intelligence build is task-specific: prior auth and denial prediction are in progress and coding knowledge graphs have been built. Management said a full ambulatory system-of-intelligence is about a one-year journey.
Technology spend at TruBridge to be re-optimised rather than cut.
demand_pricing: TruBridge engagement: 50+ customer meetings; management says EHR stickiness is higher than assumed and the patient-record base is 3.5-4x the ~5 million assumed at deal time.
Of 600+ TruBridge EHR hospitals, not more than ~200 use the financial health (RCM) offering, which management calls a large white space.

Top-10 client revenue fell from ~INR480 crore in Q1 to ~INR342 crore in Q2 because of a short-term project from a top-five client; management said this was replaced by other clients and that one-time projects across multiple clients are expected around calendar Q3-Q4 (e.g. HCC coding, retrospective chart review).
Pricing: outcome-based model; management expects incremental price compression as the model becomes more AI-led, which it says will be more than offset by productivity gains.
Competition: TruBridge clearing house (TruBridge RCM) is being offered in two or three new proposals; legacy clients under existing clearing-house contracts will not switch.

qa_highlights.question: Which cost levers will drive TruBridge margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating-cost levers from moving financial health RCM and medical coding to the global human-in-the-loop model with technology, technology spend re-optimisation, and SG&A synergies from removing public-company costs and integrating G&A (three of TruBridge's top five executives moved into the combined leadership).

qa_highlights.question: How should organic growth be modelled for legacy IKS and TruBridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy IKS to keep beating the ~12% industry growth; TruBridge flat through FY27, moderate growth from FY28, and 10-12% in its system-of-action book from late FY28 into FY29, with the system-of-record book kept flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a five-year facility with an 18-month principal moratorium, so repayments start around end of calendar 2027; interest is about $10 million per quarter, and the spread steps down from SOFR+2.75% to SOFR+1.75% at 1.7x leverage.

qa_highlights.question: When does the ESOP performance-linked charge hit P&L and what immediate synergies were realised?
qa_highlights.answer: The ESOP charge starts in the second half of Q3 FY27 once approved. Management said no material synergies were realised in the 82 days, with the bulk ahead, and the near-term triggers are RCM operating-model restructuring and G&A integration from the second half of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can IKS products be cross-sold into TruBridge's base, and vice versa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not cross-sell the TruBridge EHR into the legacy IKS physician base; instead, TruBridge's acute RCM and its Encoder coding tool are to be sold into the IKS base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the system of intelligence commercially ready?
qa_highlights.answer: It is being built by task. Coding knowledge graphs exist, and prior auth and denial prediction are in development; a complete ambulatory system of intelligence is about a one-year journey.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI productivity being passed on to clients as price compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the outcome-based model keeps most productivity gains in margin, and it expects incremental price compression as the model becomes more AI-led, which it expects to be more than offset.

risks_watch: TruBridge client churn in the financial health base, which management says is being stabilised and is flat in FY27.
Synergy delivery: whether the second-half FY27 restructuring of the RCM operating model and G&A integration deliver margin gains toward early-to-mid 30s by FY30.
Lumpiness of one-time revenue projects (calendar Q3-Q4) and the top-10 client revenue decline (INR480 crore to INR342 crore QoQ).
Execution risk: Q1 FY28 target for the three features in the legacy COBOL TruBridge EHR, and Project Endeavor timelines.
Price compression as AI automation increases, and competition for clearing-house and RCM deals.
ESOP grant (~4% of equity) dilution and its effect on adjusted EBITDA, plus leverage reduction versus the INR3,000 crore FY30 EBITDA target.
544309|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the TruBridge integration, EHR stickiness and the long-term AI strategy, but explicitly non-committal on numbers ("not giving guidance at all"). Management was evasive on the TruBridge margin split, deferring it to an offline call, and on the client-level detail behind the top-10 revenue drop.
key_quotes: I am happy to report that we are able to maintain those margins in spite of significant acquisition expenses, of which there were about nearly INR25 crores of acquisition expenses in this quarter.
I wouldn't model too much growth, at least for FY 2028 and FY 2029, in the TruBridge system of record business, because the idea is that's the platinum mine.
If I were you, I would not be modeling any significant growth in the TruBridge business this fiscal year.
The bulk of the synergies lie ahead of us. That is by design.

rows.why: Management reiterated early-to-mid 30s EBITDA margin by FY30 across both books, with synergies from RCM restructuring and G&A integration starting H2 Q3 FY27, though legacy IKS margin is ~34.5-35% and blended Q2 EBITDA is ~28% including ~INR25 crore one-time costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; the only build is software features (TruBridge EHR add-ons by Q1 FY28) and TruBridge utilisation is not quantified, so no physical capacity signal.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Legacy IKS constant-currency revenue grew a little over 13% YoY to ~$101 million and management guided to keep beating the ~12% industry growth, while TruBridge is modelled flat for FY27 at ~$75 million quarterly run rate.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and utilisation was not disclosed; the company is an asset-light services business with no utilisation metric given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance is given; TruBridge is modelled flat for FY27 and management is explicitly non-committal on numbers, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Top-10 client revenue fell from ~INR480 crore in Q1 to ~INR342 crore in Q2 (about -29% QoQ), and synergies are not yet realised, so the flat TruBridge case and margin path carry execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TruBridge EHR add-ons (denial prediction, medical coding, clinical documentation) are to be released to customers by Q1 FY28, and two TruBridge customers have started assessments for the full IKS system-of-action platform.

rows.label: Outcome-based pricing with AI-led price compression
rows.why: Management expects incremental price compression as the model becomes more AI-led, which it says will be more than offset by productivity gains, so margin benefit depends on that offset.

rows.label: One-time TruBridge projects in calendar Q3-Q4
rows.why: Management expects one-time projects across multiple clients (HCC coding, retrospective chart review) around calendar Q3-Q4, after Top-10 client revenue fell from ~INR480 crore to ~INR342 crore QoQ.

rows.label: TruBridge RCM restructuring and G&A integration synergies
rows.why: Synergies start from the second half of Q3 FY27 via moving financial health RCM and coding to a global human-in-the-loop model, with nothing material realised in the 82 days so far.

tone.note: Management was confident on TruBridge EHR stickiness, the AI strategy and legacy IKS growth above 12%, but non-committal on numbers and evasive on the TruBridge margin split and top-10 client detail; analysts pushed on margins and revenue lumpiness.

544310|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 57% to INR235.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 25.7%; order book above INR400 crore and FY27 order-booking target of INR500+ crore.
544310|2026-03.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported record FY26 revenue of INR235.1 crore (up 57%), EBITDA of INR60.4 crore (up 75%, 25.7% margin, about 260 bps higher) and PAT of INR37.4 crore (15.9% margin). H2 FY26 revenue was INR135.5 crore (up 46% YoY), with H2 EBITDA of INR37.2 crore and PAT of INR23.7 crore. Order book stood at over INR400 crore on 31 March 2026. Management said the Greenfield RIP facility is in final commissioning, with trial production by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production targeted around October 2026.

segments.name: OIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units out of about 7,200); management says OIP is in shortage and deliveries are constrained by capacity, with a brownfield expansion planned.

segments.name: RIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units); core is still imported (about 95% per the presentation), and localisation via the Greenfield facility at Jarod is targeted in H2 FY27.

segments.name: HCP / high current
segments.commentary: Balance of volumes in FY26 (combined with OIP, about 15-18% of order book per management).

segments.name: Retrofit
segments.commentary: About 6-7% of overall revenue per management; described as high-margin, with no segment EBITDA disclosed.

segments.name: Sukrut Electric (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR25-26 crore; management targets INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years (5-6x growth). No Sukrut EBITDA guidance given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 invoicing target of INR360-400 crore (management: 40-45% growth).
Order inflow target of at least INR500 crore in FY27.
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 24-25% in FY27; margin expansion expected from FY28 as import dependence falls.
Long-term growth aspiration of around 40-42% for the next four to five years.
Exports to reach at least 20% of revenue in the next two to three years.
Greenfield RIP facility: trial production by end Q2 FY27, commercial RIP core production about 3-4 months after internal trials and type tests; management targets October 2026.
Total capacity to rise to about 15,000 bushings (about INR700 crore revenue potential), with about INR100 crore for OIP and the balance for RIP.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 9,000-10,000 bushings; about 7,000+ produced in FY26 (75-80% utilisation); FY27 utilisation target 65-70%.
Greenfield facility at Jarod (about 20 km from Baroda airport): design expanded from 220 kV to 550 kV; adds about 5,000-7,000 units a year, focused on RIP/RIS.
Greenfield capex of about INR153 crore, of which about INR80 crore spent; balance expected within two to three months.
Equity raise approval up to INR150 crore; management is eyeing INR100-110 crore for capex (550 kV production, testing, brownfield) and working capital of INR28-30 crore.
Constraints in autoclave capacity; new autoclaves being invested in. Brownfield OIP expansion planned to address OIP shortage.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds global bushing supply; transformer OEMs are giving blanket orders for 24-36 months.
Prices are secured with suppliers and customers via pass-through arrangements for commodity and currency moves; management says indirect cost escalation from oil/gas is being passed on.
Management sees no direct impact from the Middle East war; no exports to or imports from affected countries.
Management says Chinese bushings have never been restricted in India, yet Indian buyers have not bought them, citing pricing, availability and service.
Competitive RIP entrants in India named as CG Power, Hitachi India and MIM (Massa Izolyator Mehru).

qa_highlights.question: Top-line growth expected over the next 2-3 years and impact of the Middle East war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 40-42% growth for the next four to five years (38-40% CAGR over the past five to six years); no direct war impact, only indirect cost escalation passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new RIP plant contribute revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end Q2 FY27; job-work assembly and testing revenue starts earlier, with indigenous RIP commercial revenue expected towards year-end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and EBITDA margins improve in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally higher H2 volumes, scale-driven negotiation, customer price recovery, supplier price negotiation and currency hedging; no single specific reason.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of margin compression if lower-kV capacity comes online across the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to hold given rising global demand, localisation of RIP cores and export pricing for RIP, and sees input-stage margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sukrut revenue potential and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukrut revenue about INR25-26 crore in FY26, targeted at INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years; management declined to give Sukrut EBITDA guidance until later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capacity after expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15,000 bushings with a revenue potential of close to INR700 crore; about INR100 crore OIP and the balance RIP.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity rather than debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is mathematically cheaper but it wants good investors on the cap table and prefers to remain debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Cyber incident impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No recovery to date; a police complaint has been filed and the expense has already been charged to the P&L.

risks_watch: Commissioning and type-test success for the Greenfield RIP core line; management says a 2-3 month delay would not affect FY27 guidance.
Input-cost and currency volatility from oil, gas, insulators and rupee depreciation; Middle East war effects over the next two to three months.
Supply-chain bottlenecks: vendor development takes about 6 months and suppliers may deprioritise the company; people attrition in a niche skill set.
Pricing and capacity risk if sub-400 kV capacity expands industry-wide, or if restrictions on Chinese bushings are eased.
Sukrut integration and profitability not yet disclosed; equity raise size (INR100-110 crore vs INR150 crore approval) still to be finalised.
Swiss technology contract for core knowledge runs to mid-2027 for supplies; the agreement itself has ended.
544310|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, growth and order visibility, but measured and somewhat hedged on timelines and specifics. Management declined to give several numbers (RIP/OIP realisations, retrofit EBITDA, Sukrut EBITDA) and kept some answers general.
key_quotes: Financial year '26 has been a landmark year in the journey of Yash Highvoltage.
So, we, we have a target to book at least INR500 plus crores order this year also.
Sukrut, we assume that in next four to five years, we should be able to cross at least INR150 to INR160 crores of revenue.
We understand that mathematically the debt is always a better route. But we also want good investors on our cap table

rows.why: Greenfield Jarod RIP facility is under construction with INR80 crore of INR153 crore spent, adding about 5,000-7,000 bushings a year against a current 9,000-10,000 capacity with 77.5% utilisation.

rows.why: FY27 invoicing target INR360-400 crore is 40-45% growth, with demand exceeding global bushing supply and transformer OEMs giving 24-36 month blanket orders.

rows.why: Utilisation at 75-80% (77.5%) with OIP in shortage and a brownfield OIP expansion (about INR100 crore) planned; equity raise up to INR150 crore approved with INR100-110 crore earmarked for capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book above INR400 crore on 31 March 2026 against FY27 invoicing target of INR360-400 crore, with inflow target of at least INR500 crore, gives visibility but management has not raised guidance.

rows.why: Greenfield commissioning and type-test slippage risk, input-cost and rupee volatility from Middle East war, and vendor development takes about 6 months; management says a 2-3 month delay would not affect FY27 guidance.

rows.why: Management targets at least 20% of revenue from exports in 2-3 years, with RIP export pricing cited as supportive, but no current export share is quantified.

rows.why: Approval for up to INR150 crore granted with INR100-110 crore for capex and INR28-30 crore for working capital; size still to be finalised and management prefers to remain debt-free.

rows.why: Order book above INR400 crore at 31 March 2026 against FY26 revenue of INR235.1 crore, with blanket orders of 24-36 months from transformer OEMs.

544310|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 95% YoY to INR194.5 crores, with EBITDA margin up to 28.1% and PAT of INR36 crores (18.6% margin).
544310|2026-09.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR194.5 crores, up 95% YoY, with volume up about 40% to roughly 4,000 bushings. Gross margin expanded to 48.3% from 42.4%, and EBITDA rose 139% to INR55 crores, lifting margin to 28.1% from 23.3%. Order book stood at INR760 crores as of 30 September 2026, against INR400 crores at the start of FY27, with execution over 15 to 18 months. Greenfield capex of INR220 crores is INR106 crores spent so far, with the balance over the next 12 months, and management reiterated the Brownfield expansion completing by Q3.

financial_highlights.change: +139% YoY vs INR23 crores; margin vs 23.3%
+157% YoY vs INR14 crores; margin vs 13.7%
vs INR400 crores at start of FY27
vs INR2.6 crores in H1 FY26

segments.name: RIP bushings
segments.commentary: Contributed 86% of H1 FY27 revenue by value, while volume split was roughly 40% higher-voltage mix driven; H1 production close to 2,200 RIP units versus about 1,500 OIP units.

segments.name: OIP and high-current bushings
segments.commentary: Contributed 14% of H1 FY27 revenue by value; export order book is about INR40-50 crores, roughly 5-7% of the order book, mainly OIP for US customers.

segments.name: Retrofit and services (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew to 8% of domestic sales from 4% a year earlier, per management.

guidance_outlook: Greenfield Jarod facility: ready up to 245 kV this year; localized 550 kV after 1 to 1.5 years. Commercial production of localized up-to-245 kV bushings expected from Q4 FY27; 420 kV and 550 kV from Q4 FY28 or mid-FY28.
Combined Unit 1 and Unit 2 invoicing potential of INR900-1,000 crores, with full utilisation expected by FY31.
Management said the existing order book should carry through 15-18 months (or 18-20 months), with new orders booked in the meantime.
Export RIP bushing orders expected from mid-next year (FY28), with the export mix changing from FY28-29.
Expects H2 revenue to be broadly balanced with H1 and says it is not targeting a sharp H2 skew; no FY27 revenue number given.
Expects PAT margin to be maintained despite depreciation of about 2.5 to 3 times last year's level, with most of the increase falling in H2.
Targets global market share of at least 5% in 4 to 5 years, from about 1-1.2% today.
capex_capacity: Greenfield capex of INR220 crores, of which INR106 crores spent until 30 September 2026; balance over next 12 months.
Brownfield expansion expected to complete by end of Q3 FY27, with capacity visible in Q4.
Halol existing unit running at about 90% capacity utilisation on three shifts; new facility using assembly and testing halls since September, with ramp-up in H2.
Localized core trial results described as very encouraging; bushings to be sent for type test in the next couple of weeks, with external lab validation pending.
Future capex expected to be funded from internal accruals; management said remaining investment is not expected to be substantial.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from India and abroad is rising, and that the market is a seller's market for the next 2 to 4 years, with bushings having reasonable entry barriers.
Some new entrants have announced bushing investments; management said it is prepared.
Bushing prices range from INR30,000-35,000 for a 72.5 kV OIP unit to INR36-44 lakh for a 420 kV unit.
Import cost, duty and freight currently about 18-20% of cost; localization expected to remove this, subject to customer pricing and competitor pricing.
US: representation agreements cover close to 27 states; agents in close to 30 countries; OIP export orders carry 6-15 month lead times.

qa_highlights.question: What drove EBITDA margin to 28% and is it sustainable into H2 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited product mix, sales and procurement improvements, factory efficiency and overhead absorption from higher volume; said the aim is to maintain or improve margins without giving a specific number.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise to 32-35% after core localization?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah declined to give a specific target, saying the company will see the impact of localized production before committing; earlier guidance was about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Order book from exports and share of export orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Export order book is about INR40-50 crores, roughly 5-7% of the INR700-odd crore book at the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: H1 production split between RIP and OIP?
qa_highlights.answer: Close to 1,500 OIP and close to 2,200 RIP bushings were produced in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential from expanded capacity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined Unit 1 and Unit 2 invoicing potential of INR900-1,000 crores, with full utilisation by 2030-31.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4,000 bushings in H1 FY27 versus 2,950 in H1 FY26, around 40% growth; no product-wise split given.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and non-current assets rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days were 47 in H1 FY27 versus 45 for full FY26; the rise in other non-current assets to INR40 crores from INR11 crores reflects advances to international core vendors to secure slots.

risks_watch: Localized core type testing and approval (plant and product approval) expected in Q3 FY27; delay would postpone localized margin benefit.
Dependence on imported cores from international vendors; advances to vendors rose to INR40 crores.
Competition from new high-voltage bushing entrants and from Chinese component players, which management says is limited historically.
H2 revenue linearity: management aims for balanced H1 and H2, but past years saw H2 outperform.
Depreciation rising to about 2.5-3x last year; PAT margin target depends on maintaining profitability.
Management did not confirm FY27 revenue guidance; analyst-cited INR450-500 crore figure not endorsed.
544310|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and execution, with clear optimism on localization and US expansion. Cautious and evasive on forward numbers: declined to give specific margin, FY27 revenue, and localized realization figures.

We have got reasonable idea, but not that much that I can make a commitment today.

544317|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR6,880 crores with record EBITDA; FY27 guidance trimmed to 20-22% growth and about 11% EBITDA margin.

Q4 FY26 was softer: revenue INR1,863 crores, EBITDA INR207 crores (11.08% margin) and PAT INR96 crores, which management attributed to project-cycle timing and supply-chain delays in February and March. Working capital days fell to 81 from 91 and net debt reduced to INR274 crores.

Order book stood at INR14,218 crore at September 30, with INR1,747 crore declared post-quarter. Management guided to 20% revenue growth for at least 3 years, annual order intake above INR10,000 crore, and a solar IPP entry via a 49% stake in a 990 MWac Maharashtra project.

rows.why: Tower capacity rising from 1,84,400 MTPA to about 2 lakh MT by end FY27 and conductor capacity from 40,800 to about 49,500 km/yr by year-end, both under construction; 400 MW solar targeted by Mar/Apr 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20% revenue growth for 3 years, backed by INR14,218 crore order book plus INR1,747 crore post-quarter, and tower and conductor capacity expansion, with capacity seen as sufficient for 20-22% growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already raised and solar IPP (INR3,900 crore project, INR500 crore equity) is approved; a further BESS or data-centre capex is possible but no firm plan was given, so a new announcement is likely rather than certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held revenue growth at 20-25% and EBITDA at 11%+ and said it will only revise guidance around March/April 2027 once solar contribution is visible, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables over 6 months rose (INR200-300 crore per questioner), PAT margin guided down to 5.5-6% vs EBITDA 11%+, and the Middle East disruption and rising competition (10-12% win ratio) are open risks, though management reports no guidance miss since listing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BESS results are hoped for by end of this year or next FY, and the BESS/data-centre team is being built, with BESS under GEC-III sized at about INR50,000 crore over 5 years; timing and order intake were not disclosed.

rows.label: Order intake of INR10,000-plus crore a year
rows.why: Management is confident of INR10,000-plus crore annual order intake against a INR30,000 crore pipeline with a INR18,000 crore bid already submitted at a 10-12% win ratio.

rows.label: Solar IPP 400 MW commissioning
rows.why: Board approved 49% of a 990 MWac Maharashtra SPV with about 400 MW targeted by Mar/Apr 2027 and full commissioning by Mar 2028, with partial revenue from FY28.

rows.label: Receivables collection improvement
rows.why: CFO said over-6-month receivables, which rose by about INR200-300 crore per the questioner, will decline in the coming quarter; NWC held at 82 days for H1.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter, 20% growth, order intake and 11%+ EBITDA margin, but cautious and evasive on unit economics, HTLS per-km cost and BESS/data-centre order intake; analysts pressed on the PAT-EBITDA gap and receivables.

544318|2026-03.headline: Mamata Machinery FY26 revenue fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 8.2%, which management attributes mainly to a 50% US decline and one-offs.
544318|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a consolidation year: revenue from operations fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore (FY25: Rs 254.6 crore) and Q4 revenue was Rs 73.9 crore versus Rs 111 crore a year earlier. The US business (including Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, hit by unresolved tariffs through Q2-Q3, then West Asia uncertainty and higher polymer prices in Q4. EBITDA fell to Rs 19.1 crore (8.2% margin) from Rs 54.6 crore (21.4%), and PAT to Rs 15.1 crore from Rs 40.8 crore. Management says the company remains debt-free with Rs 69.26 crore cash and guides FY27 revenue growth of about 15% with margin normalisation toward about 20%.

segments.name: Converting machinery
segments.commentary: US converting sales fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%). Domestic converting grew over 6% and rest-of-world converting grew 23%, but the segment moderated overall because of the US share.

segments.name: Packaging machinery
segments.commentary: Packaging revenue was flat to down about 1%, at roughly Rs 48-49 crore. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore, while domestic packaging grew about 55%.

segments.name: Co-extrusion
segments.commentary: Marginal degrowth due to lumpy order timing. Three large nine-layer orders: two executed in FY26, one (about Rs 9 crore) due in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at conservatively about 15% over FY26, with management avoiding a truncated base.
EBITDA margin expected to normalise to historical average of about 20% as the top line recovers and one-offs roll off.
US business expected to recover in FY27, with residual headwinds from West Asia affecting capex sentiment.
Domestic packaging growth targeted at 30-40% in FY27 based on the current FMCG pipeline; domestic converting targeted at double-digit growth.
RecTech recyclable film expected to take 12-18 months before meaningful traction; treated as incremental, not part of the 30-40% packaging target.
Europe: incremental revenue of US$2-3 million over the next three to five years; South-East Asia initial business target close to US$1 million.
risks_watch: US recovery depends on tariff stability and West Asia-driven customer capex sentiment; the Rs 3.5 crore Saudi shipment is stalled.
Gross margin fell 6.2 percentage points on mix, lower exports and commodity inflation; watch H1 FY27 gross margin and pass-through.
RecTech adoption timeline of 12-18 months is long and depends on early-adopter FMCG trials and certifications (Europe and US pending).
Europe ramp is slow and depends on the Carpentier GmbH partnership, which is non-exclusive for initial years.
Lumpy co-extrusion and exhibition-linked spends can swing quarterly results.
Order book conversion: Rs 80 crore due in H1 FY27 must be executed on time to support the 15% growth guidance.
544318|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term direction and the packaging pipeline, but candid that FY26 was weak. Management attributes the decline to external events (US tariffs, West Asia) and one-offs. Answers on RecTech and Europe were measured and conservative, and some figures (such as the margin split) were deferred or not quantified.
key_quotes: This was a year of consolidation for the company.
We expect profitability to normalize to historical averages of around 20% as the top line recovers and these one-off costs roll off.
It is definitely not because we are cheaper. In fact, we are the most expensive in India today.
We have zero B2C in business. Our entire business is B2B.

financial_highlights.change: about +34% vs Rs 66.64 crore in FY25

qa_highlights.question: Does the FSA exemption and three-year carry-forward mean packaging users face minimal near-term compliance pressure, making FY27-28 the inflection point?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RecTech needs first two or three early adopters after 6-9 month trials, with 12-18 months before traction. RecTech is incremental growth; the 30-40% domestic packaging target is based on the current FMCG pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there other markets to diversify into if the US stays weak? What is the Russia revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging is being taken to Africa and Europe in FY27; a Russia branch office was approved. Russia has no packaging revenue yet, only a couple of converting machines. Converting is already present in about 84 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Order book split and margin difference between exports and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book Rs 89.59 crore: 62% exports, 38% domestic. Gross margin about 60% on exports vs about 42-43% domestically. Rs 80 crore executes in H1 FY27 and Rs 9 crore in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Were any orders delayed due to West Asia, and what is the FY27 growth expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Three machines worth about Rs 3.5 crore for Saudi Arabia are ready but unshipped. Management said it will not use a truncated base and conservatively expects FY27 revenue about 15% above FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins normalise, and who bears the input cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to normalise as top line recovers and one-offs (exhibition spend, wage code) roll off; costs are semi-variable. Majority of cost increase passed on to customers project-by-project; no numeric split given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the US decline is in the US entity versus Canada and Mexico, and how were packaging and converting US figures split?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50% drop includes the US, Canada and Mexico. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore; US converting fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe market size and the Carpentier partnership's scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Addressable market about US$800 million for the product lines; target US$2-3 million incremental over 3-5 years. Partnership with Carpentier GmbH is non-exclusive for Western Europe in initial years; Eastern Europe to use additional channel partners.

capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 order flow: capex decisions by customers were put on hold in Q4 amid West Asia conflict and polymer price spike; a few US orders came in during Q4 and are expected to execute over the next two months.
Multi-machine VFFS order from a leading Indian snacks and namkeen brand: 4 machines delivered in FY26 (3 in India), orders for 18 more scheduled for delivery in H1 FY27.
First packaging machine order from South Africa, scheduled for delivery in Q2 FY27; Africa groundwork reported as 18 months old.

demand_pricing: US business (incl. Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, or about Rs 31 crore gross; US converting fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%), US packaging from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore (about -20%).
Recovery in FY26 gap of Rs 31 crore: domestic converting +Rs 3 crore (about 6%), domestic packaging +Rs 6 crore, rest-of-world converting +Rs 11.5 crore; total Rs 20.65 crore recovered.

Gross margin 54.6% vs 60.8%; management cited lower export share (exports higher margin, about 60% gross margin vs about 42-43% domestic on order book), adverse mix (lower co-extrusion), and H2 commodity inflation; 6.2 pp EBITDA margin impact.

Pricing: most of the polymer/input cost increase passed on to customers on project-by-project basis; management said it was the most expensive machine supplier in India and won on cost-to-output ratio, not price.
Competition: converting is highly fragmented (customers in about 84-86 countries per management); packaging customers are FMCG/organised-sector MNCs and marquee brands.

Europe: addressable market for product lines about US$800 million; initial target US$2-3 million incremental revenue over 3-5 years via Carpentier GmbH (non-exclusive for Western Europe in initial years).

RecTech: trials of 6-9 months with large FMCG companies; needs 2-3 early adopters; 12-18 months before traction; certifications (Indian Institute of Packaging, CPET) done, EU/US Class A testing pending.
Russia: no revenue yet; only a couple of converting machines shipped; branch office approved for CIS.

rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue about 15% above FY26's Rs 233.1 crore, backed by a Rs 89.59 crore order book (up ~34%, Rs 80 crore due in H1 FY27) and domestic packaging targeted at 30-40% growth, though US capex is on hold.

rows.why: No capacity expansion or capex plan was discussed, and customer capex decisions were put on hold in Q4 FY26 amid the West Asia conflict and polymer price spike, with the Rs 3.5 crore Saudi shipment stalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 80 crore of the Rs 89.59 crore order book must execute in H1 FY27 to support the 15% growth guide, and the US recovery depends on tariff stability and West Asia-driven capex sentiment.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RecTech recyclable film needs 2-3 early adopters after 6-9 month trials, with traction 12-18 months away and EU/US Class A testing pending; Europe incremental revenue is only US$2-3 million over 3-5 years.

rows.label: Multi-machine VFFS order for 18 more machines
rows.why: Orders for 18 more machines from a leading Indian snacks brand are scheduled for delivery in H1 FY27, after 4 machines were delivered in FY26.

rows.label: South Africa first packaging order and Europe/SE Asia entry
rows.why: First packaging machine order from South Africa is due for delivery in Q2 FY27; SE Asia initial target is close to US$1 million and Europe US$2-3 million over 3-5 years.

rows.label: US order flow recovery
rows.why: A few US orders came in during Q4 and are expected to execute over the next two months, but US revenue fell about 50% (about Rs 31 crore) in FY26 and customer capex is on hold.

tone.note: Management was confident on the packaging pipeline and the 15% FY27 guide, but candid that FY26 was weak and blamed US tariffs, West Asia and one-offs; analysts probed the margin split and RecTech/Europe timing, which management left largely unquantified.

544319|2026-03.headline: Senores FY26 consolidated revenue rose 62% to about INR664 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR122 crore; FY27 guided to 30-40% revenue growth.
544319|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 66% YoY to about INR190 crore, with EBITDA of INR62 crore (32.7% margin, up about 1,151 bps) and PAT after minority interest of about INR32 crore (up 78%). Regulated markets drove the quarter at INR118 crore (up 83%), while emerging markets grew 26% and India branded generics roughly doubled to about INR9 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and PAT growth of 50-60%, with blended EBITDA margin held at 29-31%. The Apnar Pharma acquisition (75% stake, 25% due by year-end) weighed on working capital and margin in Q4, with commercial shipments only starting in April 2026.

segments.name: Regulated markets (US and others)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR427 crore, up 75%; Q4 INR118 crore, up 83%, driven by portfolio expansion. Sourced/spot business is 10-12% of total revenue and is not expected to grow.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR145 crore, up 20%. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter with EBITDA margin of 18-19%; management expects this margin to hold, and the segment is now cash-flow positive. FY27 revenue projection is about INR180 crore.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR40 crore, roughly 5x FY25. FY26 budget is INR60-70 crore; about 120-130 MRs in field, with a long-run plateau of about 200 MRs.

segments.name: CDMO-CMO and own products
segments.commentary: Management says own products are about 50-53% and CDMO-CMO about 47-48% of revenue. Apnar facility is expected to contribute INR80-100 crore in FY27 and INR180-200 crore in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 30-40%, with PAT growth of about 50-60%; management called 30-35% the minimum achievable and will review after one or two quarters.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at 29-31% for FY27; ex-other-income, Q4 FY26 margin of 26.5% could be about 28-28.5%.
Apnar Pharma FY27 revenue budgeted at INR80-100 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue expected at INR10-20 crore; INR180-200 crore in 2-3 years.
Emerging markets FY27 revenue projected at about INR180 crore, with EBITDA margin of about 18-21%.
Amerisyn JV FY27 revenue budgeted at INR50-80 crore (management cited INR80-100 crore, then conservative INR50-70 crore), at EBITDA margin around 40%.
Capex FY27 about INR200 crore, including about INR100 crore for injectables and the balance for other plants and maintenance; management expects FCF generation in FY27.
Long-term aspiration of INR2,500-3,000 crore (up to INR4,000 crore) US revenue in 3-4 years across India and US facilities; ANDA rollout of 90-95% of the 51 approved ANDAs within 6-8 quarters.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR230 crore, including about INR65 crore for an ANDA acquisition.
FY27 capex expected at about INR200 crore, including about INR100 crore for injectables; about INR100 crore IPO proceeds earmarked for sterile manufacturing, to be started within this year.
Apnar Pharma (Baroda, USFDA-approved, also approved by UK MHRA and Health Canada): 75% acquired in Q4 FY26, remaining 25% by end of year; multiple pre-built clean rooms and expansion-ready.
Atlanta OSD facility: three lines commercialised; fourth line deferred due to Apnar acquisition; decision on fourth line or Apnar expansion expected within two quarters.
Emerging markets PIC/S approval for the facility expected around June-July 2026; more than 4,000 products under registration in emerging markets.
demand_pricing: Approved ANDAs rose from 22 (March 2025) to 51 (March 2026), covering more than 150 strengths; 20-21 launched, 30 to be launched over next few quarters; about 27 further molecules (60+ strengths) in development.
Management estimates the total accessible market for currently approved products plus pipeline at close to $1 billion.
Emerging market realisation per unit rose from about INR1.20 to about INR1.90 over 1-1.5 years (about 60-70%), with a shift to niche molecules.
Amerisyn JV (entered April 2026) targets US federal, VA and military procurement and FSS tenders; management says margins are not thin.
Management says branded generics do not need a large MR expansion to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net working capital days rise from 114 to 187, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the jump is due to Apnar being consolidated with no sales yet; excluding Apnar, the cycle is about 104 days. Apnar is expected to align with group cycle from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is other financial assets of INR172 crore (previously unbilled revenue)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is profit share on cost-plus B2B supplies, booked as income and parked as a financial asset until realised, typically 1-6 months. Balance should plateau then fall as launches mature. Not warranty or royalty.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance conservative given 60% growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited external uncertainty (shipping, US inflation) and said 30-35% is the minimum achievable; guidance to be revisited after one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging market margin improvement: forex versus operations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margin gain mainly came from product mix; forex contributed about INR3 crore of realised gains in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate jump from about 17% in FY25 to about 23.6% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to the Apnar tax provision, US tax at 20-21%, and India at 26%, and to FY25 benefit from US carry-forward losses. Long-term rate guided at about 23%.

risks_watch: Apnar revenue ramp: only about INR2.5-3 crore in the last three months; management guides INR10-20 crore in Q1 FY27 and INR80-100 crore for FY27.
Working capital and receivables: other financial assets (INR172 crore) and working capital days (187) need to normalise.
Guidance credibility: management said FY27 revenue guidance is conservative; a revision is possible after one or two quarters.
Execution on 30 pending ANDA launches over 6-8 quarters and the INR2,500-3,000 crore US target, which depends on launch timing.
Macro factors (shipping, US inflation, geopolitics) flagged by management as affecting margins.

Management was evasive on the other financial assets line, deferring the explanation to an offline session, and on the margin definition (EBITDA with or without other income).

544319|2026-06.headline: Senores Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR180 crores and EBITDA 87% to INR54 crores (~30% margin); FY27 guidance is 30-40% revenue and 50-60% PAT growth.
544319|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR180 crores, up 36% YoY, led by regulated markets (up 42%) and emerging markets (up 30%). EBITDA was INR54 crores (up 87%, margin ~30%, up 810 bps) and PAT was INR31 crores (up 56%). Sequentially, absolute EBITDA and PAT dipped versus Q4 FY26, which management attributed mainly to about INR14-15 crores of forex gains in Q4 that did not recur. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and a INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue ambition in three to four years, while the company shifted INR100 crores of IPO proceeds from sterile injectables to oral solids capacity.

segments.name: Regulated markets (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 42% YoY in Q1 FY27. ANDA portfolio rose from 30 (June 2025) to about 58 approved (June 2026), with 23 commercialised and 35 planned over the next 18-20 months.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY; EBITDA margin was about 14% (mid-teens) against about 20% in Q4 FY26. Management guides 18-20% for the full year and says the business is cash flow positive, with INR18 crores operating cash in Q1.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR8 crores in Q1 FY27. Management shifted focus to profitability, targeting INR50-60 crores for FY27 at 35-40% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Apnar facility (Baroda, USFDA approved)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 80-90% of production capacity, though much of it goes to qualification and launch batches. About six products have been commercialised from Apnar, and about 30 million units were produced in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-40% and PAT growth of about 50-60%, with similar growth expected thereafter.
Revenue ambition of INR2,500-3,000 crores in three to four years, based on the current pipeline and excluding NDA products; management said variance of 5-10% is possible in any given year.
FY27 capex of about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, with a run rate of INR60-75 crores in the following year.
Emerging market EBITDA margin target of 18-20% on a full-year basis.
Branded generics FY27 revenue target of INR50-60 crores, with 30-40% YoY growth expected.
Zoraya (US front-end) and Amerisyn (US government business) expected to become operational around September-October 2026.
Management expects a 70:30 regulated to emerging market revenue mix to hold for at least the next few years.
Chhatral facility PIC/S approval targeted around Q2-Q3 FY27, opening access to markets such as Vietnam, South Africa and Mexico.
capex_capacity: Apnar (Baroda) facility is at about 80-90% production capacity utilisation, though a large part goes to product qualification and launches. Third production line is under work and a fourth is planned.
Capex is being spent on oral solid capacity in the US and India, plus a scaled-down sterile injectable pilot plant. Shareholder approval for the object change is pending.
Sterile injectable project has about INR100 crores of IPO proceeds left, now pushed to the second half of FY27 with a pilot approach.
Of the 18 products mapped for Apnar, about six are commercialised; portfolio rationalisation between US and India sites is planned from next year.
Management said the Chhatral site in Ahmedabad is PIC/S inspected and makes oral solids, injectables and liquids.

qa_highlights.question: Why did emerging market EBITDA margin fall from about 20% in Q4 FY26 to 14% in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weaker than H2, and Q1 is still the strongest first quarter in four years. Management reiterated the full-year 18-20% margin target and cited product mix and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded generics decline 2%, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus has moved from sales to profitability after the business rose from INR8 crores to INR40 crores in FY26. It targets INR50-60 crores at 35-40% EBITDA margin for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 'other income' restated for June 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no restatement or policy change. Forex gains were moved from above the operating line into other income, so the presentation changed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sequential EBITDA and PAT decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 included about INR14-15 crores of forex gains that were nil in Q1 FY27. Excluding this, margins are in line sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO proceeds use changed from sterile injectables to oral solids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Apnar acquisition and oral solid pipeline growth needed capacity sooner, so it reallocated proceeds to oral solid lines in the US and India. A small sterile injectable pilot will follow, and shareholder approval is pending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans, and what is Apnar's utilisation and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, and the run rate is INR60-75 crores after that. Apnar utilisation is 80-90% but partly used for qualification; revenue was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 PAT growth be similar to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a FY28 number and pointed to the INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue goal in three to four years. It said the EBITDA margin of about 30% is the minimum to sustain.

Sequential decline in absolute EBITDA and PAT versus Q4 FY26 was attributed to about INR14-15 crores of forex gains in Q4 that were practically nil in Q1. Management said gross margin improved about 1% versus Q4. Other income presentation changed: forex gains moved from above the operating line into other income, with no restatement.

544319|2026-09.headline: Senores Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR192 crores and EBITDA 38% to INR58 crores (30% margin), with FY27 guidance of 30-40% revenue growth reiterated.
544319|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR192 crores (+25% YoY), the highest quarterly revenue to date, with EBITDA of INR58 crores (+38%, 30% margin, up 290 bps) and PAT of about INR36.6 crores (+22%). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR372.5 crores (+30%), EBITDA INR111 crores (+58%) and PAT INR67 crores (+31%). Management said Zoraya and Amerisyn had no revenue yet but carried setup and operating costs of about INR4 crores in Q2, and both were expected to start contributing in H2 FY27. The company reiterated FY27 guidance of 30-40% revenue growth and 50-60% PAT growth, and guided to around 25% annual growth over the next 2-3 years.

segments.name: Regulated markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 28% YoY in Q2 and 34% in H1 FY27. ANDA portfolio rose from 34 (Sep 2025) to 64 (Sep 2026), of which 23 are commercialised. Q2 saw one new ANDA approval (controlled substance) and three sANDA approvals; CDMO/CMO made up about 35% of regulated market revenue.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 21% YoY in Q2 and 25% in H1 FY27. Q2 margin dipped to about 4% on large beta-lactam orders; H1 margin about 10%. Management guides mid-to-low teens for full FY27 and says October was strong. The business is cash positive. About 558 registrations approved and about 944 filed.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Gross margin improved to more than 60% this year from 18-20% last year on similar scale, as the company shifts from volume to margin. Management expects INR50-60 crores of revenue this year at a similar gross margin.

segments.name: Apnar (US FDA-approved plant, acquired)
segments.commentary: Management said Apnar would contribute about INR100 crores or more in FY27. Q2 Apnar revenue was about INR21 crores per CFO, though an analyst cited INR31 crores; the transcript leaves this unresolved. Current revenue is mainly from five acquired ANDAs.

segments.name: Others (API, services, government incentives)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue of INR7.8 crores in Q2, mainly API with some service income and government incentives.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: revenue growth of 30-40% and PAT growth of 50-60%. Management said H1 EBITDA growth of 58% already supports this.
Management expects H2 to be heavier than H1, with H1 about 45% of full-year revenue, as in FY26. Apnar, Zoraya, Amerisyn and new launches are expected to drive H2.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 30% or higher (CFO: aiming at 30%-plus; chairman: not lower than 30%). Emerging markets margin guided at mid-to-low teens for FY27.

Apnar expected to reach full-scale operations and further expansion over the next 12-18 months. Four commercial lines targeted by March 31, 2027 (about 1.2 billion units capacity).

H1 FY27 capex about INR46 crores.
Heavy investment in AI applications and SAP HANA digitisation.
demand_pricing: Controlled substance ANDA approval in Q2 is awaiting DEA quota (45-50 days), with launch expected by end-November 2026. Management expects four to five controlled substance launches before March 2027.

Q2 saw three sANDAs commercialised covering four strengths. Two strengths were first-to-market in the US for a molecule with over $1 billion in US revenue. The other two strengths were second-to-market in niche products.
Propranolol ANDA approved in late October 2026, to be commercialised in Q3. Management expects 3-4 new ANDA approvals and 12-15 sANDA approvals in Q3 FY27.

Amerisyn expected to start business within about 10-15 days of the call. Zoraya expected within about 45 days. Management said 14 ANDAs are planned to launch under Zoraya in FY27, and more than 10 products under Amerisyn within two quarters.
Emerging-market GLP-1 products are in commercialisation in 18-20 markets (Middle East, Africa, LatAm, Far East, CIS), with a wider peptide portfolio.
Q2 emerging-market margin dip was attributed to beta-lactam orders, which carry higher prices but a competitive landscape.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no new ANDA launch in Q2, and how many ANDAs can be commercialised per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: The Q2 approval was for a controlled substance, which needs DEA quota (45-50 days) before launch. Non-ANDA-approval time lags of 3-12 months apply to acquired ANDAs. Management said 41 of 64 approved ANDAs are not yet commercialised, to be launched over six to eight quarters, and gave no quarterly figure.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Zoraya and Amerisyn costs in Q2, and can FY27 EBITDA margin stay at 28-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR4 crores of costs were incurred with no revenue, and the CFO put the floor at INR2-2.5 crores. Management said the costs would be absorbed as revenue ramps. Management said FY27 margin would be 30% or more, not 28%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Amerisyn and Zoraya JV structured, and where does inventory sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 90% of Amerisyn products are made at the company's US facility. Zoraya is similar. Both are wholly owned subsidiaries, so inventory sits on the company's books, and inventory build-up is tightly controlled.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 50-60% PAT growth guidance be achieved given higher costs from the new subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 is expected to be heavier, with Ratnatris, new launches at Aavis and Havix, and Amerisyn contributing to profit. The chairman said bottom-line growth should exceed top-line growth, and about 50% PAT growth is the internal estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the growth outlook cut to 20-25% from the earlier 30-40%, and is it caution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approved ANDA count rose from 58 to 64 and the pipeline is strong. The chairman said the company has guided about 25-30% growth to be maintained beyond FY27 and is confident of more aggressive growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did emerging market margins fall to about 4% in Q2, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip was due to large beta-lactam orders with competitive pricing. Management expects recovery to the mid-to-late teens, with full-year margin in mid-to-low teens. H1 margin was about 10%, and October was strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unbilled revenue (other financial assets) rise, and what share is over one year old?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise is from big sANDA launches billed and shipped in September, not yet sold through by distributors. Under 10%, about 8-9% of the total, is overdue for more than one year.

544320|2026-03.headline: Carraro India FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore and EBITDA margin reached 10.8%; FY27 growth guided at 4-12%, with West Asia risk flagged.

For FY26, revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore, EBITDA rose 33% to INR2,475 million, and PAT rose 48% to INR1,306 million. Management said FY27 growth could be 4-12% depending on how the West Asia situation evolves, and it declined to restate the 100bps-a-year margin improvement target. A final dividend of INR6.75 per share was recommended.

segments.commentary: Ramp-up for a major international OEM is progressing. Management targets ~INR30 million of TBH revenue by FY29, with incremental additions of ~INR10 million and ~INR18 million over the next 2-3 years.

Export mix (approx.): Europe including Turkey ~50% or less, China ~8-9%, Latin America ~10%, US ~9-10%. Management cautioned these are approximate because of contract-manufacturing invoicing.

Mix was the main reason for lower Q4 gross margin: the company prioritised dispatches to customers, with cost efficiency compromised. Commodity cost pass-through lag is ~3 months under most contracts.
Labour availability has tightened, with migrant workers having left, which has pushed up labour costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Rai said the TBH program is on track, with ~INR30 million of TBH revenue targeted by FY29. Backhoe export order book is 'good', but visibility is limited given geopolitical volatility.

qa_highlights.answer: Davide Grossi said the Q4 increase was mainly adverse product mix, not material or freight inflation. Most customer agreements pass through commodity changes over ~3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue growth stay at 8-12% and how much margin expansion is expected?

qa_highlights.question: Why not repeat the 100bps-a-year margin expansion target?

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 results, the Pune luxury position and the project pipeline, but cautious on near-term travel and gave no quantified April-May trends; analysts pressed on Maldives arrival data, diesel exposure and the FX-driven Q4 EBITDA growth.

544321|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR554 crores, but EBITDA fell about INR16 crores as Maldives diesel costs spiked; India grew 16% at INR74 crores.
544321|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR554 crores and consolidated EBITDA was INR205 crores at a 37% margin. The decline in EBITDA was attributed almost entirely to Maldives fuel and ancillary costs, which rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores as diesel prices roughly doubled from pre-war levels in April-May. India delivered 13% revenue growth and 16% EBITDA growth, with occupancy and ADR both up. Reported PAT of INR124 crores was inflated by a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal following the tax regime switch.

financial_highlights.change: YoY decline of about INR16 crores
Broadly flat; about 3% growth adjusted for one-off transaction costs
Includes INR102 crore net deferred tax liability reversal from tax regime change; tax rate cut from 34.94% to 25.17%

financial_highlights.value: INR2,095 crores (India INR1,329 crores; Maldives USD81 million / INR766 crores)

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR203 crores (+13%) and EBITDA INR74 crores (+16%); occupancy rose about 7% to 67% and ADR about 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 20%. Adjusted for a one-off electricity benefit in the prior year, EBITDA growth would be 18%.

segments.name: Maldives resorts
segments.commentary: Revenue INR218 crores (+5%) but EBITDA INR32 crores (-32%); fuel and ancillary costs rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores. Excluding the fuel spike, management says EBITDA would have grown about 10%.

segments.name: Annuity (commercial/leased assets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR128 crores (+3%) and EBITDA INR111 crores at 87% margin; committed occupancy 98%. Narmada Estates in Pune was recently added.

segments.name: Hospitality total
segments.commentary: Hospitality EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR106 crores; adjusted hospitality EBITDA growth was about 14%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove simultaneous occupancy and ADR gains in India in a seasonally soft quarter, and is there headroom in Pune?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Pune dominance (about 65% of luxury inventory), MICE, corporate demand in IT/BFSI micro markets and weddings; it expects Pune occupancy to stabilise in the high 70s and sees 200-300 luxury and upper-upscale room nights a day added from office growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where do India margins settle, and is there operating leverage beyond cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the solar capex (about INR60 crores, 3-year payback) could add roughly 4-5% to margin from Q1 next year, and that high occupancy is driving operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is Maldives demand doing in April-June, July and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: India source-market demand rose to about 9% from 6%; China and Russia grew at double-digit occupancy; July tourist arrivals were back to 2025 levels with only 27 disrupted flights versus about 170 earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Sahyadri/Kelzai acquisition be funded, and what is the threshold for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said funding will mix debt and internal accruals, with tourism incentive subsidies of 15-20% of capital expected and operations in about 2 to 2.5 years; debt to be drawn in stages as needed. The acquisition criteria answer was not captured clearly in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Maldives EBITDA decline was diesel versus operations, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline entirely to fuel: fuel bill up INR17 crores plus INR2 crores indirect, total about INR19 crores; ex-fuel Maldives EBITDA would have grown about 10%. Diesel was still about 20% below spot due to cluster procurement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Goa Hilton performance and expansion timing and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy and revenue are improving post-acquisition (104 keys), gave no unit-level numbers, and said the 50-plus key extension and refurbishment are in planning, with delivery around FY29-FY30; it expects to conservatively double EBITDA with the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sri Lanka Arugam Bay commissioning moved from FY28 to around FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Permissions are the constraint due to environmental sensitivity, about 1.5 km of shoreline and adjacency to Yala National Park; completions and formalities are near, with target around FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are July and August trends for Maldives, and what do Q3/Q4 look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify August EBITDA margin, which depends on the war; it said occupancy remains strong and bookings on the books for Q3 and Q4 look very strong.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Maldives margin to recover as diesel prices ease and solar capacity comes online; Q3 and Q4 peak seasons expected to recoup the Q1 and Q2 fuel-driven decline (about INR15 crores impact).
Fuel costs in July were already about 26% below the April-May peak, per management.

India: solar capex (about INR60 crores, Pune) targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning, expected to add 5-6% to India EBITDA (elsewhere cited as 4-5% margin increase); management expects margin uplift from Q1 next calendar year.
Maldives solar: Raaya to reach about 80% solar with battery backup by April 2027; expected savings about USD1.5 million a year (about 2.5% of Maldives EBITDA), with results from FY28.

Pipeline of over 1,700 keys across 8 upcoming hotels: AC by Marriott Whitefield (Bengaluru), Varanasi Marriott, Ritz-Carlton Reserve Arugam Bay (Sri Lanka, 73 villas), and Soho House Delhi, progressing toward completion FY28 to FY30. Arugam Bay timeline slipped to around FY30 on permissions.

Promoter ROFO pipeline of 1,114 keys (JW Marriott Navi Mumbai and 3 Moxy hotels) cited toward a 4,000-plus key ambition; Goa Hilton (104 keys) brownfield extension of 50-plus keys in planning; Sol De Goa (21 boutique keys, Nerul) and Saipem Hills land in planning, delivery around FY29-FY30.
demand_pricing: India: occupancy up about 7% to 67% with ADR up about 8%, RevPAR up about 20%; management said occupancy and rate rose together, driven by Pune, Bengaluru and Goa demand, MICE, corporate and weddings.

Annuity: revenue up 3% to INR128 crores, committed occupancy 98%.
Same-store revenue up 10% and same-store EBITDA up 15% in the quarter, per management.
risks_watch: Maldives fuel cost trajectory and the West Asia conflict: management says the Q3/Q4 recovery depends on diesel easing and the war situation, and it declined to give an August margin view.
Maldives Q3/Q4 recovery of about INR15 crores of lost EBITDA is assumed but not yet proven; monitor Maldives EBITDA margin in Q2 and Q3.
Execution risk on Sri Lanka Arugam Bay (permissions, environmental clearances, timeline slipped to around FY30) and on the 8-hotel pipeline (FY28-FY30).

Pune demand concentration: India growth rests on Pune and the 65% luxury share; monitor occupancy sustainability versus management's high-70s target.
Earnings quality: PAT of INR124 crores includes a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal; underlying PAT is much lower.
key_quotes: The pressure this quarter was on costs, not on demand.
So, if we look at the cost of Maldives EBITDA, it would have grown by 10% versus the -32% EBITDA decline in a non-peak quarter under war conditions.
We have acquired it 100% at an equity consideration of around INR281 crores and enterprise value of around INR466 crores, targeting a yield-on-cost above 12%.
So that is why I feel the pricing power in Pune will, is here to stay and strong.

544321|2026-09.headline: Ventive Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 11% to INR211 crores on 5% consolidated revenue growth to INR582 crores; reported PAT fell 47% on higher D&A.
544321|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was seasonally the softest quarter, yet operating revenue grew 13% and operating EBITDA 11%, with Maldives returning to growth after a fuel-hit Q1. Reported consolidated EBITDA fell 5% to INR242 crores because other income dropped on lower forex gains, ICD interest and export incentives. Reported PAT declined 47% year-on-year as depreciation and amortisation rose from INR79 crores to INR102 crores. Management guided to a stronger H2, citing Q3 business on books of about 67% and mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth.

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% to INR207 crores and operating EBITDA grew 8% to INR80 crores at a 39% margin. ADR rose 11% to INR12,629, occupancy up 2 points to 68%, RevPAR up 15% to INR8,606, TRevPAR up 14%. Adjusted for one-offs, India EBITDA would have grown 11% vs 5% reported.

segments.name: Maldives hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% to INR213 crores and operating EBITDA grew 25% to INR30 crores; EBITDA margin about 14% vs 15% in Q1. TRevPAR rose 20% to INR45,000 and occupancy rose 3 points to 57%. Q1 EBITDA had declined 32%.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 5% to INR131 crores and EBITDA was INR117 crores at a 90% margin. Committed occupancy was 98% across 3.4 million sq ft.

guidance_outlook: H2 seasonally strongest in both India and Maldives; management expects H2 occupancy above 70% and India ADR above INR14,500.
Q3 FY27: about 67% of forecast revenue on books; management guided to mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth with occupancy above 70%.
Maldives diesel cost drag was about INR12 crores in Q2 vs about INR20 crores in Q1; management expects EBITDA and margins to strengthen further.
AC by Marriott Whitefield (Aloft Whitefield conversion) to open in Q1 FY28 and Varanasi Marriott in Q3 FY28, adding about 360 keys; Sahyadri Hills Ritz-Carlton Reserve launch remains FY29.
Solar installation at Raaya expected in January 2027, enabling about 17 hours a day generator-free operation.
capex_capacity: Over 1,500 keys under development.
AC by Marriott Whitefield (Aloft Whitefield, shut for AC conversion) targeted for Q1 FY28; Varanasi Marriott targeted for Q3 FY28; management says timelines and budgets are on track.
Financial closure obtained on both Whitefield and Varanasi; company is using more of its cash surpluses to fund these projects.
Sahyadri Hills (India's first Ritz-Carlton Reserve, branded residences) master plan being finalised; FY29 launch timeline firm. Acquisition of Sahyadri Hills has increased leverage.
Solar programme across Raaya, Conrad and Anantara in progress as planned; Roha project acquisition finance drawn.
demand_pricing: India: growth on both rate and occupancy; MICE contributed 7% of revenue at JW Marriott Pune and Ritz-Carlton Pune; JW Marriott Pune hosted BRICS Communications Ministers Meeting with around 5,000 delegates over 11 days.

Maldives: occupancy gain of 3 points to 57% during an off-season affected by elevated airfares and lower tourist arrivals; diesel averaged about $1.1/litre in Q2, about 1.5x last year, down about 31% from the April-May peak.
Ritz-Carlton Pune launched YA:LA Mediterranean restaurant, expected to generate INR1.5-2 crores a month; Ritz-Carlton Pune received its first MICHELIN Key.

Other income fell about 50%: forex gains were INR21 crores vs INR48 crores last year; ICD interest ended after repayment; INR4 crores export incentive no longer available. No hedging strategy in place.
Aloft Whitefield and some Hilton Goa wings closed for refurbishment in the quarter, and the new wage code added employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Maldives EBITDA margin fall from Q1 (15%) to Q2 (14%) despite diesel prices falling about 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Batra said the added diesel cost was INR12 crores in Q2 vs about INR20 crores in Q1, and that Q2 EBITDA was flat YoY, typical for Maldives low season. He cited pricing actions, HVAC and desalination energy savings, and solar.

qa_highlights.question: Why did effective interest cost rise QoQ, and was expensive debt taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Paresh Bafna said acquisition finance for the Roha project and a 25 bps policy rate increase (about 8-10 bps passed through to the Ventive portfolio) raised costs. He said rates remain competitive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the colour on Q3 for India and Maldives, including MICE?
qa_highlights.answer: Batra said H1 operating revenue grew 10% and operating EBITDA 2%; for Q3, about 67% of forecast revenue is on the books, with mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth and occupancy above 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there hedging against forex-driven swings in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Bafna said there is no hedging strategy; the drop reflects lower forex gains (INR21 crores vs INR48 crores), ended ICD interest income and the absence of a INR4 crores export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Whitefield and Varanasi Marriott projects on time and budget?
qa_highlights.answer: Shoaib Shariff said timelines and budgets are on track: Aloft Whitefield (AC by Marriott) in Q1 FY28 and Varanasi in Q3 FY28, adding about 360 keys; financial closure is done and cash surpluses fund capex.

risks_watch: Maldives diesel: still about 1.5x last year's level, and the Q1 fuel shock showed sensitivity; solar roll-out (Raaya January 2027) is the mitigant.
Reported PAT down 47% on D&A rising to INR102 crores; monitor depreciation trajectory as Whitefield and Varanasi open.
Other income is volatile (forex, ICD repayment, export incentives) and unhedged; reported EBITDA diverges from operating EBITDA.
Leverage up to 1.6x net debt/EBITDA after Sahyadri Hills; interest costs rising with acquisition finance and rate changes.
Execution risk on Whitefield (Q1 FY28) and Varanasi (Q3 FY28) openings and the FY29 Sahyadri Hills launch.
544321|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Maldives recovery and H2 bookings, with a few admissions: India EBITDA growth was held back by refurbishments and the wage code, and PAT decline was framed upfront. Answers on the Maldives margin and interest cost were somewhat defensive, leaning on seasonality and 'competitive' rates.
key_quotes: Double-digit growth in the monsoon quarter in TRevPAR and RevPAR of both 18% each is something I'm really proud of.
I'll be upfront, EBITDA could have grown faster. This quarter was for investing in our product.
Revenue up, EBITDA up, cash profit up.
So this quarter was not a quarter where the market did the work for us. Our teams did.
