rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Aloft Whitefield (AC by Marriott) is shut for conversion and targeted for Q1 FY28, with Varanasi Marriott in Q3 FY28, together adding about 360 keys; financial closure is obtained and timelines are said to be on track.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India H2 occupancy guided above 70% (up from 68% in Q2) and Q3 revenue growth guided to mid-teens with about 67% of forecast revenue on books.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Over 1,500 keys are under development and cash surpluses are funding projects, but no new capex programme was announced and leverage rose to 1.6x net debt/EBITDA after Sahyadri Hills.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided mid-teens Q3 revenue and EBITDA growth with 67% of revenue on books, which is ahead of Q2's 5% reported and 13% operating revenue growth, but it is not yet a formal upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Interest costs are rising (25 bps policy hike, acquisition finance for Roha), Maldives diesel is still about 1.5x last year, and D&A rose to INR102 crores from INR79 crores, which pressures PAT even if EBITDA holds.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sahyadri Hills Ritz-Carlton Reserve launch is firm for FY29, outside the 2-4 quarter window; no other new product launches were named.

rows.label: Solar roll-out at Raaya, Conrad and Anantara
rows.why: Raaya solar installation expected January 2027 enabling about 17 hours a day generator-free operation, reducing exposure to Maldives diesel that cost about INR12 crores in Q2 and about INR20 crores in Q1.

rows.label: Leverage rising after Sahyadri Hills
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR1,859 crores with net debt/EBITDA at 1.6x vs 1.2x in Q1, and gross debt is up 11% YoY, so deleveraging is not in the outlook.

rows.label: Q3 business on books
rows.why: About 67% of forecast Q3 revenue is already on the books, supporting the guided mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Maldives recovery, H2 bookings and the Whitefield/Varanasi timelines, but was more defensive on the Maldives margin dip and rising interest costs, leaning on seasonality and 'competitive' rates; analysts probed margins, interest cost and hedging.

544322|2026-03.headline: Unimech to acquire Hobel Bellows for about INR450 crore EV, all-cash from internal funds, at roughly 7x EV/EBITDA on ~INR129 crore FY26 revenue and >50% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-03.overview: Unimech announced the acquisition of Hobel Bellows, a metallic bellows and precision assemblies maker, via a subsidiary, for about INR450 crore EV on an all-cash basis funded from internal balance sheet cash. Management said Hobel reported about INR129 crore revenue for FY26 with EBITDA margin above 50%, and projected 15-17% growth over 3-4 years on existing customers without new-customer wins. Management said the core business saw demand recovery and better Q4 FY26 momentum, and that the FTWZ facility awaits only customs clearance, expected by end-May 2026. Q&A centred on customer concentration (two OEM groups ~93% of revenue), valuation rationale, NPCIL and AS9100 certification timelines, and capacity utilisation of 50-60%.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - metallic bellows
segments.commentary: Over 75% of Hobel revenue per management; bellows range 2 to 16 inches, 500 g to 330 kg, for engines of 900 to 9,000 BHP. About 70% of products are single-source.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - exhaust manifolds and structural components
segments.commentary: Remainder of revenue (under 25%) per management; margins said to be similar to bellows.

segments.name: Unimech core business
segments.commentary: Management said demand is normalising after a muted prior year, with improved momentum in Q4 FY26 and a healthy order book; no quantified figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management guides 15-17% growth over the next 3-4 years for Hobel, described as conservative and excluding new customers.
Synergies expected mainly on revenue (cross-selling, nuclear, marine/naval, aerospace), not cost; cost optimisation described as limited.
No new borrowings planned; no major capex expected near term beyond maintenance, with capex deferred until utilisation reaches 80-90%.
FTWZ facility: all approvals received, only customs clearance pending, expected by end-May 2026; delayed versus earlier timelines.
NPCIL qualification expected in about one year; AS9100 certification needed before aerospace work, timing not specified.
Payback on the acquisition estimated at 8-10 years (initial calculation).
capex_capacity: Hobel operates from a 200,000 sq ft facility plus 20,000 sq ft warehouse in Visakhapatnam SEZ; current utilisation 50-60%.
Management targets 85-90% utilisation before deploying new capex; automation and robotics expected to lift effective capacity.
Unimech had planned about INR100 crore capex for metal forming, tube bending and sheet metal; acquisition used instead.
Recent machinery additions include FANUC welding robots, seam welders, automated underwater leak test machine and 3D printer; some yet to be commissioned.
Management said no additional capex needed for AS9100 certification.
demand_pricing: Management cites a global metallic bellows addressable market of about $2.6 billion growing ~6% annually.
Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of Hobel revenue; end uses include power generation, locomotive engines, automotive and industrial systems; exports ~90%.
Cummins QSK95 gensets are an end use; Hobel's wallet share with Cummins described as small.
Margins attributed to high entry barriers, long qualification cycles, proprietary drawings and pricing power rather than cost; previous competitors were European and American.
Management says it will not sacrifice margins for growth, including avoiding automotive volume segments.
Aerospace and semiconductor customers have shown initial interest in tube bending and metal forming capabilities; no quantified pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the seller exiting at ~7x EV/EBITDA when peers trade at 25-30x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the promoter had no succession plan (daughters settled abroad) and had crossed retirement age, so wanted an exit to a suitable buyer.

qa_highlights.question: What is client concentration and working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of revenue across 10-12 geographies; about INR60 crore working capital retained and monthly cash generation said to be sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CCD a dilution risk and what are its terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCD is an internal instrument between holding and subsidiary, with no near-term intent to convert and negligible interest; the transaction is all cash apart from a 10% holdback for one year.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be amortisation or goodwill?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no amortisation because the investment is in a subsidiary; fixed assets are small and the deal is capability-led and asset-light.

qa_highlights.question: Can Hobel supply NPCIL reactor-island components such as expansion joints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hobel is not NPCIL certified; qualification is needed, taking about a year, and tubular assemblies are the target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between bellows and manifolds, and by industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Bellows over 75%, with manifolds and other structural components the rest; industry-level split not available and to be taken offline.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: two OEM groups ~93% of revenue, with a single-source product base.
Execution risk on FTWZ customs clearance (expected end-May 2026) after prior delays.
Aerospace and nuclear expansion depends on AS9100 and NPCIL qualification, with timelines of roughly one year or more.
Growth guidance (15-17%) is below the analyst view of 10% standalone CAGR being conservative and Cummins-linked demand; watch actual growth.
Retention of senior and technical staff at Hobel, with compensation benchmarking and ESOPs planned over the medium term.
Integration of metal forming and tube bending operations, which stay at the Hobel facility.
544322|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the strategic and margin story, but guarded on growth and certification timelines. Management was non-committal on aggressive growth targets, NPCIL, and the CCD, and deferred several detailed questions (installed capacity, industry split) offline.
key_quotes: This debt-free business acquisition is margin accretive with strong annual cash generation, enhancing the overall quality of Unimech's earnings profile.
So instead of taking, you know, 18 to 24 months to build this organically, we now get immediate access to those opportunities.

The intent for the first 12 months or the short term I should say will always be a slow moving, but eventually when the synergies are going to catch up, so over a medium term you will see the growth coming up.
So it's basically exhaust systems, fuel lines in a high temperature are some of the applications in the aerospace.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Hobel guided 15-17% growth over 3-4 years (midpoint 16%) on existing customers, backed by an INR65 crore+ six-month order book and 50-60% utilisation with headroom.

rows.why: Utilisation at 50-60% is well below the 80-90% trigger management set, the INR100 crore metal-forming capex was replaced by the acquisition, and management said only maintenance capex is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Core Unimech momentum improved in Q4 FY26 on a healthy order book and Hobel has an INR65 crore+ six-month order book, but the core improvement was not quantified.

544322|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 71% YoY to about INR108 crore, with Hobel Bellows consolidated for two months and a 36.5% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR108 crore, up 71% YoY and 32% QoQ, with Hobel Bellows contributing about INR22 crore over two months. PAT was about INR28 crore (24% margin), up 46% YoY, though other income of INR7 crore (vs INR15 crore in Q4 FY26) flatters the quarter less than in the prior quarter. Management guided Q2 to be stronger, with three months of Hobel and a heavier precision component (PCA) contribution in H2. Confirmed order book stood at about INR280 crore including Hobel, slightly lower QoQ, which management attributed to customer pull-ins; the company also signed a USD7.5 million five-year supply agreement with FACC Austria.

segments.name: Aero tooling
segments.commentary: Contributed approx. 76% of Q1 revenue; management said demand visibility is constructive for next quarter and is dominated by aero engine tooling. Tooling orders are largely PO-to-PO.

segments.name: Precision component and assembly (PCA)
segments.commentary: Covers nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace and Hobel Bellows, making up the remaining 24% of revenue. Management expects a much heavier PCA-led contribution in H2 FY27; about 80% of qualified PCA parts are moving into serial production.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of Q1 revenue (about INR22 crore for two months). Management guides 15-20% growth for this business; AS9100 certification for Vizag facility targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Cumulative nuclear order wins of approx. INR87 crore, with about 50% of the existing order book to execute in FY27, mainly in H2.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be stronger, with higher revenue and robust EBITDA margins, supported by three months of Hobel consolidation.
Blended gross margin of 65% seen as sustainable for FY27.
Consolidated EBITDA margin of about 34-35% expected for FY27, versus a long-run 30-32%+ range.
Other income expected to be roughly half of Q1 level in Q2 onwards.
Working capital days expected to rise gradually to 160+ days by end of FY27.
Gross block by end-FY27 expected to be about double the current level, mainly due to Saudi JV capex.
ROCE of about 15-16% expected to hold for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation; asset turns of about 2.5x over 2-3 years.
Two new customers (locomotive and power generation) expected to be onboarded by end FY27, subject to qualification.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing facilities at approx. 58% utilisation; about 10% of available capacity committed to new product introduction and qualification programs.
Capacity expansion being advanced earlier than originally planned to serve qualification programs converting into serial production; no significant core business capex was planned for FY27 earlier.
Saudi JV (Dheya/Kanoo venture) capex to proceed as scheduled; approx. USD10 million infusion into the JV expected in August 2026.
Board approved a QIP enabling resolution of up to INR750 crore; management said this is not an immediate fundraise.
Dheya Engineering seeking about USD10 million via equity and debt; Unimech intends to participate, with possible modest dilution.
demand_pricing: FACC Austria long-term supply agreement: initial value USD7.5 million over five years, with scope for expansion; marks entry into recurring aerospace component supply.
Discussions with one leading engine Tier-1 at an advanced stage; qualification and commercial talks ongoing with several airframe and engine Tier-1s.

Confirmed order book about INR280 crore including Hobel as of 30 June 2026; tooling backlog mostly consumed within the quarter, precision parts over about six months, nuclear INR87 crore split across H2 FY27 and FY28.
165 FAIs completed in the quarter; six new prospective customers engaged.
Four new nuclear reactors in the pipeline; management eyeing these opportunities.
Tariff risk: free trade warehousing zone is fully operational; management says it is watchful, with new European and Saudi exposure as hedges.

approx. half of Q4 FY26 (about INR15 crore)
broadly in line with FY26 run rate

qa_highlights.question: Order execution timeline, current order pipeline and nuclear order book outlook (INR87 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR280 crore order book is confirmed POs only, excluding FACC forecasts. Tooling backlog mostly gets consumed within the quarter, precision parts over about six months, and nuclear INR87 crore runs into H2 FY27 with some portion in FY28. New nuclear bits are in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue growth and gross/EBITDA margin range for FY27, and capex needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides one quarter at a time: Q2 to be stronger with three months of Hobel, and H2 to see a much heavier PCA-led contribution. Blended gross margin of 65% is seen as sustainable for FY27. The company is open to further investment and will plan capacity early.

qa_highlights.question: Tooling mix between engine and airframe, and growth from SKU expansion versus existing programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise mix but said it is dominated by aero engine components, with airframe tooling an opportunity being explored. Growth will come from both SKU expansion and underlying end-consumer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Where Unimech sits in the value chain across precision components and aerospace?
qa_highlights.answer: In semiconductors and PCA it is already Tier-1 and deals directly with OEMs. In aerospace it is largely Tier-2, with some direct OEM work. In nuclear it is mostly Tier-2 where EPC contractors are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear margins and the nuclear mix two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose segment margins. Consolidated EBITDA margin is guided at 30-32%+ long run and about 34-35% for FY27. Four new nuclear reactors are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Hobel Bellows revenue and margin, and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Hobel contributed about INR22 crore over two months. Segment margin is not disclosed; consolidated EBITDA was 36.5%. Growth is guided at 15-20%, though management called it premature to treat as a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income normalise, and what is the FY27 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 other income fell to INR7 crore because investable funds were deployed into the Hobel acquisition. Q2 onwards other income should be about half the Q1 level. FY26 other income was about INR46 crore.

qa_highlights.question: FACC agreement scope over two to three years, and ROCE and asset turn outlook as utilisation rises?
qa_highlights.answer: The FACC deal is a wave-specific agreement, and scope grows as new RFQs arrive. Asset turns are about 2x currently, expected at 2.5x over two to three years. ROCE of 15-16% holds for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of potential US tariffs and the QIP plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to quantify. Mitigants include the free trade warehousing zone, European customers and the Saudi JV. The INR750 crore QIP is an enabling resolution to meet the minimum public shareholding requirement within 18 months, not an immediate raise. M&A is open for both organic and inorganic growth.

risks_watch: Order book slipped marginally QoQ to about INR280 crore; management attributes this to customer pull-ins, so Q2 order inflow and book replenishment need tracking.
Working capital days guided up from about 130 to 160+ by end FY27 as long-cycle aerospace and nuclear programmes build inventory, which pressures ROCE and cash flow.

Gross block to roughly double by end FY27 mainly on Saudi JV capex, with about USD10 million infusion into the JV in August 2026 and an earlier-than-planned capacity expansion; watch return on this capital.
Other income falling to about half of Q1 INR7 crore from Q2 means earnings depend more on operations; the 36.5% Q1 EBITDA margin needs to hold against the 34-35% FY27 guide.

Nuclear INR87 crore order book is mostly H2 FY27 and the rest FY28; the Hobel AS9100 certification by Q4 FY27 is needed for aerospace entry; the Dheya USD10 million fundraise may cause modest dilution.

Potential US tariffs (100% on India was raised by an investor) remain unquantified by management; the QIP of up to INR750 crore is an enabling resolution, so the timing of any raise is an open question.

Our consolidated order book, including Hobel Bellows, stood at approximately INR280 crores as of 30th June, marginally lower than the level indicated with the previously consolidated order book, including Hobel.
So, close to around 34%-35% of margins is what we will be able to deliver for this financial year.
So, this INR280 crores is the confirmed order book.

544322|2026-09.headline: Unimech H1 FY27 revenue rose 85% YoY to INR231 crore at 38% EBITDA margin; order book INR855 crore, up over 700% YoY.
544322|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was about INR123 crore, up 98% YoY and 14% QoQ, with Q2 PAT of about INR32 crore (24% margin). H1 PAT reached INR60 crore, up 71% YoY, and management said H1 already equals about 96% of FY26 revenue and about 94% of FY26 PAT. Management guided H2 revenue above H1 at similar margins, driven by semiconductor, nuclear and Hobel. The company said the consolidated order book is INR855 crore, of which about INR589 crore is tied to LTAs and award letters, and it flagged working capital rising toward 150-160 days by end-FY27 and a possible equity raise in early CY27.

segments.name: Aero tooling
segments.commentary: Contributed about 67% of H1 FY27 revenue; anchor business on short-cycle PO-to-PO orders, with long-term supply agreements being negotiated for high-demand tools such as engine stands.

segments.name: Precision components and assemblies (PCA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 33% of H1 revenue, of which Hobel accounted for 30% of total H1 consolidated revenue. Management said semiconductor was still small in H1 with a step-up expected in H2.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Acquired entity; integration complete, with demand from key customers strong and additional capacity requested. AS9100 certification for the Vizag facility targeted by Feb 2027.

segments.name: Dheya Engineering (associate)
segments.commentary: Unimech holds about 27% equity and exclusive manufacturing rights for micro gas turbines; Avaana Capital invested at about INR200 crore valuation on 26 Sep 2026. 40 kg thrust engine in serial production initiation.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to exceed H1 at similar margins, driven by semiconductor capital goods OEM deliveries, nuclear orders and steady run-rate in other businesses.
H1 EBITDA margin (~38%) considered sustainable for FY27; H2 margins expected to be maintained.
Aspiration of INR1,000 crore revenue, a broad indication rather than formal guidance; about 20% of that vision expected from Hobel; internal accruals sufficient for it.
Gross block expected to reach roughly INR500 crore by end FY27 including JV; asset turns of 2-2.5x cited.
Working capital days expected to move to 150-160 days by end FY27.
Over 590 qualified parts targeted by end FY27 (250+ qualified plus 340+ in throughput); 320+ parts targeted for qualification in FY27.
Saudi JV commercial manufacturing readiness targeted March or April 2027; Dheya's 20/40/50/100 kg engine variants targeted by March 2027.
Equity fundraise considered in early calendar 2027, also to help meet minimum public shareholding; needed for larger expansion, not for the INR1,000 crore vision.
capex_capacity: Facilities at about 65% utilisation, including 15-20% of capacity reserved for new production introduction, prove-outs and qualification.

Automated special process cells (anodizing, electroless nickel, passivation, zinc/cadmium plating, heat treatment, NDT) at existing facility: trials in Oct-Nov 2026, commissioning by 26 Dec 2026, Nadcap targeted 27 Mar 2027.
Saudi JV capex roughly INR200-250 crore; construction on schedule with Kanoo Group. Initial equity of about USD4 million (call transcript states USD4 billion and USD4 million in different places).
Management believes existing capacity suffices for about the next 2 years, but expansion decisions for the 3-5 year opportunity are under internal assessment; capacity build takes 18-24 months.
demand_pricing: Semiconductor: one established customer and two in pipeline; 60 FAIs qualified; another 20 parts/assemblies targeted by end of calendar 2026; discussions with a Dutch semiconductor OEM for tooling.

Aerospace: three established customers and several in pipeline. Contracts include FACC (USD7.5 million, five-year aerostructure LTA, may double), a French Tier 1 door-components programme (about USD43 million over 10 years), and Honeywell (10-year LTA for engine and control-system components, extendable).
Nuclear: four new reactors in bidding stage through Tier 1 bidders, with opportunity possibly before calendar year-end; about 13-15 sub-assemblies qualified.
Management declined to disclose margins by vertical or customer, citing internal policy; directionally said to look at the overall picture rather than product-level margins.
Management said competition is not the main concern in semiconductors; scale is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of H1 revenue came from semiconductor, and what is expected in H2? Status of the semiconductor LTA?
qa_highlights.answer: Semiconductor is small in H1, within a PCA contribution of about 33% of revenue. Management expects a step-up in H2 and further qualifications leading to an LTA; it did not quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What do the INR589 crore of LTA and award letters within the order book comprise, and when does execution start?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR589 crore is linked to FACC, Honeywell and a French Tier 1, with visibility spanning 5-10 years. Execution depends on continued qualification, supported by firm POs and exhibit forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: What peak revenue can existing infrastructure support without new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no forward guidance on this. It cited a INR1,000 crore revenue aspiration, sufficient capacity for about 2 years, and asset turns of about 2-2.5x on gross block.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 and FY29 margins be based on the H1 level?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said it is too early to set FY28-29 margins and it will guide one year at a time. H2 FY27 margins are expected to match H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dheya UAV engine revenue timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are testing the engine on their platforms, and revenue would follow that testing. Management implied FY28 or FY29 at the earliest, with serial production in 2027-28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the proposed fundraise is for the INR1,000 crore vision versus new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals are enough for the INR1,000 crore vision. The raise is for larger expansion and possibly inorganic growth, because RFQs need visible capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How do margins change as the mix shifts toward precision components?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is expected to move toward roughly 50:50 tooling and PCA at the INR1,000 crore scale. PCA carries slightly lower margins, so compression is expected, with R&D adding 1-2% margin pressure, but management does not expect a large decline.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility depends on converting qualification and first-article-inspection pipelines (250+ qualified, 340+ in throughput) into serial production; management said harvesting is mainly a FY28 event.
Working capital is set to rise from about 110 days to 150-160 days, which could pressure cash flow.
Capacity constraint risk: utilisation is about 65%, and new capex timing is still under review, with a possible equity raise in early CY27.
Dheya engine certification milestones (CDR before Dec 2026, final certification by Feb 2027) and Saudi JV commercial readiness (Mar/Apr 2027) are dated items to track.

rows.label: Semiconductor step-up and nuclear orders
rows.why: Semiconductor is small in H1 with a step-up expected in H2 (60 FAIs qualified, 20 more targeted by end CY26), and four new nuclear reactors are in bidding with an opportunity possibly before calendar year-end.

rows.why: Management is considering an equity fundraise in early calendar 2027 to meet minimum public shareholding and fund larger expansion, not the INR1,000 crore vision that internal accruals cover.

544328|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.73% YoY to ₹128.58 crore while FY27 guidance calls for 20–25% revenue growth and ~12.5% operating EBITDA margin.
544328|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was ₹128.58 crore (up 2.73% YoY, up 27.77% QoQ) and EBITDA was ₹17.47 crore (up 0.57% YoY). FY26 turnover grew 14.39% to ₹419.54 crore, with tractors up 42.85% to ₹201.45 crore and cranes down about 3% to ₹218.09 crore. Management attributed the crane weakness to the Term III to Term V emission norm shift and steel cost spikes, and said pass-through is now complete. The new Bhud (Himachal Pradesh) pick-and-carry crane plant and a tower crane line are guided to start commercial production in Q2 FY27, after repeated delays. Several answers on order book, cash flow and the NBFC provisioning were vague or deferred to email.

financial_highlights.change: down from prior periods per analyst

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹201.45 crore (+42.85%) on 3,006 units; FY27 guided to grow 25–30%. Steady-state EBIT margin guided at about 10%. Consolidated tractor profit fell to ₹410 lakh vs ₹631 lakh standalone, attributed to NBFC NPA-norm provisioning.

segments.name: Cranes (pick-and-carry, existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹218.09 crore (about -3%) on 1,003 units; existing plant utilisation about 80%+ in FY26 vs 90%+ in FY25. FY27 guided to grow 15–20%. Q4 margin fell to about 10.4%, attributed to emission-norm cost pass-through and steel inflation.

segments.name: Tower cranes (new)
segments.commentary: Trials complete; commercial production targeted Q2 FY27. Small order book in single digits, all from north India, with ASP guided at ₹60–70 lakh (range ₹40 lakh to ₹75–80 lakh). Management guided 60–80 machines over the next six months, with 50–60% utilisation in year one.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth of about 20–25%; tractors 25–30%; existing crane plant 15–20%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at about 12.5% vs about 13% in FY26, with pressure from new products and markets.
New Bhud pick-and-carry plant to start commercial production in Q2 FY27; about 30–35% utilisation in first six months, 500–600 units minimum from that point.
Full utilisation of new pick-and-carry and tower crane capacity expected by FY28–29; 70–80% crane plant utilisation by FY29–30.
Other costs expected to settle at about 11–12% of revenue; working capital days to come under 200 by FY28–29 from about 307 days.
Internal plan of about 25% average annual growth until existing capacity is fully used.
capex_capacity: Total capex for new crane project about ₹70-plus crore, of which about ₹25 crore spent to date; balance to be spent in FY27.
Tower crane capacity of 240–250 machines per year initially, expandable without more capex (only welding machines to add).
Combined crane capacity after new plant cited as about 5,000 units (existing about 1,200 plus about 3,600 additional).
Existing tractor plant utilisation about 35% on reported volumes; management suggested 40–45% when including transmission supplied to cranes.
Bhud site: main shed steel nearly complete, pre-engineered building expected by July 2026; machine orders placed.
demand_pricing: Crane market size estimated at about 12,000–14,000 pick-and-carry units last year (management estimate, no public association data).
Company currently operates in less than half of India for cranes; crane dealer network 25+ and tractor dealer network 225+ after adding 23 in Q4.
Tractor FY26 growth was helped by a one-time custom hiring order from a southern state; export business in Nepal and Myanmar has weakened.
Export: a trial order of about 48 tractors from a German company worth about ₹6 crore; FY26 export about ₹21 crore.
About 20%+ of tractor sales financed through captive NBFC Barota; retail financing availability cited as a past constraint.
Tower crane competition is a two-player market (one foreign at 25–30% higher pricing, one Indian).

qa_highlights.question: Why did tractor volumes stay around 3,000 vs 4,500 in FY22, and why did margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY22 included a one-time southern custom hiring order and Nepal/Myanmar exports that have since weakened; retail financing constraints also held back volumes. Captive NBFC investment and financier support are expected to drive growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane margin down in Q4 and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to the emission-norm upgrade cost, only partly passed on earlier, plus a sharp steel price rise in Q4. Management says full pass-through is now done and the market will accept it from the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the crane capacity commissioning delayed and why are dealers flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Himachal monsoon delays, sand mining permission hurdles, and gas/commodity supply problems after the Middle East situation. It said the delay is not deliberate and it is confident of the planned numbers once the market is opened.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for other costs and the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Other costs rose from ₹56 crore to ₹64 crore on freight, discounts and promotions and are guided to 11–12% of revenue. Working capital days, now about 307, are expected to fall below 200 by FY28–29 as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tower crane order book and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a small order book in single digits, all from north India, with deliveries starting Q2. Margins are expected to be similar to pick-and-carry cranes, and initial margins will be low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no long-term order book; dealers replenish stock monthly, with some corporate and government orders (such as one from NTPC) on 60–90 day terms. Export was about ₹21 crore last year and a German trial order of about ₹6 crore has been received.

risks_watch: Crane plant commissioning has slipped repeatedly (October, then March, then Q2 FY27); fund utilisation about 73% as of March, with funds parked in FDRs.

544333|2026-03.headline: Standard Engineering Technology posted FY26 total income of INR793 crores (+26.7% YoY) and PAT of INR83 crores (+21%), but Q4 gross margin fell to ~32% from ~39% in Q3.
544333|2026-03.overview: Management called FY26 the best year in company history, with revenue, profitability, operating cash flow and working capital all improving together. Q4 total income was INR231 crores (+35% YoY), with EBITDA of INR36 crores (15.5% margin) and PAT of INR21 crores (9.1% margin). Q4 EBITDA was pressured by higher metal input prices and deliberate manpower additions ahead of expected FY27 growth. Management guided FY27 growth and margin improvement qualitatively, with no numeric guidance, and disclosed a new INR130 crore greenfield facility on a 36-acre campus, due in two phases in April 2027 and April 2028.

segments.name: Glass-lined equipment
segments.commentary: Management says glass lining is still about 30% of the business and remains one of the most profitable verticals, though its share is shrinking as other lines grow. Shell and tube glass-lined heat exchangers (with GL HAKKO, Japan) have over 200 units in order book, with 100 delivered.

segments.name: C2C Engineering (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was INR24 crores, with order book of about INR46-47 crores. FY27 target is INR60 crores, and margins are said to be similar to the group average.

segments.name: Scigenics (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR20 crores in FY26 (consolidated for only part of the year). Management targets about INR60 crores in FY27, with margins similar to the group.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue roughly doubled in FY26 versus FY25 per management, but the Q4 export share was 5.3% against guidance of 12-13%. Export order book is only about INR30 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow faster than FY26's 25% rate, per management; no numeric target given.
EBITDA margin in FY27 to improve over FY26 (17.4%); management declined to give a number, and said 'figure I can't confirm' on a 16-17% margin.
Working capital days targeted around 170 in FY27 (vs 150 in FY26), with cash conversion expected to improve versus FY26.
Management expects a INR250-300 crore quarterly revenue run rate from FY27 onwards; said 'possible and definitely we are going to do'.
Capex of INR130 crores over two years for the greenfield facility (INR65 crores in FY27 and INR65 crores in FY28), plus INR35-40 crores for modernisation of existing plants.
Heat exchanger full-fledged Indian manufacturing to start July 1, 2026, with capacity of 200 units per month.
Nuclear and oil and gas entry targeted around FY28.
Pre-cast building subsidiary is being set up to serve pharma and chemical clients only.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR40 crores; modernisation of existing plants with robotic and automatic welding and polishing machines continues with another INR35-40 crores planned.
Existing plants run at 70-80% utilisation; management says they can handle 60-70% more revenue after modernisation, taking existing capacity to about INR2,000 crores.
Greenfield 36-acre campus: INR130 crores capex, two phases. Phase 1 (50%) due April 1, 2027; phase 2 due April 1, 2028. Adds about INR2,000 crores capacity, for a total of about INR4,000 crores.

Heat exchanger unit: 80% of equipment is built in Japan and 20% in India. About 50 units were made and sold in India in FY26 (per management), with another 50 in order book. Full-scale Indian manufacturing starts July 1, 2026, at 200 units per month capacity.
Pre-cast building capability for production blocks, targeted to finish in about six months; greenfield projects to complete in 12-14 months.
demand_pricing: Order book is about INR1,000 crores, with about INR30 crores from exports and the balance domestic. Execution is expected in about 8-10 months. Management declined to split the order book by segment.
Advances of 10-30% are taken from customers, typically 20-30%.
Management says it is booking raw materials once orders are received because metal prices are volatile. Freight on exports is passed to customers.

Management claimed a global TAM of USD10 billion for one German competitor's product, with USD5 billion revenue, and a heat exchanger TAM of INR2,000 crores in India (USD2 billion globally). Management says it is the only Indian manufacturer of this product.
Export focus is Europe, US and Middle East; some export discussions were delayed by the war. Management said inventory is mainly raw material and WIP for export and project orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from about 39% in Q3 to 32% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher metal prices and manpower hiring ahead of expected FY27 growth. It said FY27 margins would improve, without a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q4 export share (5.3%) miss the 12-13% guidance given on the Q3 call?
qa_highlights.answer: A client asked to defer some equipment that was nearly ready. Management said the pending orders would be cleared in Q1 FY27, and export revenue had doubled in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR250-300 crore quarterly revenue run rate achievable from FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, 'possible and definitely we are going to do'.

qa_highlights.question: What are C2C and Scigenics targeting for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: C2C FY26 revenue was INR24 crores, with a target of INR60 crores. Scigenics was about INR20 crores in FY26 and is also targeted at about INR60 crores. Margins are similar to the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter pre-cast buildings, and does this raise margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clients insist on civil work, and pre-cast buildings cut build time to 12-14 months. It will serve only pharma and chemical clients and says it is not an EPC business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory of INR438 crores and its ageing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all inventory is under 180 days old, with no dead stock, and it expects to clear it over about 10 months. Inventory is high because of expected FY27 growth. The CFO said inventory days fell after netting customer advances.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from metal prices and manpower costs; Q4 gross margin was about 32%, against about 39% in Q3.
Export execution: Q4 export share of 5.3% missed 12-13% guidance, and USD3.5 million of deferred export equipment is now due in Q1 FY27.
Working capital intensity: management targets about 170 days in FY27, with inventory of about INR438 crores and rising receivables.
Greenfield execution timelines (April 2027 and April 2028) and heat exchanger full-scale start on July 1, 2026.
Management said the war is causing delays in some export discussions, and volatile metal costs are affecting the whole industry.
Governance: Ikeda's re-designation to Executive Director and a new Independent Director are subject to AGM approval. Management also said further acquisitions are planned, with no details.
544333|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth, with the company describing itself as a unique one-stop solution provider. The tone turns evasive and vague on quantified questions: FY27 margin, order book split, export numbers and the heat exchanger revenue potential. Management also repeated its answers on the pre-cast business and the margin question.

We are selling solutions; we are not independent equipment sellers.
We are going to complete within 2 years. First phase we are going to complete '27 April 1st, so it will 50% will going to coming into operations.

544333|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR250 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA INR44 crore (+27%), margin 17.5%; company entering AI data-centre business via GScale (up to 51%).
544333|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR250 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR44 crore (+27%), PBT of INR36 crore (+26%) and PAT of INR26 crore (+26%), with EBITDA margin at 17.5%. Two strategic moves were announced: acquisition of up to 51% in GScale Energy (AI data-centre power, cooling and skid products) and a ~19% stake in GL Hakko Japan for ~INR71 crore, with a right to rise to 51%. Management guided core business revenue to ~INR1,200 crore (+40-50%) and GScale to ~INR250 crore in FY27. Many forward figures (GScale revenue, margins, FY28) were left unquantified and deferred to future guidance.

financial_highlights.change: post Q1 billing, before some Q2 billing
management targets below 200 days in FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Export share of revenue in Q1

segments.name: Core engineering (pharma, chemical, CDMO glass-lining)
segments.commentary: Guided to grow 40-50% in FY27 to ~INR1,200 crore; CDMO is ~50% of the unexecuted order book, balance pharma and chemicals. Management says it is moving to solutions sales, with no product-vs-turnkey split disclosed.

segments.name: GScale Energy (AI data-centre products and turnkey)
segments.commentary: Targeting ~INR250 crore revenue (management clarified revenue, not bookings) by end-FY27; five customers in advanced discussions (three global MNCs, two Indian). Expects 23-25% EBITDA margin and ~20% ROCE on ~INR500 crore investment; plant ~4 lakh sq ft, first phase operational by November.

segments.name: GL Hakko (Japan glass-lining technology partner)
segments.commentary: GL Hakko revenue ~INR200 crore; target INR400 crore in 2-3 years. Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchangers already being made in India (80% built in Japan, 20% finished locally); exports planned from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance ~INR1,450 crore (core ~INR1,200 crore plus GScale ~INR250 crore).
Core business growth guided at 40-50% for FY27, up from earlier 25-30% minimum; management excluded current order book from the change.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 17-18% going forward; GScale margin expected 23-25%.
Working capital days to fall below 200 in FY27 (September-half expected), and GScale targeted at 100-150 days.
GScale data-centre projects targeted at 18-20 months versus 24-36 months industry typical; ROCE expected ~20%.
FY28 GScale and consolidated revenue guidance deferred ('we will guide soon'); no quantified margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining yet.
capex_capacity: GScale has acquired ~4 lakh sq ft factory space; ~2 lakh sq ft in full execution with robotic equipment ordered from multiple countries, arriving by mid-September.
GScale operations targeted to start by November 2026; further 2 lakh sq ft (factories 3 and 4) to be added by December 2026.
Total GScale investment cited at ~INR500 crore.
Management said full-fledged manufacturing setup to be complete around March (2027).
Manufacturing mix: GScale to make 60-70% of equipment in-house and source the balance; management says this can be increased.
Semiconductor-grade glass-lining reactors: glass sourced from Japan, fabrication and glass spraying in India; no technology transfer agreement currently.
demand_pricing: Management cites India data-centre capacity of 1.8 GW expected to grow to ~10.2-10.5 GW by ~2030-31; investment of USD5-7 million per MW, of which ~65% is products and installation.
GScale has one big order from a top Indian client for semiconductor-related glass-lining reactors (GL Hakko-linked); pilot-plant order for LED/electronic chemicals also cited.
Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger price cut claimed: from ~INR30 lakh to ~INR12-15 lakh per unit (>50% lower), with management arguing it is a client benefit and margin-accretive.
India glass-lining TAM cited at ~INR1,500 crore; shell-and-tube heat exchanger TAM ~INR2,000 crore in India and ~USD2 billion globally.
Management claims no global competitor makes the GL Hakko shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger or low-leaching glass; unverified.
Export share remained low at 2-3% in Q1 due to global uncertainty; shipping costs cited by an analyst as up ~4x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GScale business, margins, and timing of order conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Brahma Reddy said five customers (three global MNCs, two Indian) are in LOI or near-order stage; target is ~INR250 crore revenue by end-FY27, clarified as revenue not order booking. Margin guided at 23-25% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise slightly as shell-and-tube and semiconductor products scale from September, but gave no quantified figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an unexecuted order book for core business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, ~INR1,400 crore after Q1 billing, with some billing expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin down and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to mechanisation in two units, which reduced consumable consumption; employee costs rising with recruitment. Management said margins will be maintained at 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said days were ~320 last year, targeted below 200 by September, driven by customer advances and receivable collection with stock held flat.

qa_highlights.question: Royalty on imported technology?
qa_highlights.answer: No royalty currently; licensing model, with JV and technology-transfer discussions ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre project timelines and value-add?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical industry project 24-36 months; GScale targets 18-20 months. Customers may free-issue some long-lead items; the 60% in-house share can be increased.

risks_watch: GScale execution: equipment arrival (mid-September), November start, and ramp to INR250 crore revenue in FY27 with only ~2 lakh sq ft initially in full execution.
Working capital: management's <200 day target versus ~320 days last year; GScale projects may carry advances and receivables.
Margin pressure: the 17.5% EBITDA margin reflects rising employee and other costs; management says 17-18% is sustainable.
Dependence on GL Hakko technology: critical glass manufacturing remains in Japan with no technology transfer agreement; GL Hakko stake to step up to 51% only on targets.
Forward guidance gaps: FY28 numbers for GScale and consolidated revenue not yet guided; a Q&A figure of ~INR3,000 crore for FY28 was not confirmed by management.
Customer concentration: GScale's five named-stage customers are unnamed; claims of no global competitor are unverified.
key_quotes: This has been another record quarter for us, and I want to say this clearly , this is not a one-time achievement.
Working capital days I think last year 320 days, 320 days. And this year we are that is going to coming down to below 200 days.
Margins? No. No.
Mr. Shiva, go ahead.
Brahma Reddy: We will guide soon.

544333|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 62.3% YoY to INR296.6 crore and EBITDA 79.7% to INR51.4 crore, while PAT grew 37.9% to INR28.2 crore.
544333|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR296.6 crore (up 62.3% YoY), EBITDA INR51.4 crore (up 79.7%) and PAT INR28.2 crore (up 37.9%). PBT grew more slowly (41.4%) because interest income fell after surplus fixed deposits were deployed into GScale Energy and GL Hakko stakes. H1 FY27 revenue was INR544.3 crore (up 53%) and operating cash flow was INR61 crore, above the INR45 crore for all of FY26. GScale is still pre-operational, with revenue targeted from December 2026 and FY27 guidance of over INR250 crore from GScale alongside about 50% core growth, for a total of INR1,450 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Exceeds INR45 crore generated in full FY26

segments.name: Core engineering (SETL)
segments.commentary: Management says core business grew about 50% in FY27 guidance; order book stated at almost INR1,000 crore, with H1 inflow about INR600 crore and a further INR600 crore targeted in H2. Core EBITDA margin is 17.3%. Exports are 7-8% of revenue this year.

segments.name: GScale Energy (data center infrastructure)
segments.commentary: Pre-operational. Secondary fluid network (SFN) revenue targeted from 15 December 2026, power products production from 15 January 2027. Target over INR250 crore revenue in Q4 FY27. Long-term EBITDA margin target 20-25%. Stake: 34% acquired for about INR125 crore cash, with a further 17.45% via INR64 crore share swap pending exchange approval, taking the holding to 51%.

segments.name: GL Hakko (Japan)
segments.commentary: 19.19% stake acquired as first phase of investment, supporting glass-lining technology, R&D and engineering capabilities. Export-focused.

GScale revenue of over INR250 crore targeted in Q4 FY27, subject to timely production readiness and execution.
Factory go-live slipped about 15 days from end-November to around 15 December 2026.
Exports targeted at 20-30% of consolidated revenue in 2-3 years; FY27 exports about 7-8%.
Management expects QoQ absolute PAT to rise from Q3 FY27 as interest income effect stabilises; FY28 and FY29 guidance to come later.
GScale EBITDA target 20-25%; core business to rise from 17.3% to about 20% over coming years.
Installed capacity after adding 3-4 lakh sq ft: core production capacity of about INR3,500-4,000 crore (management's figure); no timeline given.
risks_watch: GScale go-live timing: factory now targeted 15 December 2026; SFN revenue depends on it, and any further slippage pushes the INR250 crore Q4 target.
No named or signed GScale orders disclosed; MNC tender results pending and described as large and slow to close.

Pending exchange approval for the 17.45% share swap needed to reach 51% of GScale.
Interest income loss from deployed funds will continue until GScale and GL Hakko contribute; PBT growth trails EBITDA growth.
Management declined to give capex per MW or peak revenue from the current 4 lakh sq ft facility, and deferred FY28 guidance.
544333|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, data center opportunity and order visibility, but evasive on specifics: order names, peak revenue, capex per MW and FY28 guidance were all deferred. Timelines have already slipped by about 15 days.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the company plans to raise its stake in GScale, given the INR125 crore for 34%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR64 crore share swap for a further 17.45% (taking the holding to 51%) is awaiting stock exchange approval; shareholders have approved it.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 consolidated revenue growth from GScale, the Japan subsidiary and the group, plus 2-3 year guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 guidance is almost 50% growth in the core business plus over INR250 crore from GScale, for a total of INR1,450 crore; FY28 and FY29 guidance to come later.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the profit decline was due to inventory build-up and whether absolute PAT would rise QoQ from next quarter.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not inventory; lower interest income from deployed fixed deposits explains it. It confirmed absolute QoQ PAT should rise from the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the factory delay affects the INR250 crore target and whether any clients have signed.
qa_highlights.answer: GScale said go-live slipped about 15 days from end-November; SFN revenue targeted from 15 December. It cited more than 10 inquiries and pre-operational visits with a couple of unnamed customers, but no signed orders were named.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about peak revenue and capacity utilisation timelines for the existing facility.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave facility sq ft figures and said core capacity of about INR3,500-4,000 crore after the expansion, but gave no timeline and deferred guidance on peak revenue.

capex_capacity: Core SETL facility is about 8 lakh sq ft; management plans to add 3-4 lakh sq ft, to reach about 1.2 million sq ft, with an update expected in one to two months.
After the added 3-4 lakh sq ft, core production capacity is about INR3,500-4,000 crore (management figure). No timeline given; CEO said 'we will guide you on this growth prospect'.

GScale has about 4 lakh sq ft; 2.9 lakh sq ft to be operational from 15 January 2027, with another 1 lakh sq ft added in 3-4 months. A greenfield GScale facility of about 1.5-1.6 million sq ft on a 36-acre site is being built, taking GScale to 1.95 million sq ft in total.
GScale factory go-live slipped about 15 days from end-November to around 15 December 2026; most machinery is in place and a few components are yet to arrive for commissioning.
Management declined to give capex per MW or peak revenue from the current facility. Analyst cited INR500 crore data-center investment; CEO said the stake purchase is separate from that capex.
Analyst asked whether the company would go beyond 51% in GScale; management answered 'No'.
demand_pricing: Core order book stated at almost INR1,000 crore; order inflow about INR600 crore in H1 FY27, with a further INR600 crore targeted in H2 and about INR400-500 crore carrying into FY28.
CDMO and pharma demand described as strong with significant orders received, but no customer names or order values disclosed.

Exports about 7-8% of revenue in FY27; one large export order of USD 8-9 million said to be expected any time. Exports targeted at 20-30% of consolidated revenue in 2-3 years. Tie-ups: IPP for Europe and US, API Pharma for Middle East, Biocon Solutions for Southeast Asia (resellers).

GScale: more than 10 inquiries; pre-operational visits done with a couple of customers (unnamed). Recently qualified for a tender from one MNC; results pending. Management said a couple of MNCs are active and closure expected in the next couple of weeks.
GScale pricing: management said India is at least 25-30% cheaper than Southeast Asia for a switchgear panel delivered into the EMEA market.
GScale revenue mix for INR250 crore target: SFN pipes, installation and commissioning, and power products; management said the major portion comes from SFN.
