544370|2026-03.headline: Nukleus FY26 total income rose 25.49% YoY to INR 36.19 crore, with PAT of INR 213.53 lakh and EBITDA of INR 917.34 lakh.
544370|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong growth in income and EBITDA, with management attributing margin expansion mainly to technology-led sales and operating productivity. Operational footprint is about 25 centres (17 co-working, 8 managed office) across Delhi NCR and Bengaluru, with roughly 7.3 lakh sq ft under management, about 3.06 lakh sq ft operational (figures differ across answers), and occupancy near 85%. Management is shifting the mix toward managed office and back-to-back deals, guiding to about 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, but declined to give revenue numbers for that capacity. Several slides had revenue-mix errors that management said would be corrected later.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 92.75 lakh earlier; management stated about 8% increase, which conflicts with the figures quoted

segments.name: Co-working
segments.commentary: Management said co-working grows about 10% a year and carries the highest margin (illustratively about 30%). Its share of the portfolio is falling, from about 70% at IPO to roughly 50% now.

segments.name: Managed office
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-40% a year per management. Targeted to reach about 70% of portfolio in the expansion phase and about 90% over 3-4 years. Illustrative margin about 25%.

segments.name: Back-to-back / enterprise deals
segments.commentary: Illustrative margin about 20%. Landlord-funded fit-outs and revenue-sharing deals are increasing, reducing Nukleus's capex needs.

guidance_outlook: Operational area is expected to reach more than 10 lakh sq ft by end FY27, up from about 3.5 lakh sq ft now; management said this is a 10x rise from the IPO's about 1 lakh sq ft.
Management declined to give a revenue estimate for the current 3.5 lakh sq ft, saying it was too early to quantify.
Management said it intends to sustain the pace of square-footage addition for at least five years, without giving a percentage target.
Plans to expand beyond Delhi NCR and Bengaluru into Pune and Hyderabad, and eventually be a national brand in major cities.
Management said it will be among the biggest operators in three years, without quantifying this.
Management said accounts will move to Ind AS in FY27.
capex_capacity: Centre set-up takes about 3 months; bookings start around month 2; occupancy typically reaches a good level within about 6 months of opening.
Around 7 lakh sq ft under management; about 3.06 lakh sq ft operational per the presentation, while the call cited 3.5-3.6 lakh sq ft operational; the rest is CWIP or under development.
Committed area of about 7.5 lakh sq ft against about 2.5 lakh sq ft expected at IPO; RHP commitment was 1.04 lakh sq ft and the company said it delivered 1.24 lakh sq ft.
Flagship centres include Noida Sector 142 (about 1.5-2 lakh sq ft inventory), Logic Cyber Park, Skymark, IFCO Tower Gurugram and Prestige Blue Chip Bengaluru (Dairy Circle).
demand_pricing: Management cited office leasing of 82.6 million sq ft in CY2025, with GCCs taking about 44% of Q1 2026 absorption (9.1 million sq ft, 48% in Bengaluru).
Management said it is equipped to serve current GCC requirements and has started participating in RFPs; no GCC client signed yet, though it expects to sign its first one soon.
Pricing is set manually per centre to target 85-95% occupancy; dynamic pricing is not used and management said it is four to five years away for the sector.
Management said managed-office clients sign 4-9 year agreements, with revenue starting from day one and no vacancy gap for back-to-back deals.
Management said the client base has moved from startups and SMEs toward Fortune 500 and blue-chip companies, without naming clients.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs and leverage evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finance cost rose to about INR 11.5 lakh from INR 92.75 lakh, described as an 8% increase, while long-term borrowings grew materially. The figures quoted do not reconcile, so the change needs checking against the filed accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is targeted on new fixed-asset investment, and when do new centres stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: No ROCE target was given. Management said centres take about 3 months to build, reach a good occupancy level in about 6 months, and that revenue impact from the 10 lakh sq ft pipeline will fall mainly in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain came from operations versus accounting adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed most of the gain to productivity. An AI call-filter reportedly cut calls handled per salesperson by 60-70%. No capitalisation adjustment was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand-based dynamic pricing used, and how does Nukleus compete with larger players?
qa_highlights.answer: Dynamic pricing is not used. Management said the largest operator holds about 1.5 crore sq ft and nobody in the sector is large yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current operational area, and how much will be managed office vs co-working?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 7 lakh sq ft under management, about 3.5 lakh sq ft operational, and over 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, with a mix moving toward 70% managed office and 30% co-working.

qa_highlights.question: Why focus on managed office, and what are the margins and contract terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said managed office and back-to-back deals deliver scale and longer contracts, while co-working has higher per-sq-ft profit but is slow to grow. Contracts run 4-9 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nukleus adopt Ind AS and use NDS-based EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Nipun Gupta said the accounts will be converted to Ind AS in this financial year (FY27).

risks_watch: Inconsistent figures: the operational area was stated as 3.06 lakh, 3.5 lakh and 3.6 lakh sq ft in different parts of the call; the revenue-mix slide was flagged for correction; and the finance-cost numbers do not reconcile.
Execution risk on the pipeline of more than 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, given a 3-6 month occupancy ramp and the need to fill newly added space.
Rising debt to fund expansion, with management not giving a leverage target and ROCE falling as capital employed grew.
No GCC client signed yet despite RFP participation; GCC conversion is a key watch item.
Related-party and governance questions: a management board member (Pooja Gupta) handles finance, and the company is only about a year post-SME listing.
544370|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, technology and national ambitions, but cautious and evasive on numbers: it declined to quantify revenue potential, ROCE targets and client names, and admitted errors in its slides.
key_quotes: So, during the financial year, all the money that we took from the market has been deployed effectively.
We will be one of the biggest in next three years. That is what I can assure you today.
I think there will be a significant growth is better put, putting a number to this is something I don't think is a good idea at this kind of a stage.

rows.why: Operational area is guided to more than 10 lakh sq ft by end FY27 from about 3.06-3.5 lakh sq ft now, with centres already under construction (about 7 lakh sq ft under management and committed area of 7.5 lakh sq ft), though the figures are inconsistent across the call.

544396|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 2.4x YoY to INR 68.46 crore; FY26 revenue about INR 209 crore with EBITDA near INR 65 crore, with management guiding ~70% CAGR to INR 850-900 crore by FY29.
544396|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a transformation year, shifting mix away from PPaaS toward TSP, with international, SaaS and RegTech as the planned growth drivers. Q4 revenue was about INR 68.46 crore, EBITDA INR 19.26 crore and net profit INR 12.24 crore, and the call noted Q4 as the lowest EBITDA margin quarter. FY26 operating cash flow was negative, which management attributed to longer TSP credit periods. Management guided to ~70% revenue CAGR over three years, with the first-year (FY27) run-rate on the order of INR 340-350 crore, and said the mix shift would lift margins over time.

net profit fell 9.7% per analyst question; PAT margin about 20% vs 25%

segments.commentary: Management said more than a year of effort has not delivered desired results; engine being pivoted to domestic merchant orchestration and global PPaaS. Guided at 5-8% contribution in FY27-FY29 per analyst reading of slides; about 40+ accounts in funnel.

Management said about 40% of FY27 international business is already in hand, and bagged a large RegTech order including a central payment body abroad. Mix of license and SaaS.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of about 70% over three years; FY29 revenue INR 850-900 crore per management (analyst cited ~INR 950 crore), from FY26 base of about INR 209 crore.
FY27 growth of about 70% targeted; analyst-proposed FY27 range INR 340-350 crore accepted as 'anything around that range'.

Operating cash flow conversion expected to improve as TSP credit periods shorten; no specific conversion figure given.
AI targets: 30% efficiency in support functions, 50% faster development, 1.5x capacity from existing business; RegTech AI revenue from FY27; revenue per employee up 300% in three years.
Market growth cited: payment processing 22% CAGR, RegTech ~32%, digital lending and orchestration above 40%.

Unallocated Tata Mutual Fund funds (INR 300 crore referenced by analyst): management said no inorganic deal has been signed; some deals rejected after due diligence; deployment expected in global assets and beyond-payments areas (RegTech, lending).

Management said credit period reflects TSP mix and will reduce with mix shift; analyst-cited receivable days of about 180 are not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 operating cash flow negative and what EBITDA-to-OCF conversion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Aggarwal attributed it to the shift from PPaaS to TSP, which carries longer credit periods; expects conversion to improve gradually as international and other mix rises. No numeric conversion target given.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the 70% CAGR and when will EBITDA reach 33-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Thakur said confidence is high given the funnel: about 200 SaaS tenants, about 10 international countries, and 40+ PPaaS accounts. Said full-year FY26 margin impact came from TSP mix, and balancing the year should bring EBITDA back to prior levels; no quarter given for 33-35%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the absolute revenue numbers for FY27-FY29?

qa_highlights.answer: About 40% is in hand at the start of the year, with the balance dependent on advanced discussions expected to convert in Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.answer: Management defined high margin as above 70% over India margin, with international margins of 30-40% or more on a 15-20% India base; the gap is due to the product being roughly 5-6 years ahead of the target markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for PPaaS given weak results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pivoting PPaaS to merchant orchestration domestically and to global markets; two advanced discussions expected to close by end Q1 or early Q2; will not over-invest until results show.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profitability decline and what is the status of the Tata Mutual Fund funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin decline attributed to the mix shift from high-margin PPaaS to low-margin TSP. Some inorganic deals were rejected after due diligence; the company is looking for a deal that gives instant global presence and execution, or moves into RegTech and lending; no deployment made yet.

544396|2026-06.headline: NPST Q1 FY27 revenue about INR 61.42 crore, roughly 75% YoY but down QoQ; management reiterates 60-70% FY27 growth and ~30% EBITDA margin guidance.

Management held FY27 guidance of 60-70% growth and around 30% EBITDA margin, and flagged MDR on UPI as a possible future revenue driver that is not yet quantified. International revenue is about 10-12% of consolidated revenue, and management targets around 50% over about two years.

544396|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated income rose about 50% YoY to Rs 72.95 crore, a record quarter, with PAT of Rs 13.21 crore.
544396|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 consolidated income of about Rs 72.95 crore, up roughly 50% YoY from Rs 48.68 crore and about 19-20% QoQ from Rs 61.42 crore. rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the acquisition (funded from existing cash, announcement expected by next quarter) is not capex and its size is undisclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was held unchanged and H2 must ramp steeply, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue of Rs 134 cr must roughly double-plus in H2 to reach the analyst's Rs 216-226 cr, several deals are unquantified, and the UPI MDR impact is unknown.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Compliance-in-a-box is being added to bank-in-a-box, DPDP and compliance products are rolling out, and the Sri Lanka and bank-in-a-box deals are slated to start Q4 FY27 with first revenue.

rows.label: Sri Lanka telecom deal execution
rows.why: Execution starts Q4 FY27, contribution from FY28 with bigger numbers in FY29-30 on a five-year term, though value is unquantified.

rows.label: International pipeline 5-15 opportunities
rows.why: Management is in active discussions in more than 10 countries and expects some results in Q3-Q4 FY27, with no numbers disclosed.

rows.label: Acquisition funded from cash
rows.why: Management expects to announce a deal between now and next quarter, funded from existing cash with international targets prioritised, though size and terms are undisclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 execution, the Sri Lanka deal and the international pipeline but cautious on margins and evasive on sizing the Sri Lanka deal, bank-in-a-box value, acquisition cost and UPI MDR impact; analysts probed H2 achievability and the margin path.

544397|2026-03.headline: Ather's FY26 volumes rose ~66% with Q4 at 83,000 units; Q4 EBITDA loss narrowed to about -2% of revenue, while commodity inflation is expected to pressure margins near term.
544397|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a breakthrough year, with volumes up about 66% led by Rizta (almost three-quarters of sales) and market share up from about 8% to 18.6% in Q4. Store count doubled from 351 to 700 by March 2026, and AGM with subsidy improved from 19% to 24% (about 12% to 21% without subsidy) on COGS reduction of about 9 percentage points. Q4 EBITDA loss improved about 2,000 bps to roughly -2%. Management flagged sharp commodity inflation (lithium, rare earth magnets, memory, aluminium) that will pressure margins in the short term, with only a small part passed on so far, and said the Factory 3.0 (AURIC) and EL platform are the key FY27 levers.

financial_highlights.change: up ~23% QoQ per analyst question/management reference to volume growth
highest ever; rose through the year

segments.name: Middle India (Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, MP, Odisha, Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Market share rose from about 4% at start of FY25 to 17.3%; store additions up 125% YoY. Gujarat and Odisha at about 19-20%, Maharashtra at 16%+ from about 8%.

segments.name: South India
segments.commentary: Market share moved from 13% to 23% with 80% more stores; quarterly sales rose from about 27,000 to about 41,000 units. Kerala Pro-Pack attach about 98-99%.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Market share tripled from just under 4% to about 12%; Rest of India Pro-Pack attach at 81%, the weakest zone.

guidance_outlook: EL platform (mass and mass-premium focus, INR1-1.25 lakh segment where Ather has no product) to be commercialised by festive season and in the field before end of CY26; management said no exact launch month given.

Factory 3.0 (AURIC, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar): Phase 1 of 5 lakh units capacity (10 lakh total) to start trial production before end CY26 and 42,000 units/month incremental capacity fully operational before end FY27; first revenue from new factory expected in Q4 FY27.
Cost reduction to come mainly from EL over FY27 (more back-loaded); 450/Rizta platform cost reduction to be smaller than prior two years.

Short-term margin pressure expected from commodity inflation (commodity cost inflation estimated at 40-50%, BOM increase a fraction of that); further price hike possible in coming months after roughly INR4,000 blended hikes in CY26 so far.
FAME subsidy expiry in coming months to reduce realisation by about INR5,000 per vehicle.
No specific new-store guidance for FY27; management expects the current quarterly EC opening pace to broadly continue.
capex_capacity: Current Hosur plant designed for 35,000 units/month; running at 90-95% utilisation for multiple recent months, with some headroom left.
AURIC Factory 3.0 Phase 1: 5 lakh capacity out of 10 lakh planned; adds 42,000 units/month; trial production before end CY26.
Factory 3.0 to add in-house battery pack assembly, transmission assembly, painting, electronics assembly and CED coating, raising vertical integration.
Hosur plant moved to triple-shift operation, adding depreciation.
Service centres more than doubled in FY26; store count doubled to 700.
demand_pricing: Q4 retail demand ran above estimates (retail includes units sold by dealers pending registration); supply rather than demand was the binding constraint.
Price hikes: about INR1,000-1,500 in Q4 FY26 and about INR2,500 blended in April 2026, roughly INR4,000 in CY26 so far.
Q4 ASP flat QoQ; management attributed this to Q4 offer structures and newer stores in Middle/North India, expecting it to rise as stores mature.
Pro-Pack attach: Kerala about 98-99%, Middle India second, Rest of India 81%; Madhya Pradesh rose from 40-50% to over 80-85% within about a year.
Lithium up about 2-2.5x from around $8/kg to about $24/kg at peak, cooled somewhat; cell share of BOM rose from 15-16% (sub-20%) to a larger share.
Competition: peers have many variants across price bands while Ather has 6 premium, 3 mass-premium and no mass or entry variants.
Industry: management views the sub-INR1 lakh segment as 15-20% of market, INR1.25 lakh and above as 25-30% (top-five-OEM volumes only, indicative).

qa_highlights.question: How do Pro-Pack attach rates differ between mature South markets and newer Middle/Rest of India markets?
qa_highlights.answer: South highest (Kerala ~98-99%), then Middle India, then Rest of India at 81%; new cities start lower and reach 80%+ within two to four quarters, with existing dealer partners ramping faster (about three-quarters of new stores).

qa_highlights.question: Is 400 branch expansion in FY27 accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific FY27 store guidance; EL is the main FY27-28 growth driver and store expansion is becoming business-as-usual at the current quarterly pace.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost inflation has been passed on, and how will it be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a small part passed on so far due to procurement and stockpiling; some burden may be shared with suppliers, but the bulk is expected to fall on the company or customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 ASP flat QoQ despite the price hike and higher attach rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 offer structures and newer stores in Middle and North India with lower ASPs, expecting these to normalise as stores age.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 34% and depreciation rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose on variable warranty and logistics costs with volume up, plus marketing and a year-end warranty calibration; depreciation reflects the 450 platform (seven-year life), triple-shift operation at Hosur, and useful-life recalibration of tools; EL amortisation starts next FY.

qa_highlights.question: Are there supply issues compared with competitors and when will new capacity contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Only localised constraints (Nov-Dec variants, April election-related labour disruption); no secular material shortage. New factory revenue expected in Q4 FY27.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (lithium, aluminium, rare earths, memory) with management expecting margin pressure in the short term and limited pass-through so far.
EL launch timing (festive season or by end CY26) and Factory 3.0 Phase 1 commissioning slipping beyond CY26 / Q3 FY27.
FAME subsidy expiry removing about INR5,000 per vehicle from realisations in coming months.
Supply constraints at 90-95% utilisation of current plant limiting volume capture in South and Middle India.
Rising warranty provisions and variable other expenses; depreciation step-up as EL amortisation begins next FY.
Electric motorcycles would need a separate Zenith platform; no timeline given.
544397|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, market share and EBITDA progress, but cautious on near-term margins, saying commodity inflation will pressure margins and cannot be fully mitigated. Management avoided giving exact dates or FY27 store guidance, pointing to EL and Factory 3.0 timelines as directional.
key_quotes: Which means there will be a pressure on margins, one that we will try and mitigate as much as possible with price hikes and even more work on things like accessories and software, but they can't be fully mitigated.
So, we're definitely running at the edge, and hence any gaps are very unforgiving.
We're not giving any specific guidance for new store expansion in FY '27.
And the full 42,000 should be operationalized before end of this FY for sure.

rows.when: trial production before end CY26; 42,000 units/month fully o
rows.why: Factory 3.0 Phase 1 (5 lakh of 10 lakh total, +42,000 units/month) is already under construction with a stated timeline, and Hosur is running at 90-95% utilisation on a 35,000 units/month design.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 volumes rose about 66% with Q4 at 83,000 units and market share at 18.6%; demand ran above estimates and supply is the binding constraint at 92.5% utilisation, though volume capture depends on Factory 3.0 and EL timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Hosur at 92.5% utilisation with triple-shift already in place, so further capacity beyond AURIC Phase 1 (5 of 10 lakh units still to build) is a plausible next step, though no new capex figure has been given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no numeric revenue guidance, but volume momentum (+66% FY26, Q4 share 18.6%) and above-estimate retail demand could support upside if supply is added, offset by margin headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity inflation of 40-50% with only a small pass-through, a FAME subsidy hit of about INR5,000 per vehicle, and EL or Factory 3.0 timing slipping past CY26 or Q3 FY27 are the named risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: by festive season / before end CY26
rows.why: Management expects the EL platform (INR1-1.25 lakh segment where Ather has no product) to be commercialised and in the field before end CY26, though no exact launch month has been given.

rows.label: Further price hike to offset commodity inflation
rows.why: Roughly INR4,000 blended hikes in CY26 so far, with management open to another hike after commodity cost inflation of 40-50%, yet only a small part of inflation has been passed on.

rows.label: EL platform cost reduction in FY27
rows.why: Management said cost reduction will come mainly from EL over FY27, with the 450/Rizta platform saving less than the prior two years, and AGM already up to 24% (21% ex-subsidy) from COGS cut of about 9 points.

rows.label: Store network expansion
rows.why: Stores doubled from 351 to 700 in FY26 and management expects the current quarterly opening pace to continue, though no specific FY27 store number was guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume share gains, store expansion and Factory 3.0 and EL timelines, but cautious on near-term margins from commodity inflation and limited pass-through; analysts pressed on Q4 ASP flat QoQ, Pro-Pack attach gaps and cost pass-through.

544397|2026-06.headline: Ather Energy Q1 FY27: wholesale volumes up 81% to 83,000 units, first-ever positive EBITDA of Rs 9 crore (~0.8% margin), AGM down to 22.4%.
544397|2026-06.overview: Management described a sharp demand upswing driven by policy support, fuel-availability concerns and TCO gains, with registrations up 102% YoY and paid preorders up 158% to 1.5 lakh. Production was constrained at the Hosur plant (35,000 units/month max, reached near full utilisation by June), leaving dealer inventory at about 3 days versus 14 days earlier. Commodity costs rose sharply, cutting adjusted gross margin by 5.6 percentage points to 22.4%, partly offset by an average selling price rise to Rs 1.61 lakh and disciplined fixed-cost control that delivered the first positive EBITDA. Management expects further commodity hits of 100-200 bps, to be largely offset by price increases that were only partly reflected in Q1.

segments.name: Middle India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 141% YoY, the highest of all zones in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Retail grew 118% YoY in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: South India
segments.commentary: Retail grew 76% YoY in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue (AtherStack Pro, accessories, services)
segments.commentary: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for established two-wheeler peers; accessories undisclosed.

guidance_outlook: Commodity headwind: management expects a further 100-200 bps hit beyond the 5.6% in Q1, to be largely absorbed through price hikes; Q2 full-quarter ASP benefit expected.

AURIC Phase 1 (Aurangabad, Factory 3.0) go-live later in calendar 2026; expected to take total capacity from 4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units per year; full ramp to 42,000 units/month in 4-5 months, possibly spilling into early FY28.
EL scooter (brand name to be unveiled) launch later in August 2026; target 60,000 units/month capacity across Aurangabad and Hosur (42,000 from AURIC Phase 1 plus 18,000 from Hosur).
AURIC Phase 2 could add 5 lakh units/year (total 14.2 lakh); planning stage only, firmer timeline possibly within a quarter or two.
Fundraise: Rs 1,300 crore QIP completed; a further Rs 1,200 crore preference issue pending shareholder approval, total Rs 2,500 crore.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension awaited; about 15-20% of Q1 vehicles sold without subsidy; Q2 subsidy treatment uncertain.
capex_capacity: Hosur plant: maximum 35,000 units/month (about 4.2 lakh/year), near 100% utilisation as of the call; can allocate 18,000 units/month to EL or to Rizta/450X, not both.

AURIC (Aurangabad) Phase 1: equipment installation ending in next couple of months; trial production from festive period; reliable daily output from 1 January; assembly line set up, paint shop under trial.
Ather Community Day on 29 August 2026 in Bengaluru to unveil the EL scooter.
New store openings slowed in Q1; expected to surge once EL and AURIC are live around the festive season. Stores reportedly reach operational profitability in about 5-6 months on average.
demand_pricing: Industry e-2W penetration reported at 11%, up 44%; industry registrations up 68% YoY to 525k in Q1 FY27; Ather inquiries up 95%; over 7 lakh inquiries in Q1; Ather brand searches up about 118%.

Management estimates unrealised retail potential of 13,000-15,000 units per month above the roughly 30,000 units/month retailed; some dealers have stopped accepting preorders with waits of about 2 months.
Pricing power: ASP moved from Rs 1.5 lakh (Q4) to Rs 1.53 lakh (April and May) and Rs 1.61 lakh (June), with price hikes described as 100% margin accretive.
Customer profile reportedly unchanged; retail finance and TCO advantage cited as supporting willingness to pay higher prices.
EL launch expected to depress ASP somewhat, with launch focus on northern and rest-of-India markets and attach rate guided at least 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the commodity headwind be a similar 5-6% again next quarter, or stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a further 100-200 bps of hit, not 5-6%, and says commodity costs may be near the top; quarterly averages understate end-of-quarter costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee and other expense control a new baseline before AURIC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not exceptional, reflecting cautious spending in FY27 after a strong FY26; some AURIC costs will be capitalised initially, with P&L impact from Q4 onwards alongside volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does 60,000 EL capacity relate to Hosur's 35,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: AURIC Phase 1 is dedicated to EL at 42,000/month; Hosur gives flexibility of 18,000 units/month, shared with Rizta and 450X, so total is 60,000 for EL and not additive.

qa_highlights.question: Can AURIC Phase 2 be brought forward, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is in planning; the Rs 2,500 crore raise gives funding to fast-track it, with firmer timelines possibly within one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-vehicle revenue and service?
qa_highlights.answer: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item and benefited from price increases; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for mature peers, and is expected to compound with fleet size.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ather enter electric motorcycles soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on EL platform products over the next year; a motorcycle launch is more than a year away, probably two years or more.

risks_watch: Commodity costs could rise a further 100-200 bps; margin recovery depends on price increases and commodity cooling, which management says is hard to predict.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension not yet confirmed; about 15-20% of Q1 volumes sold without subsidy.
AURIC Phase 1 ramp risk: go-live slated for later in 2026, possible slip into early FY28; supply already short of demand by about 15,000 units per month per analyst.
EL launch may lower ASP and could cannibalise Rizta; attach-rate and margin mix to be watched.
Dealer inventory at about 3 days leaves little buffer; new store additions paused until capacity arrives.
544397|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and pricing power, with management calling demand unprecedented and the first positive EBITDA a milestone. More cautious on commodity costs and timelines, repeatedly declining to commit to exact AURIC ramp months or Phase 2 dates.
key_quotes: Happy to report that our teams have been able to drive very strong success on both added sales price increase and improved SKU.
Our EBITDA came in at a Rs. 9 crore margin for Q1 2027, which is roughly about 0.8%.
Hosur can anyways do 35,000 a month, and we are also trying to push that up a little bit more.
I would cautiously guide at least 75% attach rates with EL also, but I would hope for even higher.

544397|2026-09.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
544397|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

segments.name: Zones (registrations growth)
segments.commentary: Industry registrations grew 82% YoY to about 6 lakh in Q2. Ather growth was 82% in South, 85% in Middle India and 79% in Rest of India; Rest of India was the fastest-rising zone as Konarc rolled out in northern states and sales were prioritised there.

segments.name: Konarc (new mainstream scooter)
segments.commentary: Launched 29 August 2026 with only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Mid variants SR2 and SR3 are live, SR1 is due by Q4 FY27, and the Z variant is not yet in production.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue
segments.commentary: Non-vehicle revenue was 15% of total. AtherStack Pro is more than 50% of it, with accessories and servicing split roughly equally. Management indicated gross margins of about 30-40% for accessories, 40-45% for spares and 80-90% for AtherStack Pro.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

AURIC Phase 1 trial production expected in the next few weeks (Q3 FY27), with capex installation complete by Q4 FY27; full capacity realisation takes a couple of quarters, with ramp-up expected within FY28.
Dealer/experience-centre network expansion to restart from around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4 FY27; fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters.

No further price hikes in Q3 FY27 and no planned price increases on the current portfolio for the next few quarters; Konarc's entry variants may lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.
Management expects like-to-like Konarc gross margin to be 6-7% better than Rizta in the long term; Konarc is already a few thousand rupees cheaper than Rizta on a like-to-like basis.
Commodities seen as flat in recent weeks; management says Q3 is not expected to be worse than Q2 but volatility remains high. Subsidy is broadly unchanged QoQ.
Electric motorcycle launch: no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Current manufacturing capacity averaged 33,000 units/month in Q2 FY27, up from 28,000 in Q1; Hosur is at 35,000 units/month capacity and is described as at its limit.
Hosur expansion adds 6,000 units/month, live later in Q3 FY27. Total installed capacity is about 77,000 units/month after AURIC Phase 1 base (42,000) before the additional expansion.
AURIC Phase 1 (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) adds 12,000 units/month of incremental capacity by Q2 FY28, taking installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units/year from 9.2 lakh units/year.
Management estimates about 20,000 units/month of unrealised retail demand at current run-rate, with demand in the 50,000-60,000 units/month range.
Ather Node (apartment EV charging) is being industrialised and will begin deployment in the next few months; Ather Bedrock 5th-gen battery packs are live across 450, Rizta and Konarc.
demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.
Pan-India E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time, at about 11.2% for Q2 FY27 (industry commentary cites 11.6% as the quarterly figure).
Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, helped by price hikes and SKU/incentive management. Management says part of the gain is temporary.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory chips) hit gross margin by about 9.4%. Management says SKU management recovered 2.7pp of this, a more temporary lever.
Structural gross-margin gains of about 5.3pp over two quarters came from price hikes, VAVE and cost reduction.
Konarc early Stack Pro attach rates are said to be as strong as Rizta, but management wants at least two quarters before assuming ~90% attach for Konarc, given a more non-South-heavy mix.
Tier 2 penetration is rising fastest; Maharashtra Tier 2 penetration is about 18-19%. Company is not yet present in rural markets.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the new AURIC Phase 1 capacity ramp up, given it is greenfield, and when will the 6.5 lakh figure be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AURIC Phase 1's base 42,000 units will take about two quarters to ramp; the additional 12,000 units going live in Q2 FY28 may ramp faster. Full ramp is expected within FY28, while Hosur ramp is expected to be rapid from the end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much pricing headroom remains if commodities stay elevated into next calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not want to raise prices on the current portfolio for the next few quarters. Konarc's more aggressive entry portfolio gives better unit economics, so it could lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are Konarc bookings and cannibalisation trending in launched regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Konarc has only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Inquiries, preorders and walk-ins are up several times in Rajasthan and UP, and Konarc Z demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ASP rise driven by scooter buyers or motorcycle buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the buyers are still scooter buyers paying for better experience, quality and features, not motorcycle buyers. Stack Pro attach is high across the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% margin gain sustainable, and does the 2.7% SKU lever reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5.3% is broadly structural (price hikes, VAVE, cost reduction). The 2.7% SKU/incentive lever is more temporary and can be reopened if supply is tight or commodities stay high, but it is not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: How are dealer network expansion and experience-centre additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters as dealer expansion was held back. Expansion restarts around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Konarc variant rollout sequenced with mid variants first and entry variants later?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity constraints on 450 and Rizta changed the plan. SR2 and SR3 launched first, SR1 is due by Q4 once Aurangabad capacity is available, and Z comes later. Geographic rollout started in the North.

544402|2026-09.headline: Jash Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 195 Cr, but INR 46 Cr of Sept-end deliveries stuck in transit cut recognised revenue; FY guidance of INR 875 Cr retained.

Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Karnataka concentration is limited.
Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales in Q1, down from last year because of IPL spend in the base quarter.
E-commerce profitability is said to be close to retail profitability, with growth now coming without deep discounting.
Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why the divergence between primary and secondary sales in Lifestyle wholesale, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

risks_watch: Wholesale growth of 5% and gross margin contraction of about 150 bps in Q1; watch whether the festive shift reverses in Q2.
3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and the wage-regulation outcome in Karnataka at the High Court.
Consumer wallet pressure from inflation; management says it has seen no meaningful demand shift so far but is cautious about H2.
Reebok BIS certification risk on imports from factories outside India, renewed annually.
Net store additions of 150-200 against a gross plan above 300; watch LFL sustainability through closures.
key_quotes: So, when you look at Quarter 2, you will find the Quarter 1 plus Quarter 2 in as strong a place as rest of the channels.
We expect a major part of it comes through productivity and the rest through cost rationalization.
But we are cautious that this may play out in the second half of the year.
Over the years, we have managed to bring this channel profitability very close to our retail profitability.
544403|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on headline growth, margin expansion and store roll-out, and openly described Q1 wholesale as a timing shift. It was cautious on H2 demand from consumer wallet inflation and on 3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3, and it deflected on brand-wise revenue splits and gross margin drivers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose 50 bps to 16% and Emerging Brands margin rose 240 bps to 4.3%, but gross margin fell about 150 bps and 3-4% cost inflation is expected in Q2-Q3, mostly to be offset by productivity and small price hikes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Guided more than 300 gross and 150-200 net store additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures, on a base of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft), with 65-68 gross openings already in Q1; Van Heusen distribution to add about 20% over the next couple of years from 38,000-40,000 outlets.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth, and management expects early double-digit retail growth backed by 150-200 net store adds and small-town stores growing above 15% versus about 10% in metros.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only early double-digit retail growth and no explicit revenue or margin upgrade; Q1 wholesale was 5% on a festive timing shift and H2 caution was voiced.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged 3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and caution on H2 consumer wallet pressure, with wholesale at 5% growth in Q1 and gross margin down about 150 bps.

rows.label: Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing evens out
rows.why: Wholesale grew only 5% in Q1 on a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2, and management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to match other channels, with underlying secondary growth in early double digits.

rows.label: Small-town retail share rising to over 20%
rows.why: Small-town (about 500 stores) is 15-16% of retail revenue, growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros for five straight quarters; management expects it to exceed 20% of portfolio.

rows.label: Reebok BIS certification renewal for imports
rows.why: Two Reebok factories outside India still operate pending BIS annual renewal, and Reebok revenue of about Rs 500 crore relies on imports while domestic sourcing is being built up.

tone.note: Management was confident on double-digit growth, margin expansion and store roll-out, and framed Q1 wholesale as a timing shift; it was cautious on H2 wallet pressure and 3-4% Q2-Q3 cost inflation, and deflected on gross margin drivers and brand-wise splits, which analysts pressed on.

544403|2026-09.headline: ABLBL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR2,266 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 60 bps to 17.2%, with PAT more than doubling to INR53 crore.
544403|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR2,266 crore, led by Lifestyle Brands (+9%, INR1,906 crore) and Emerging Brands (+27%, INR371 crore). EBITDA rose 15% to INR390 crore with margin up 60 bps to 17.2%, and PAT grew 126% to INR53 crore. Retail like-to-like growth was 5.3% in Q2 but September LFL was zero due to the festive-calendar shift, while the company added over 100 stores, its highest quarterly addition in more than 2 years. Management guided to continued double-digit growth in steady state, a net debt target of about INR600 crore by Q4, and capex of about INR300 crore on track.

financial_highlights.change: Down vs same period last year

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,906 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR371 crore (+10%), margin 19.5%. Retail LFL 5.3% in Q2 and 6.6% in H1; September LFL was zero due to festive shift.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR371 crore (+27%), like-to-like growth 11%, EBITDA margin 6.8% (+530 bps). Reebok opened its 250th India store; management expects over 300 Reebok stores by year-end.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail revenue +8% YoY with LFL 5.3% across 3,000+ stores; small-town network (500+ stores) has delivered double-digit LFL for six consecutive quarters. Network at 3,434 stores across 800+ cities, about 5.1 million sq ft.

segments.name: Wholesale and e-commerce
segments.commentary: Wholesale grew 18% and e-commerce 12% YoY. Management said e-commerce secondary sales were healthy double-digit through H1.

guidance_outlook: Management expects steady-state double-digit growth; aspiration remains around 15% but management earlier guided 11-12% revenue and slightly better EBITDA growth.
Like-to-like growth steady state of 7-8%, per management.
Net debt target close to INR600 crore by Q4 FY27 from about INR950 crore currently; management said broadly on track.
Capex for FY27 about INR300 crore, more or less on track.
Price increases of about 6% taken for the season, with the full effect expected in Q3; a small part reflected in Q2.
Management expects one profitable quarter for Innerwear this year.
Festive season started encouragingly; management expects an even stronger H2. H2 store closures expected to be lower than H1 (about 90 net closures in H1 from about 180 gross additions).
capex_capacity: Over 100 stores added in Q2, highest quarterly addition in more than 2 years; management aims to sustain this pace and expects Q3 and beyond expansion to be stronger.
Retail network 3,434 stores across more than 800 cities and towns, about 5.1 million sq ft.
Reebok: 250+ exclusive stores; target above 300 by year-end; typical store 1,000-1,100 sq ft.
H1 gross store additions about 180 with net addition about 90 (closures about 90-100).
Capex guidance about INR300 crore for FY27, on track.
demand_pricing: Like-to-like Q2 5.3%, H1 6.6%; September LFL zero due to festive shift, which management said would have been about 8%+ otherwise.
Small towns: about 2,500 towns (population below about 1.5 lakh), about 500+ stores, about half Peter England; they contribute about 5-6% of sales.
Casual vs formal mix about 51:49 or 49:51 per management; Q3 expected to be more wedding-heavy.
VYBE collection contributes about 10% of sales in stores carrying it and brought about 50,000 new consumers in their 20s.
Price increase about 6% against cost inflation; management says vendor partners absorbed part of cost increases.
Pre-Ind AS margin not reported quarterly; management says it improved and will be shared once a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit growth continue into Q3 and can growth move closer to 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit is expected in steady state, with expansion stronger in Q3 and beyond; it declined to commit to 15% and said aspirations remain higher than 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases and inflation are in the portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6% price increase taken for the season, with the full effect in Q3; a small part is in Q2 with a mix of old and new inventory, and vendor partners absorbed part of costs.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt targets and net cash positive goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Target close to INR600 crore net debt by Q4; currently about INR930-950 crore, and H2 cash flows are stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Why no operating leverage on a pre-Ind AS basis (analyst-computed H1 margin about 6.1% vs 6.4%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the analyst's calculation is not the correct method for pre-Ind AS margin due to store openings and closures; margins improved at all levels and MIS EBITDA grew a couple of points faster than sales, with advertising investment.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging brands margin drivers and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are operating leverage, discount reduction, store-level leverage at double-digit LFL, and lower store costs; Reebok should eventually match other brands' margins less royalty.

qa_highlights.question: E-commerce slowed to 12% growth; what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce mixes marketplace and B2B; secondary sales were healthy double-digit through H1. Q3 growth expected to stay around H1 levels, not Q1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: When will Innerwear break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Innerwear India EBITDA margin of 6.5-6.8% vs 1.5% a year ago and said it expects one profitable quarter this year.

risks_watch: Price increase of about 6% may face consumer pushback and lead to higher discounting.
Raw material and vendor cost inflation, with the bigger impact expected in H2.
Pre-Ind AS margin disclosure is annual only, so analysts cannot verify lease-adjusted margin trend quarterly; questions remained open.
Like-to-like was zero in September; festive timing may distort Q3 comparisons.
Net debt reduction to about INR600 crore by Q4 depends on H2 cash flows.
Management did not commit to 15% growth; current guidance is 11-12% revenue growth.
544403|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on brand and store momentum and on Emerging Brands margin, but guarded on the 15% growth ambition and evasive on pre-Ind AS margins and lifestyle-only store counts, which were deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Importantly, this marks our 4th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth and 5th consecutive quarter of margin expansion.
So while Q2 was good on expansion, I think Q3 and beyond should be even better on expansion.
Our holy grail, Abhijeet, is always going to be built around how do we keep driving greater throughputs from our retail stores.
Margin has expanded, so you'll have to help me understand where you got that. We've actually expanded margin.
We're pushing ourselves very hard to be able to deliver that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose 60 bps to 17.2% and H1 by 50 bps to 16.6%; Emerging Brands margin up 530 bps to 6.8% on operating leverage and discount reduction, and ~6% price increase has full effect in Q3 with vendors absorbing part of cost inflation, though raw material inflation is expected to hit more in H2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Over 100 stores added in Q2 (highest in 2+ years), H1 gross additions ~180 with net ~90, management expects Q3 and beyond expansion to be stronger, and Reebok targets 300+ stores by year-end from 250 today.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail LFL 5.3% in Q2 and 6.6% in H1 with steady-state LFL of 7-8%, plus wholesale +18%, e-commerce +12%, and Q3 expected to be more wedding-heavy; ~6% price increase means part of growth is price.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex program or capacity announcement discussed; the existing ~INR300 crore FY27 capex is on track, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to commit to 15% growth and kept revenue guidance at 11-12%, with steady-state double-digit growth only; Q2 revenue +11% and H1 +11% sit within that range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: September LFL was zero due to festive shift, price increases may cause discounting, and raw material and vendor inflation is expected to bite more in H2, while net debt target depends on H2 cash flows.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was discussed beyond VYBE collection's existing ~10% share of sales in stores carrying it.

rows.label: Net debt to ~INR600 crore by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Net debt was about INR950 crore (INR956 crore in Q2) and management said it is broadly on track to reach close to INR600 crore, with stronger H2 cash flows, though this depends on those flows.

rows.label: Innerwear profitable quarter this year
rows.why: Innerwear India EBITDA margin rose to 6.5-6.8% from 1.5% a year ago and management expects one profitable quarter this year.

rows.label: Small-town network LFL momentum
rows.why: Small-town network of 500+ stores has delivered double-digit LFL for six consecutive quarters and contributes about 5-6% of sales, supporting volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on store and brand momentum, Emerging Brands margins and deleveraging, but guarded on the 15% growth aspiration and evasive on pre-Ind AS margins, which were deferred to offline follow-up; analysts pushed on operating leverage, pre-Ind AS margin and e-commerce slowdown.

544405|2026-03.headline: Belrise Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn with EBITDA margin at 11.4%; FY26 adjusted PAT up 41% to INR5,020 mn.
544405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn and manufacturing revenue grew 21% to INR21,763 mn, while EBITDA rose only 5% to INR2,901 mn, with margin at 11.4%. Adjusted PAT rose 17% to INR1,290 mn, with a one-time INR94.7 mn operational loss at the aerospace and defence subsidiary absorbed in the quarter. For FY26, total revenue grew 15% to INR95,091 mn and adjusted PAT grew 41% to INR5,020 mn. Management reported new two-wheeler and exhaust/fuel-tank orders, the Chester Hall acquisition in the UK, and guidance of mid-teens growth with broadly stable margins for FY27.

segments.name: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 83.2% of Q4 manufacturing revenue and 82.0% in FY26. Content per vehicle rose 65-70% during FY26 (management also cited 60-65% on another basis), with two-wheeler content per vehicle moving from about INR12,000 to INR20,000 including the Badve Auto Comps and Eximius merger.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.2% of Q4 and 5.2% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. Suspension business currently serves two- and three-wheeler OEMs only, not PV OEMs.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.4% of Q4 and 8.3% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. CV segment grew 32% in Q4 and 35% in FY26.

segments.name: Four-wheeler
segments.commentary: Four-wheeler business grew 71% in Q4 and 37% in FY26 (transcript initially said 31%, corrected to 37% in footnote). Content per vehicle rose from about INR25,000 to INR40,000-45,000 with the H-One acquisition.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (Belrise Aerospace and Defense)
segments.commentary: Acquired SDM (France) in Q3 FY26 and Chester Hall (UK) in Q4 FY26. Q4 carried a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 mn from startup costs, legal and professional fees and personnel costs; management expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth expected to continue, supported by the order book.
EBITDA margins expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels (FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.1%); cost pressures seen as short-term and not expected to affect medium-to-long-term margins.
Capex expected at 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue, with R&D included within this range.
Doubling four-wheeler and CV revenue versus FY25 within the current fiscal year requires about 40% to 45% growth, per management endeavour.
Final dividend of INR0.55 per share declared.
SDM expected to turn EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time Q4 loss.
capex_capacity: Bangalore brownfield expansion to supply exhaust systems and fuel tanks to a fast-growing two- and three-wheeler OEM; production slated to begin Q2 FY27 with peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Large order from a Japanese two-wheeler OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue about INR220 crore, production starting Q4 FY26-27 (transcript says 'this fiscal year').
Haridwar plant ramp-up: trial parts dispatched to a large two-wheeler OEM; peak production targeted within FY27, sourcing from Greater Noida and Pantnagar.
Chassis, battery trays and metal components for an emerging EV player; supplies expected to start Q3 of the fiscal year.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation or break-even timelines for new plants (Chennai, Pune, Bhiwandi).
Over 850 robots deployed across the company; medium-term vision is a large integrated aerospace and defence facility in India.
demand_pricing: Sector saw strong Q4 growth, helped by the GST rate cut late last year; management hopes for structural rather than pull-forward demand.
Back-to-back raw material pricing model passes steel and plastic cost changes to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.

Q4 headwinds: oil-crisis-related supply chain disruption, higher raw material, energy and logistics costs, and Haryana minimum wage increase. Fuel and labour costs expected to be passed on over time; transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs.
Two-wheeler segment only recently returned to pre-COVID peak; management sees long-term headroom.
Aerospace demand described as very strong, with OEM order backlogs of 8-10+ years; qualification cycles of 12-24 months cited as the main barrier.
Chester Hall: rejection rate 0.5%-1%; advanced discussions to transfer part of its subcontracted work to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend through the quarters, and how will the company absorb commodity, fuel and labour cost pressures to hold full-year margins stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 was hit by the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss and acquisition fees, both called one-time. Fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time; transport costs still under discussion. Full-year guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the two new two-wheeler OEM customers become over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to become very large over 2-3 years, with content per vehicle rising sharply and cross-model penetration. The Japanese OEM order is about INR200 crore annually, and the Bangalore program is one of the sharpest ramp-ups in three years.

qa_highlights.question: How much can aerospace contribute in four to five years, and can manufacturing move to India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and sees India as a best-cost base. It is in talks with OEMs to shift Chester Hall subcontracted work and new orders from Europe to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP of INR2,000 crore for?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an enabling resolution has been approved; no specific use was given, and management will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge in exhaust systems, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Edge comes from automation (850+ robots), high verticalisation, NVH engineering and stainless-steel plating capability. Management corrected the INR400 crore figure: the orders are INR220 crore and INR90 crore, about INR310 crore peak combined. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&D spend scale with aerospace and steering/high-tensile products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is included within the 6%-6.5% capex range. The R&D team has more than 163 people. Management directionally agreed on hiring and partnerships but gave no specific target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trading business be localised, spun off or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not commented on hiving off the trading business and will update later.

qa_highlights.question: Does suspension have passenger vehicle customers, and what are suspension and H-One revenue and PAT figures?
qa_highlights.answer: No PV customers yet; the suspension business serves only two- and three-wheeler OEMs, with four marquee customers, three onboarded in the last 18 months. Management did not have suspension, polymer or H-One revenue and PAT figures and will follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic strategy for FY27, and what are the content per vehicle and plant utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are chosen on customers, capabilities and verticalisation at mild valuations (book value to mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA); all four acquisitions are EPS and ROCE accretive. Content per vehicle has risen 60-65% in two-wheelers and is 40-45% in four-wheelers and CVs. Plant utilisation and break-even were not disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: management guides FY26-level EBITDA margins (12.1%) but Q4 EBITDA margin was 11.4%; watch whether the one-time INR94.7 mn aerospace loss and acquisition fees recur or fade in Q1 FY27.
Oil-crisis cost pass-through: fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time, transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs; a lag in recovery could compress margins.

Execution of new programmes: Bangalore brownfield (production from Q2 FY27), Japanese OEM exhaust/metal order (production from Q4 FY26-27), Haridwar ramp to peak within FY27, and EV-player chassis supplies from Q3; monitor ramp timing.
Aerospace: SDM expected EBITDA positive in 2027; Chester Hall transfer of subcontracted work to India is in advanced talks but not yet signed; qualification cycles of 12-24 months.

Capital and disclosure gaps: QIP of INR2,000 mn-equivalent (INR2,000 crore) approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified; plant-level utilisation and break-even not disclosed; suspension, polymer and H-One standalone revenue and PAT to follow offline; trading business hive-off undecided.
key_quotes: Our first commitment was to deliver mid -teens revenue growth while keeping our EBITDA margins stable. And I am glad to share that we achieved this.
We expect this loss to be one -time and expect SDM to be EBITDA positive in the year 2027.
At this point of time, it's only an enabling resolution.
We are unable to comment on plant-specific questions on utilization and break-even.
544405|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the headline commitments (mid-teens growth, stable margins, 4W/CV doubling, content-per-vehicle gains), with management repeatedly calling Q4 hits one-time. Evasive on specifics: declined plant utilisation and break-even, QIP use, trading business hive-off, H-One and suspension figures, and R&D hiring targets, deferring these to later updates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin broadly stable vs FY26's 12.1%, but Q4 printed 11.4% after the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss, and fuel/labour costs pass through only with a lag, so expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bangalore brownfield (peak INR90 crore revenue) starts Q2 FY27, EV-player chassis supplies start Q3 FY27, and Haridwar peak production is targeted within FY27; plant-level utilisation was not disclosed, so the size of the uplift is unverified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides mid-teens revenue growth (FY26 manufacturing revenue +17%, Q4 +21%), backed by the order book and new two-wheeler programmes (Japanese OEM ~INR220 crore peak, Bangalore INR90 crore).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided at 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (about INR5,000-5,000 crore-equivalent on FY26 base is not stated, so no number is given), and the INR2,000 crore QIP was approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified, so a new project announcement is conditional on use of proceeds.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held (mid-teens growth, stable margins, capex 6-6.5%), and management gave no sign of raising it, with Q4 margin at 11.4% below the 12.1% FY26 level.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA rose only 5% against revenue +12%, margin fell to 11.4%, and oil-crisis supply, energy and logistics costs plus the Haryana minimum wage increase are not yet recovered from OEMs, with transport recovery still under discussion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New two-wheeler exhaust/fuel-tank programmes start production: Bangalore in Q2 FY27, Japanese OEM order from Q4 FY26-27, and EV-player chassis, battery trays and metal components from Q3.

rows.label: Two new two-wheeler OEM customers scale over 2-3 years
rows.why: Management expects both new two-wheeler OEMs to become very large, with the Japanese order about INR200 crore annually and content per vehicle rising sharply (two-wheeler CPV about INR12,000 to INR20,000).

rows.label: Aerospace above 10% of revenue and India as best-cost base
rows.why: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and is in talks to move Chester Hall subcontracted work to India, but the transfer is not signed and qualification cycles run 12-24 months.

rows.label: SDM turns EBITDA positive
rows.why: Management expects SDM (France, acquired Q3 FY26) to be EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time INR94.7 mn Q4 loss, but no quarterly figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on mid-teens growth, stable margins, the 4W/CV doubling and content-per-vehicle gains, and called Q4 hits one-time; it was evasive on plant utilisation, break-even, QIP use, trading hive-off and H-One/suspension figures, which analysts pushed on.

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
544405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.

544407|2026-09.headline: Aegis Logistics posted record H1 FY27 PAT of INR866 crore (up 108%) and agreed to buy 89.8% of Tristar Holdings for US$809 million.

544408|2026-03.headline: Leela Palaces Q4 FY26: operating revenue up 12% to INR 484 crores and EBITDA up 13% to INR 266 crores, with ADR up 15% offsetting a March occupancy hit.
544408|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 484 crores and operating EBITDA rose 13% to INR 266 crores, at a 55% margin, while PAT increased to INR 172 crores from INR 117 crores. Growth was driven by ADR, which rose about 15% to around INR 32,000, while RevPAR grew only 6% as occupancy fell from 78% to 72% after the West Asia conflict disrupted international travel in March. For FY26, operating revenue grew 15% to INR 1,527 crores, EBITDA grew 19% to INR 743 crores at a 49% margin, and PAT reached a record INR 403 crores. Management said April occupancy had recovered to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected for April.

segments.commentary: Described as insulated from the war; management expects a strong rebound in May and June. Resort occupancy guided to mid-60s to late-60s for FY27.

segments.commentary: HMA fees grew double digits in Q4, helped by Hyderabad ramp-up to about 62% occupancy and ADR about 1.24x peer set, plus additional HMA fees from contract terms. FY27 management fees guided to grow double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Were March trends sharply weaker and what are April and May trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy fell on US and UK source markets while ADR held; April occupancy returned to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected, and May and June strong.

qa_highlights.question: Were there MICE cancellations, and are they deferred or lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancellations occurred in March; they were converted to credit notes and deferred over six to nine months, with a high share expected back in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Did Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore slip, and has capex changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Timing moved from FY28 to CY28 because of approval-linked construction risk; approvals and funding are in place, and capex is unchanged with no cost escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai write-off risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see a write-off possibility, that the asset was underwritten on conservative real estate pricing, and that it is evaluating daily.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other costs rise as a percentage of revenue in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to a one-time accrual for new labour code leave encashment and gratuity, plus hiring of value-driver staff; excluding this, payroll rose 8-8.5%, and management expects the ratio to decline.

544408|2026-06.headline: Leela Palaces Q1 FY27: operating revenue up 28% to INR3,520 mn and operating EBITDA up 41% to INR1,434 mn, margin 41%.
544408|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was driven by domestic demand, which offset a weak international start to the quarter caused by West Asia travel disruption. Six owned hotels (including Coorg) posted occupancy of 67.5% (vs 63.6%), RevPAR up 17% and ADR up 10%, with same-store RevPAR up 15%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded 383 bps to 41%, and consolidated PAT rose five-fold to INR488 mn despite a INR156 mn share-of-loss from the Dubai JV. Management reiterated double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.

segments.commentary: Operationally break-even but recorded an accounting loss at SPV level (interest and depreciation), flowing through as INR156 mn share of JV loss. Leela takes over operations in CY27, followed by about a year of renovation.

544408|2026-09.headline: Leela Palaces Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 36% to INR 1,877 million on 33% revenue growth; FY27 guidance kept at mid-to-high teens for H2.
