544410|2026-06.headline: Prostarm Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 76 crore, PAT up 156% to INR 5 crore, with a 25% minimum FY27 growth target reiterated.
544410|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 76 crore, up 38% YoY but down 27% QoQ from INR 104 crore in Q4, which management attributed to seasonality and deferred execution. EBITDA was INR 7 crore at an 8.55% margin (up 126 bps YoY) and PAT was INR 5 crore at a 6.05% margin. Management said the 12-13% margin guidance still holds on a full-year basis, while also guiding FY27 PAT margin to 8.5-9%. Order book stood at about INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1, and working capital days fell from 185 to 168.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY; -27% QoQ vs INR 104 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1 (about INR 1,090 crore total)

financial_highlights.change: from INR -49 crore in Q4 FY26
from about INR 254 crore as of March 2026

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage) developer projects
segments.commentary: Order book includes about INR 855-857 crore of developer business (Bihar and Karnataka/KPTCL). Management said no revenue recognition from these in FY27, only EPC billing on the standalone books; Karnataka dispute was resolved in KPTCL's favour and the company is targeting a sale of that project.

segments.name: Solar EPC and EPC orders
segments.commentary: Solar EPC order of about INR 165 crore from Solarium Green Energy, which management expects to execute fully in FY27. Adani EPC billing was largely completed in Q1 (INR 36 crore of deferred work executed); a further solar EPC order of about INR 12 crore (8.36 MWh) was won.

segments.name: Utility vs C&I BESS
segments.commentary: Company has stopped bidding for utility-scale BESS for about 10 months and is shifting to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh installations), where management says margins are better. Adani project gave about 26% gross margin in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target: minimum 25%.
Margin guidance of 12-13% EBITDA is maintained on a full-year basis, with H2 expected to be stronger; Q1 margin is affected by low turnover and high fixed-cost ratio.
FY27 PAT margin expected at about 8.5-9%, not 10%, due to higher costs from new plants, import costs and hiring.
Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant and Gujarat UPS plant both expected operational in Q2 FY27; SAP and Salesforce expected operational by end of H1 FY27.
Working capital days targeted at about 120-150 by March 2027; management aims for positive operating cash flow by year-end FY27.
Jhajjar BESS utilisation: not more than 20-25% in FY27, 40-50% in FY28 (around INR 500 crore revenue targeted in FY28); steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.2 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in final stage of commissioning; earlier delayed, management cited cost and logistics movements and a strategy shift to C&I. Commercial operation now expected by end of H1 FY27.
Gujarat: new UPS manufacturing facility progressing as planned, expected to start commercial operations in Q2 FY27.
Existing manufacturing in Pune and Navi Mumbai.

Bihar BESS (developer/rental model): yearly cash flow of about INR 16 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of INR 32.40 crore; SBI facility tied up in SPV, LC-backed by Bihar DISCOM, no corporate guarantee.
Karnataka BESS (KPTCL): annual cash flow of about INR 45.72 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of about INR 81 crore; management prioritising a sale post-COD.
demand_pricing: Order book approx INR 1,090 crore including L1. Excluding developer orders (about INR 855 crore), in-hand orders are about INR 236 crore, plus dealer business of about INR 10 crore per month, giving about INR 306-307 crore additional order in hand.
Bids under evaluation of about INR 2,000+ crore, including two large orders of about INR 1,800 crore.
Utility BESS margins under pressure: management said bidders quoted below cost assuming Chinese supply negotiations; cited China export restrictions and a 2% battery tax from 1 September.
Q1 FY27 order wins included an INR 11 crore BESS project from a corporate customer and a INR 165 crore solar EPC order.

Trade receivables: about INR 46 crore realised from the CCTNS (Pune) project in Q1, with a large further amount expected by end-August; management said most of the INR 231 crore is government-funded with no realisation risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the deferred Q4 orders (Adani INR 43 crore, SAIL INR 7 crore, South Eastern Railway INR 13 crore) was executed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 36 crore has been executed. Adani is almost fully billed; SAIL and South Eastern Railway are to be billed mainly in Q2, with some South Eastern Railway work spilling into Q3 pending site clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue fall 27% QoQ, and is the margin guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally low and that the Adani billing was the major Q4 item. It said the 12-13% margin is a full-year target, with H2 stronger, and that Q1 fixed-cost absorption is weak at INR 76 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital days targets and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days fell to 168 from 185; target about 120-150 by March 2027. Operating cash flow improved to about INR -16 crore from INR -49 crore, with a goal of turning positive by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin should be expected from the Jhajjar plant, and what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 utilisation not above 20-25%; FY28 40-50% with around INR 500 crore revenue targeted. Steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%, with C&I focus preferred over utility BESS.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further equity dilution or significant borrowing over the next 1.5-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution is planned for at least the next year; the Bihar debt sits in an SPV, and the INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital. Any future dilution would be tied to a major expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables position and realisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables fell from INR 254 crore (March) to INR 231 crore (June) and dropped further by mid-August. Management expects about half to be collected by end-Q2, with most of the Solarium EPC realised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on order inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR 1,090 crore order book and bids of INR 2,000+ crore under evaluation, and expects the non-developer order book to grow over the next year as qualifications and bid participation increase.

risks_watch: Utility-scale BESS pricing: bidders reportedly quoted below cost assuming Chinese battery supply; a 2% battery tax from 1 September and China export restrictions could pressure C&I and utility margins further.

Execution timing: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh plant and Gujarat UPS plant both guided to Q2 FY27, after earlier delays; SAP and Salesforce due by end-H1 FY27. Slippage would push the H2-weighted margin and FY27 growth path.

Receivables and realisation: INR 231 crore of trade receivables as of June 2026, with the bulk tied to CCTNS (Pune); management expects roughly half collected by end-Q2. Watch for actual collections and concentration of debtors.
Margin trajectory: Q1 EBITDA margin of 8.55% versus 12-13% full-year guidance requires a steep H2 ramp; FY27 PAT margin guided lower at 8.5-9% on new plant, import and hiring costs.

Developer BESS projects (about INR 855-857 crore order book) recognise no revenue in FY27 per management; Karnataka sale and Bihar SBI facility in SPV are pending. Dilution: management said no equity dilution for at least one year barring a major expansion, while INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital.

Order inflow: bids under evaluation of INR 2,000+ crore, including two orders of about INR 1,800 crore; non-developer order book about INR 236 crore plus dealer business. Outcome of these large bids is a key swing factor.
key_quotes: And by the end of quarter two, you would find a significant drop in the overall data. And numbers coming almost half of it.
So that's the reason considering our size we are not focusing on utility at all.
So that's the reason we are targeting that utilization would not be more than 25% so that we can concentrate on a high margin and C&I segment business.
There are some more developments which are happening which I cannot discuss with you right now.
544410|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the full-year targets (minimum 25% growth, 12-13% EBITDA margin, positive operating cash flow by FY27-end) but cautious and at times evasive on utility-scale BESS pricing, Jhajjar utilisation for FY27 ("I am not very confident on conveying the exact capacity utilization") and undisclosed "developments" in BESS. Answers on Q1 seasonality and receivables were specific, while the Jhajjar delay explanation was vague.

rows.why: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant in final commissioning with COD guided by end of H1 FY27, and Gujarat UPS plant guided to start in Q2 FY27; both are under construction with dates, though Jhajjar was delayed earlier.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets minimum 25% FY27 revenue growth on ~INR 1,090 crore order book (about INR 236 crore ex-developer plus ~INR 10 crore/month dealer business), a INR 165 crore Solarium EPC order, and Q1 revenue up 38% YoY, though Q1 fell 27% QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS and Gujarat UPS plants are due to start operations in Q2 FY27, with SAP and Salesforce by end-H1 FY27 and a shift to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh) under way.

rows.label: Working capital days to 120-150 and positive operating cash flow by March 2027
rows.why: Working capital days fell from 185 to 168 in Q1 and operating cash flow improved from INR -49 crore to INR -16 crore; management is targeting 120-150 days and positive OCF by FY27-end.

rows.why: Large bid outcomes would add materially to the INR 1,090 crore order book, but are not yet awarded and utility BESS pricing is under pressure from below-cost quotes.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25% growth, 12-13% EBITDA and positive OCF targets, but cautious and evasive on utility BESS pricing and Jhajjar FY27 utilisation (20-25%); analysts pressed on margin ramp, receivables and dilution.

544410|2026-09.headline: Prostarm H1 FY27 revenue rose 62.3% YoY to INR 196 crore, but Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 7.83% as costs and low-margin third-party sales weighed.
544410|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 82% YoY to INR 120 crore, but EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR 9 crore with margin at 7.83%, and PAT fell about 27% to INR 6 crore (5.08% margin). Management attributed margin compression to low-margin third-party power and other product sales, higher freight (said to have almost doubled), forex impact on fixed-price contracts, higher employee and overhead costs, and start-up costs of the Bhachau and Bakrol plants. Order book stood at about INR 1,121 crore across 97 projects at 30 September 2026, with 78% government. Working capital cycle lengthened to 192 days from 185 days, mainly on receivables and inventory build, and operating cash flow remained negative.

financial_highlights.value: Net cash of about INR 97 crore cited versus about INR 105 crore borrowings-linked figure as stated; unclear on transcript

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: About INR 178 crore of the order book (about 16%); selective, high-value solar EPC work is being taken, with volumes elevated in FY27 but expected to moderate in FY28 unless high-value orders are won.

segments.name: Developer / BESS projects
segments.commentary: Developer projects of about INR 854 crore (government, 12-year annual rental of about INR 62 crore) and total VSS/EPC/developer book of about INR 999 crore (about 81%). Management is in talks to downsell two developer projects to a buyer.

segments.name: Manufactured power solutions (UPS)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 26 crore; Bakrol UPS plant (about 3,000 pieces per day, 1 kVA to 600 kVA) can generate about INR 500-600 crore revenue per year at full utilisation.

segments.name: Third-party power and other products
segments.commentary: Low-margin third-party sales contributed to margin dilution in Q2 FY27; management said one third-party billing was executed in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 500 crore, based on about INR 266 crore order in hand plus about INR 20-25 crore of monthly billing additions.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to remain above 11%, lower than the earlier 13-14% range; management described it as a moderation with FY27 revenue growth expected to be strong.

FY28 guidance: revenue growth of about 25% described as a minimum expectation; EBITDA margin expected to recover toward 12-13% and later about 18%; BESS-led margin of 8.5-9% described as achievable if BESS volumes come through.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27; management described this as a target rather than a commitment.

Bhachau BESS plant (1.2 GWh, single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts) expected to contribute from FY28; BESS capacity utilisation expected at 25-30% in FY28, with peak utilisation in about three years.
capex_capacity: Bhachau, Gujarat: 1.2 GWh BESS assembly plant, single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts; about INR 1,000 crore potential revenue per year at full utilisation.
Bakrol, Gujarat: UPS assembly facility with lithium integration, about 3,000 pieces per day; potential INR 500-600 crore per year.
Both facilities commenced operations on 25 September 2026; Bakrol expands UPS capacity across the 1 kVA to 600 kVA range.
Inventory rose to about INR 120 crore from about INR 77 crore to support new plant output and lead times (BESS lead time over three months).
Lithium cells will still be imported; BESS assembly is in-house but no backward integration yet.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR 1,121 crore across 97 ongoing projects at 30 September 2026; 78% government, 22% private.
Management cited India BESS market growth of more than 8x between FY25 and FY34 and data centre capacity rising from about 1,150 MW (December 2024) to about 3,200 MW by FY30.
Government VGS scheme (about INR 14,500 crore, 30 GWh) with about 40% local content requirement, and a PLI of 10 GWh, cited as support for domestic BESS manufacturing.
Management says pricing pressure is high from new entrants in BESS and UPS; it is shifting to selective tenders with high ticket size and private/channel business.
Average BESS order ticket about INR 40-50 lakh; utility-scale solar pricing pressure described as continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-14% FY27 EBITDA margin still achievable, and what is the H2 margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margin would be above 11% and H2 would see moderation in costs; freight roughly doubled and forex hit fixed-price contracts. It has about INR 266 crore order in hand for FY27 revenue of about INR 500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline temporary or structural, and how will working capital and receivables evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it temporary, linked to low-margin third-party sales and start-up costs at new plants. Average receivable days were about 100 (about 178 excluding one large September billing of about INR 86-90 crore). Receivables fell from INR 257 crore at H1 to INR 201 crore in October 2026 after about INR 73-75 crore of collections.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking to downsell its developer projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with about six to seven industry players to sell down its two developer projects; no timing given beyond possibly this or next quarter. Equity IRR on these projects was said to be above 12% before margin erosion from lithium and dollar costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS capacity ramp and when will scale benefits show?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhachau plant (1.2 GWh single shift) is expected to contribute from FY28 with 25-30% utilisation next year; peak utilisation expected in about three years. Export samples of about 16 kWh units shipped to an overseas customer, with volume expected next financial year if approved.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate as BESS and solar become more commoditised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on local content, technical solutions, and OEM/technology partner positioning rather than a typical EPC; it is targeting selective tenders above INR 5 crore and private sector channel partners.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on FY28 BESS volume ramp and cost normalisation (freight, forex, lithium); management's margin guidance has been revised down from 13-14% to above 11% for FY27.
Working capital cycle at 192 days and negative operating cash flow (about INR -17 crore at September 2026 per management) remain key watch items.
Possible sale of two developer projects (INR 854 crore book) may create margin depletion and changes to the order book.
Competitive pricing pressure from new entrants and rising input costs in BESS and UPS.
Collection of about INR 201 crore receivables, including two large parties expected by December 2026.

Answers on working capital and cash flow were detailed but partly qualitative, and the company declined to give long-term margin targets or name export customers.
key_quotes: Our focus was on delivering numbers. Even if the margin is on the lower side, important for us to have the regular billing done on the books.
We would try to maintain Paras G, but still it should be above 11 percent.
So 25% is a minimum expectation that we are keeping an eye on a financial year.

rows.why: Management is in talks with six to seven industry players to sell down the two developer projects, which could reduce the INR 999 crore VSS/EPC/developer book (about 81% of orders) and may deplete margin.

rows.why: Management says pricing pressure is high from new BESS and UPS entrants and utility solar pricing pressure continues, with the company shifting to selective tenders above INR 5 crore to protect margins.

544411|2026-03.headline: Scoda Tubes FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR518.7 crore and PAT 22% to INR38.8 crore, while Q4 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore after a March gas shutdown.
544411|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a transition year with revenue up 7% to INR518.7 crore, EBITDA of INR76.2 crore and margin down to 14.7% from 16.1%. Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore, EBITDA margin 13.5% and PAT down 7% YoY to INR6.3 crore, as a 15-17 day PNG gas-driven plant shutdown in March cut production by about 40% for the month. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 25% with 14-15% EBITDA margin, backed by a 8,000 MTPA welded expansion (INR40 crore) on top of the 13,000 MTPA welded line funded from IPO proceeds. Capex was INR110 crore in FY26 and about INR100 crore is planned for FY27.

financial_highlights.value: around INR175 crore, executable in 3-4 months

segments.name: Seamless (piercing mill)
segments.commentary: Seamless capacity raised to 20,000 MTPA, total capacity 21,000 MTPA in FY26; piercing plant was shut for about 15-17 days in March on gas shortage and resumed in April. Seamless utilisation expected around 70% in FY27 and optimum in FY28.

segments.name: Welded
segments.commentary: New welded facility targeted to be operational in H2 FY27 with trial runs by end-Q2 FY27; 13,000 MTPA line funded from IPO, plus 8,000 MTPA (INR40 crore) from internal accruals, taking welded capacity to 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28. Welded utilisation expected around 25% in FY27; optimum FY29.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: India INR339 crore, Europe INR137.8 crore, Americas INR30.7 crore, others INR8.9 crore. Management cited domestic INR344 crore and export INR174 crore on the analyst's summation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 25%, with domestic about 20% and export about 25%; management called this conservative and will revisit in H1 FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%.
Target FY27 revenue mix of roughly 40% export and 60% domestic.
Inventory days expected to fall from 217 days to about 160 days in FY27 and remain 160-170 days thereafter.
Peak debt expected to rise by about INR50 crore to about INR250 crore in FY27; debt to decline once new capacity is fully utilised.
No further equity dilution planned; new capacity funded by internal accruals and term loans. No new seamless capex planned; further capex decision deferred to FY29-FY30 based on market conditions.
Solar project (8.79 MWdc: 4.99 MW seamless, 3.8 MW welded) expected to generate about 137 lakh kWh a year and save about INR8-8.63 crore a year in power cost.
Power and fuel cost about 17% of total expenses; gas prices up about 25%, to be passed through to customers.
Management said operations are fully normalised for Q1 FY27 with a higher cost base, and the plant is running at full capacity.
capex_capacity: Seamless capacity 20,000 MTPA, total 21,000 MTPA as of FY26 after additional lines and equipment.

Welded: 13,000 MTPA from IPO proceeds (capex INR45 crore, still underway); equipment from China expected July-August 2026 after delay from geopolitical and logistics issues; trial runs targeted end-Q2 FY27.

Additional 8,000 MTPA welded (INR40 crore, internal accruals and term loans) expected around Q1 FY28; total welded 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28; optimum utilisation FY29. Welded range extended to 16 inches.
IPO proceeds of INR220 crore: about INR27 crore spent on capex and INR50 crore on working capital; about INR74.2 crore remaining in bank.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crore. Mother hollow mill supplies 70% captive consumption, targeting full captive by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material is stainless steel round bar made from imported scrap; base-material prices up 25-30% due to the war. Management said these are passed through to customers at order booking or dispatch.
LPG and gas prices remain elevated; cost pressure passed to customers with a lag. Management said demand is intact and only pricing is affected.
Export end-use: about 50% oil and gas, the rest engineering, automotive, power, and cooling industries. Europe pending Rina marine approval for Italian market, expected within 3-4 weeks.

Domestic power demand hinges on a BHEL tender now expected June-July 2026 (earlier slipped from Nov-Dec 2025 and Mar-Apr 2026); Scoda is BHEL- and NTPC-approved and works with BARC. Power sector demand is for seamless tubes.
Data centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment demand targeted through welded pipes; no data-centre order book yet, with inquiries on hand and orders expected around Q4 FY27.
Receivable days rose sharply (receivables up 36% vs revenue up 7%), attributed to industry-wide supply chain disruption and longer payment cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the high-diameter welded pipe capex delayed from Q3 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed geopolitical shortages, higher logistics and energy costs, and container and shipping constraints for machines from China. Delivery now expected July-August, against a prior plan of Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 weakness and was it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March gas shutdown (about 15-17 days, roughly 7-8 March to 21-22 March) was the largest headwind; without it, Q4 revenue could have been about INR140 crore. Demand is intact, and gas availability has normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the planned acquisition withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cross-border remittance, regulatory, banking and forex constraints, plus the EU safeguard duty rising from 25% to 50% and a tariff-rate quota cut of 50% from 1 July, which removed the benefit of a European entity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for FY27 guidance and domestic/export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is conservative: domestic about 20% and export about 25% growth, with the mix targeted at 40% export and 60% domestic. Upside is seen from a BHEL win and data-centre welded demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the shift from 8-inch to 16-inch welded pipe made?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers in data centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment packages prefer one supplier covering up to 16 inches, so Scoda extended its welded range beyond 8 inches. Above 16 inches needs a different A358 technology.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise despite lower borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to borrowings for ongoing capex, the solar project and higher working-capital use, plus interest on delayed income tax payments.

risks_watch: Gas and LPG cost inflation and supply continuity; a repeat of March-type shutdown would hit volumes again.
Raw material (imported scrap-based stainless round bar) volatility, with a 25-30% rise to be passed through on order booking; lag risk on margins.
Delays in welded equipment delivery (July-August) could push welded commissioning beyond H2 FY27.
Receivable days and inventory days (217 days, target 160-170) affect working capital and debt, with peak debt near INR250 crore.
Order book of INR175 crore covers only 3-4 months; large export and BHEL tender timing (June-July) is uncertain.
Management withheld volumes, utilisation by segment, realisation per ton, EBITDA per ton and order-book split, limiting transparency.
Q4 FY26 PAT fell 7% and the company says the Q4 margin was hit by under-absorbed fixed costs; benchmarking against peer margins was declined.
Management agreed to consider quarterly calls and disclosure of new orders, as requested by an analyst, with no commitment.

Guidance is described as conservative and subject to review in H1 FY27 given geopolitical uncertainty.

So, for now, we don't have any plan for diluting any more equity.
Yes, sir. Everything is smooth now. Everything is normalized, just a little bit higher cost.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: H2 FY27 for 13,000 MTPA welded line (trials end-Q2 FY27); H1
rows.why: IPO-funded 13,000 MTPA welded line is under construction with China equipment due July-August 2026 (INR45 crore), and an extra 8,000 MTPA (INR40 crore) is approved for around Q1 FY28, though welded utilisation is only ~25% and equipment delays already slipped the timeline from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 25% (domestic ~20%, export ~25%) against an order book of about INR175 crore executable in 3-4 months, though Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore after a March gas shutdown that cut production about 40% for the month.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR100 crore is already planned, no new seamless capex is planned, and further capex is deferred to FY29-FY30 based on market conditions; seamless utilisation is guided ~70% in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called the 25% FY27 revenue guide conservative and will revisit it in H1 FY27, with upside from a BHEL win and data-centre welded demand.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include a repeat of March-type gas shutdown, welded equipment delay beyond July-August, a BHEL tender slipping again (already slipped twice), and receivables up 36% vs revenue up 7%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Welded range extended to 16 inches for data-centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment demand; no data-centre order book yet, with orders expected around Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Gas and raw-material cost pass-through
rows.why: Gas prices up about 25% and base material up 25-30% are passed through at order booking or dispatch with a lag, while management says demand is intact.

rows.label: Europe Rina marine approval for Italian market
rows.why: Approval is pending and expected in 3-4 weeks, but the acquisition was withdrawn and EU safeguard duty rises from 25% to 50% with a 50% tariff-rate quota cut from 1 July.

rows.label: BHEL tender for power-sector seamless tubes
rows.why: Tender has slipped from Nov-Dec 2025 and Mar-Apr 2026, and a win is the cited upside to FY27 guidance, with the order book only about INR175 crore covering 3-4 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term growth story, normalisation and the 25% FY27 guide (called conservative), but withheld pricing, volumes, realisation, order-book split and peer comparison; analysts pushed on Q4 weakness, the delayed welded capex, the withdrawn acquisition and finance cost

544411|2026-09.headline: Scoda Tubes Q2 FY27 revenue rose just 2.5% to INR148.9 crore while operating EBITDA margin fell 479 bps to 10.6%.
544411|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was broadly flat year-on-year at INR148.9 crore, with H1 FY27 revenue up 12.6% to INR273.3 crore. Operating EBITDA fell to INR15.8 crore from INR22.3 crore, as power, fuel and freight costs rose and private-player competition stopped price hikes. Inventory built up as production stayed high and sales conversion slowed. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth guidance, pinned on the welded expansion starting trial production in Q4 FY27, but declined to give margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +2.5% YoY vs INR145.3 crore in Q2 FY26
+12.6% YoY vs INR242.7 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Domestic INR93.8 crore (63%); export INR55.1 crore (37%)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR22.3 crore in Q2 FY26
mainly machinery shipments and solar plant
long-term debt up from about INR40 crore to nearly INR100 crore per analyst

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: Order book about INR185 crore, of which roughly 40% is export (US and Europe customers); execution time about 4-5 months. Management targets about 70% capacity utilisation in FY27, rising to 80-85% next year; 80-85% is the stated optimum. Seamless working capital cycle about 180-185 days.

segments.name: Welded pipes
segments.commentary: Expansion extends capability to 16-inch pipe; trial production in Q4 FY27 and revenue from January 2027. Welded working capital cycle about 130-140 days; gross margin about 25%, versus about 32-33% in seamless. Target end-markets: data centres, HVAC, cooling, industrial water treatment and desalination.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% reiterated; analyst computed this implies about 30-35% YoY growth in H2, which management did not dispute.
Management said Europe, despite the quota regime, is on track for its 25% annual growth guidance.
No specific EBITDA margin guidance; management said it is premature given geopolitical uncertainty, and that its priority is protecting the Q2 FY27 margin level.
Peak debt expected at INR250 crore, with no immediate plans to reduce it.
Additional 8,000 MTPA welded brownfield capacity (about INR40-45 crore capex) expected in April-June 2027 (H1 FY28), taking total welded capacity to 21,150 MTPA.
Internal capex targets are 15-20% IRR; long-term ROCE target 15-20%.
capex_capacity: Welded expansion to 16-inch pipe: trial production in Q4 FY27 (Jan 2027 revenue start, per management); solar for welded operations also due Q4 FY27.

Additional 8,000 MTPA brownfield welded capacity: civil works under way, long-lead equipment procurement on track, commissioning H1 FY28; capex about INR40-45 crore, funded by internal accruals and long-term debt.
Captive solar: 4.99 MW DC for seamless operations energised and grid-synchronised in August 2026, already offsetting power cost.

Management said remaining capex on the 20,000 MTPA programme is budgeted at about INR45 crore for the 8,000 MTPA addition, with a further INR40-50 crore for the remaining 12,000 MTPA. Analyst's 20,000 MTPA reading was clarified as 8,000 MTPA. No other capex is planned.
Seamless capacity utilisation: about 70% targeted for FY27; company declined to disclose the FY27 actual.
RINA Marine audit completed July 2026; final approval awaited.
demand_pricing: Seamless competition: about 60,000-70,000 MTPA of new private seamless capacity (hot and cold) cited; management said it limits price pass-through, so realisations are largely flat.

Domestic revenue fell about 12% in Q2; oil and gas demand weak, with capex deferred and higher crude prices. Power sector (BHEL, NTPC) and some chemicals are the main domestic demand sources; BHEL tender timing is uncertain.
Export: Europe slowed under EU quota and anti-dumping duty regime (duty rates 5-25% per quarter); customers moving to quarterly buying and bonded warehouses. US performing well.
Management said revenue growth in Q2 came from volume rather than value, because of pricing pressure.
Chinese imports of ordinary grades said to be falling to near negligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the welded line delayed, and when does the 8,000 MT line start?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction slipped 2-3 months after gas-supply disruptions in March-April 2026. Welded revenue from January 2027; the 8,000 MT line is expected around April-June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15-16%, or do they settle at 11-13% given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Power and fuel rose from 3% to 4.9% of revenue and freight from 1.4% to 2.9%. Competition blocked price hikes. Management declined to give margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term debt rise, and what is peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt funded the 8,000 MT welded capacity and about 9 MW ground-mounted solar. Peak debt is INR250 crore with no near-term reduction plans.

qa_highlights.question: What are the welded-segment working capital cycle and the inventory outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Welded cycle is 130-140 days versus 180-185 days for seamless. Inventory days rose on higher production and slower sales conversion; management expects normalisation in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the seamless capacity utilisation and optimum level?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% in FY27 (not disclosed as actual); optimum is 80-85%, targeted for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR185 crore, roughly 40% exports; executed in 4-5 months; oil and gas softer, other sectors stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Is the moat intact against private competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited specialised SS production, approvals, accreditations and customer and export diversification. It said the current downturn is a rough patch and expects improvement after January-February 2027.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin at 10.6% in Q2 with no guidance; power, fuel and freight costs remain high and pass-through is limited.
Inventory build-up and working capital intensity (cash conversion weak); management expects normalisation in H2 FY27.
Debt rising toward INR250 crore peak; interest burden against flat revenue.
Welded trial production and revenue timing (Q4 FY27 / January 2027) and the 20-25% growth guidance, which implies a sharp H2 step-up.
Seamless capacity additions of 60,000-70,000 MTPA; EU quota regime and anti-dumping duty affecting European exports; BHEL tender timing.
544411|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term prospects and the welded expansion, but cautious on near term. Management repeatedly declined to give margin, utilisation, per-tonne and cash-flow figures, citing competition and geopolitical uncertainty. Its answers on the Q2 margin and revenue shortfall leaned on general statements.
key_quotes: This is a rough patch which we have not seen since last 10 years.
Given the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and the limited visibility on how the situation may evolve, we believe it would be premature to provide specific margin guidance at this stage.
We remain confident of achieving approximately 70% capacity utilization for seamless product in FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA margin fell 479 bps to 10.6% (from 15.38%) as power and fuel rose from 3% to 4.9% of revenue and freight from 1.4% to 2.9%, and private competition blocks price hikes; management gave no margin guidance and is only protecting the Q2 level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Welded 16-inch expansion has trial production in Q4 FY27 with revenue from January 2027, and the 8,000 MTPA brownfield welded addition (total 21,150 MTPA) is due April-June 2027 with civil works under way and capex about INR40-45 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue grew 12.6% but Q2 only 2.5%, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% implies about 30-35% H2 growth; volume growth is backed by welded capacity from January 2027 and 8,000 MTPA in H1 FY28, but seamless utilisation is only targeted at about 70% and no order bridge was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already committed (about INR45 crore for the 8,000 MTPA addition plus INR40-50 crore for the remaining 12,000 MTPA) and management said no other capex is planned; seamless utilisation is about 70%, below the 80%+ level that would force a new announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose only 2.5% and the FY27 20-25% guidance was reiterated but not raised, while analysts see the H2 step-up as demanding and management gave no margin guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue growth of 12.6% needs about 30-35% H2 growth to hit the 20-25% FY27 target, with welded revenue only from January 2027, Europe slowed by EU quotas and duties, and domestic revenue down about 12% in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The welded expansion to 16-inch pipe is in trial production in Q4 FY27 with revenue from January 2027, targeting data centres, HVAC, cooling and desalination.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation in H2 FY27
rows.why: Inventory built up in Q2 on higher production and slower sales conversion; management expects normalisation in H2, but seamless working capital cycle is 180-185 days and welded 130-140 days.

rows.label: Peak debt at INR250 crore, no near-term reduction
rows.why: Gross borrowings were INR229.2 crore at 30 Sep 2026, with peak debt guided at INR250 crore and no immediate plans to reduce it, funding the welded and solar capex.

rows.label: Europe on track for 25% growth despite EU quotas
rows.why: Management says Europe is on track for 25% annual growth, but EU quota and anti-dumping duties (5-25%) are slowing buying and export revenue was INR55.1 crore (37%) in Q2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the welded expansion, the 16-inch launch and long-term prospects, but cautious on near-term margins and declined to give margin, utilisation and cash-flow figures; analysts pressed on the H2 step-up needed for 20-25% growth and margin recovery.

544413|2026-03.headline: Digitide Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.2% YoY to INR 800 crores, but adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores on wage code and accounting charges.
544413|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 800 crores, up 2.5% QoQ and 9.2% YoY, with Tech and Digital at 31.1% of mix and international at 38.1%. EBITDA was INR 88 crores (11% margin), absorbing about INR 4 crores of one-time wage code impact. Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores from INR 24 crores in Q3, mainly due to lease-accounting finance cost and a residual value policy change raising depreciation; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores after a INR 16 crores exceptional wage code charge. Management guided to 100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit FY27 and double-digit revenue growth, with early-to-mid teens cited.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 551 crores (+1.1% QoQ, +2.6% YoY); FY26 INR 2,170 crores, about 70% of revenue. EBITDA margin 16.3%, up 187 bps YoY.

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 249 crores (+27.2% YoY); FY26 INR 910 crores, 29.6% of revenue (up 280 bps from 26.8%). EBITDA margin 12.1%, up 289 bps YoY.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 304 crores (+16.4% YoY), 38.1% of mix; FY26 mix 37.3%, up 180 bps. Healthcare (US) revenue crossed about USD 25 million in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth in FY27-28; management quantified as early to mid-teens.
100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit of FY27 (Q4 FY27); mix (Tech and Digital and international) expected to contribute about 40% each, with operational efficiencies the rest.
FY31 target of INR 8,400 crores (USD 1 billion), of which about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; implies about 14-15% organic CAGR.
Healthcare expected at 12-15% of revenue by FY31 (USD 120-150 million); Tech and Digital at 40% and international at 50% of revenue by FY31.

Cash conversion baseline of about 70% of EBITDA; steady-state lease depreciation about INR 38-40 crores and PPE depreciation about INR 20 crores per year; management said at least one acquisition likely this year, with six targets evaluated and two at advanced stage.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 105 crores, mainly technology platforms, AI capabilities and IT and leasehold infrastructure.

Annual cash deployment roughly INR 100 crores: maintenance capex INR 70-80 crores, plus INR 15-20 crores for two large leasehold premises moving in FY26-27; balance accrues for internal growth and inorganic deals.
AI centres of excellence set up in Bengaluru and Coimbatore for a global P&C insurance client, with the deal running on Azure.
Management stated no plans to monetise physical assets; premises are largely leased, with one owned premises.
demand_pricing: Q4 TCV INR 620 crores, second consecutive quarter above INR 600 crores; FY26 TCV INR 2,355 crores.
About 15% of pipeline is hyperscaler-led (AWS, GCP, Microsoft); management linked part of the 27% Tech and Digital growth to hyperscaler deal conversion.
Top-10 customer revenue concentration fell about 200 bps; of FY26 incremental revenue of about INR 205 crores, about 45% came from new customers.
Healthcare: two new US provider-side deals won in Q1 FY27 (per management); positioned as revenue cycle management, revenue enablement and CX partner; compared with Sagility as not like-for-like.
Revenue per FTE up 11.4% YoY to INR 584k, supported by AI-led delivery and pyramid optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 growth in USD terms, and how much came from existing versus new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency growth was 5.2%. About INR 205 crores of incremental revenue was added, with roughly 45% from new customers and the rest from existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is the standalone Digitide business loss-making once Alldigi profits are excluded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; corporate costs sit in Digitide, including US and Canada sales leadership, and cost transfer pricing is applied, so standalone-versus-consolidated comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable OCF conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 70% of EBITDA is the baseline; FY26's 77% was boosted by novation catch-up after the demerger, with Q1 FY26 at -36%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and is it converting?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and contributions are now flowing through partners, with the Azure-based AI CoE deal cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PulseNerve become a recurring platform or IP revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: PulseNerve is an orchestration layer enabling large AI service deals rather than a standalone platform; DocuSense, SmartPay and DigiCollect were cited as IP assets with non-linear revenue potential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation run-rate and what does EBIT look like after the Q4 changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time PPE depreciation charge is about INR 4 crores; steady-state lease depreciation is about INR 38-40 crores, with total depreciation around INR 60-62 crores, and the 100 bps margin guidance was reiterated. Net margin guidance was declined, with management pointing to an FY26 adjusted PAT margin of 2.3% as baseline.

risks_watch: Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores in Q4 from INR 24 crores in Q3; management attributes this to lease and depreciation accounting, but the step-up in depreciation (Q4 INR 66 crores vs INR 49 crores a year earlier) and finance cost weigh on earnings.
Q4 EBITDA margin was flat at 11%, and management has pushed margin expansion timeline out; 100 bps expansion is now targeted by exit of FY27.
FY31 USD 1 billion target needs about 14-15% organic CAGR plus about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; inorganic progress and acquisition timing remain open.
Management declined to give a steady-state net profit margin, so analysts must derive it; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores in Q4 and INR 6 crores for FY26.
Watch whether DSO stays near 75 days and OCF conversion holds near 70% of EBITDA; watch hyperscaler pipeline conversion and healthcare wins.
544413|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and the FY27 outlook, but defensive and evasive on profitability: management repeatedly deflected questions on net margin, standalone profitability and EBIT, and framed Q4 weakness as accounting-driven.
key_quotes: What these numbers demonstrate is the absorptive capacity of our operational model.
We are looking at a strong 100-basis point expansion by the time we exit FY27.
Our normal target baseline for this is 70% conversion.
So, the 14% to 15% CAGR growth over the period is, we are very, very confident of that.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Annual cash deployment guided at ~INR 100 cr (maintenance INR 70-80 cr plus INR 15-20 cr leasehold); FY26 capex INR 105 cr, and balance is earmarked for internal growth and inorganic deals, but no sized new growth capex was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as new (early-to-mid-teens growth, +100 bps margin by Q4 FY27) and FY26 constant-currency growth was only 5.2%, leaving little room to raise guidance soon.

rows.why: Margin timeline already pushed out to exit FY27, Q4 EBITDA flat at 11%, adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 cr from INR 24 cr in Q3, and depreciation rose to INR 66 cr from INR 49 cr YoY; net margin guidance was declined.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PulseNerve orchestration layer and DocuSense, SmartPay, DigiCollect IP assets cited with non-linear revenue potential, but no launch dates given; healthcare (US) crossed ~USD 25 mn in FY26 with two new US provider deals won in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: At least one acquisition in FY27
rows.why: Management said it is hopeful of at least one acquisition this year; six targets evaluated, two at advanced stage, and FY31 target needs ~INR 1,700 cr inorganic.

rows.label: Net cash build and cash conversion
rows.why: Net cash rose to INR 182 cr from INR 125 cr in Q3 and DSO fell to 75 days; management baseline is ~70% OCF/EBITDA versus 76.5% in FY26 (boosted by novation catch-up).

rows.label: Healthcare (US) scale-up
rows.why: Healthcare revenue crossed ~USD 25 mn in FY26 and two new US provider-side deals were won in Q1 FY27, with 12-15% of revenue targeted by FY31.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (TCV INR 620 cr, early-to-mid-teens guide) and the 100 bps FY27 margin target, but evasive on net profitability, standalone economics and EBIT, deflecting those questions and framing Q4 weakness as accounting-driven; analysts pushed on margins and depreciation.

544413|2026-06.headline: Digitide Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.3% YoY to INR775 crore but fell 3.1% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 9.9% and TCV bookings of INR205 crore.
544413|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR775 crore, up 5.3% YoY and down 3.1% QoQ, as management deliberately walked away from low-margin work and book-to-bill slipped. Reported EBITDA was INR76.9 crore (9.9% margin), down about INR11 crore QoQ, of which INR9.9 crore was a one-off lease-related item in Q4 and about INR10 crore was new wage costs under labour codes and state minimum wage revisions. Reported PAT was INR2.9 crore with no exceptionals, the first positive group PAT after two quarters. Management called Q1 the margin trough and reiterated a 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion for FY27, while de-emphasising the revenue target.

financial_highlights.change: Down about INR11 crore QoQ; like-to-like operating decline about INR1 crore
Up INR1 crore QoQ from INR21 crore
Positive after two quarters; no exceptional items

financial_highlights.value: INR55 crore (about INR36 crore ROU, INR19 crore owned/intangible)
financial_highlights.change: Normalised guidance INR55-57 crore per quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR15 crore (about INR11 crore lease interest)

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR237 crore, 31% of total, growing 20.3% YoY. Management reports AI-led revenue of about INR15 crore (roughly 2% of revenue) from new AI projects; AI work inside BPM/T&D is not reported separately.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR296 crore, 38% of total, growing 10.2% YoY.

segments.name: BPM (India and West)
segments.commentary: Management describes it as margin-dilutive and resource-intensive in parts; deliberately selective on pursuits and repricing legacy contracts. Sequential decline cited by analysts; no segment revenue figure given in the call.

segments.name: Alldigi (standalone exclusion)
segments.commentary: Analyst cited standalone margin of about 5% excluding Alldigi; management said Q4 included dividend income not repeated in Q1. Management says Digitide standalone optics understate group profitability due to centrally held costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 200 bps reiterated; management says Q1 is the margin trough.
Lease cash outflows for FY27 guided at INR175-180 crore, unchanged.
Normalised D&A guided at INR55-57 crore per quarter.
Double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance not reaffirmed; management asked investors to measure on profitability growth rather than revenue.
USD 1 billion revenue ambition by FY31 retained as 'North Star' but not to be pursued at expense of profitability; no revised percentage growth path given yet.
Headcount (about 55,000) expected to decline over the next few quarters.
M&A to be pursued as 2-3 targeted acquisitions rather than one large deal; management says equity dilution is not an option being considered.
capex_capacity: About 55,000 employees mapped to business units; headcount on a declining trend as Tech and Digital grows and productivity improves.

Four-part operating model: business units, service lines, two go-to-market forces (West: US and Canada; India Plus), and consolidated corporate functions with a new COO office alongside the CFO office.
Platforms: payroll, insurance and collections; AI and cloud professional services (six new clients signed in the quarter); about 5.7 million AI interactions at 80-85% containment.
AI funnel of INR100-150 crore being chased; management open to a separate AI business unit with its own P&L at a future date.
No immediate plan to monetise land and buildings, which management says are held for operating use.
Lease renewal in March quarter capitalised as right-of-use asset.
demand_pricing: TCV bookings INR205 crore vs management ambition, with book-to-bill of about 11-13% in the quarter.
Customers deferring some planned bookings and billing into Q2 and Q3.
Wage cost step-up of about INR10 crore per quarter from new labour codes and state minimum wage revisions effective 1 April; active client repricing and cost-of-living adjustment talks underway.
Three large international deals being shaped with hyperscalers.
Verticals prioritised: BFS (India and West), insurance (US mid-market), healthcare; small presence in oil and gas and CMT in the US.
Management says competition in insurance is intense; approach is curated qualification of RFPs, not catch-all.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone margin ex-Alldigi around 5%; what is the forward margin and how much of the ~INR500 crore quarterly book has converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 standalone included dividend income not repeated in Q1, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Book-to-bill was 11-13% and some bookings slipped to Q2/Q3; some legacy contracts are being renegotiated.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR9,000 crore FY30/31 revenue target, including INR1,800 crore inorganic, be funded, and will there be dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will pursue build-partner-acquire, with two or three acquisitions rather than one large deal. Equity dilution is not an option the management team is pursuing; no land monetisation is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why has performance deteriorated since demerger and what verticals offer good margin growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed the period as Chapter 3 of the company, with strategy unchanged but execution, accountability and walking away from weak accounts emphasised. Tech and Digital tracks are payroll, insurance and collections platforms, AI and cloud services, and AI within BPM.

qa_highlights.question: Should Alldigi be merged, and will margins return to pre-demerger levels?
qa_highlights.answer: The board will decide on any legal merger at an appropriate time with no timeline. Management said Digitide's central costs and capabilities are interlocked with Alldigi and that the group should be viewed on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-led revenue incremental or cannibalised, and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue of about INR15 crore is net new from new and existing clients; the pipeline is INR100-150 crore across stages. Management is building dedicated AI sales and solutioning teams.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reaffirm it. Its priority is margin improvement, and it asked investors to track profitability and ROE rather than revenue.

risks_watch: Book-to-bill of about 11-13% and TCV of INR205 crore below ambition; watch whether the deferred bookings land in Q2 and Q3 as management expects.
DSO at 82 days (up 7 days QoQ) with higher receivables and unbilled balances; Q2 focus is converting these to cash.
Wage cost step-up of about INR10 crore per quarter from labour codes and state minimum wage revisions; client repricing and cost-of-living talks are not yet concluded.
Margin path depends on repricing and exits of low-margin accounts; FY27 200 bps EBITDA expansion reiterated but no quarterly margin path given.
Alldigi-related governance: standalone profitability is weak excluding Alldigi, legal merger has no timeline, and central costs are only partly cross-charged.
Revenue growth guidance was not reaffirmed and the FY31 USD 1 billion target has no revised growth path; headcount expected to decline over the next couple of quarters.
key_quotes: We are not going to chase top line for its own sake.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses spike in Q4 and why did interest cost rise?

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin sustainable at around 11% in Q1?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Contract Manufacturing revenue potential on current asset base and deposits?

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR 5 crore non-cash item and the deposits?

544419|2026-06.headline: ArisInfra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 291 crore, EBITDA up 68% to INR 31 crore, margin 10.49%, PAT INR 20 crore.
544419|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 291 crore, up 37% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 31 crore (up 68% YoY) and margin of 10.49%, up 191 bps. PAT was INR 20 crore versus INR 5 crore a year earlier. Management attributed margin expansion to a mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, whose combined share rose from about 46% to 63%. Net working capital days fell to 56 from 66 at March 2026 (about 97 in the prior quarter per an analyst exchange), and management reiterated 35-40% annual growth guidance.

segments.name: B2B supply
segments.commentary: Entry point to the network; contributed about 37% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Covers almost all construction materials.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 84% YoY and contributed about 53% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Covers stone aggregates, ready-mix concrete and asphalt; about 8.65 lakh MT delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: DaaS (Developer as a Service)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 28 crore, roughly 10% of top line, in Q1. New INR 650 crore mandate from Wadhwa Group (Mumbai); GDV under execution rose to over INR 1,800 crore from INR 1,250 crore at Q4 FY26. Management cited 60-65% EBITDA margin for DaaS.

segments.name: Asphalt (within contract manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR 53 crore from INR 30 crore in Q4 FY26; customers transacted rose to 38 from 28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.5% EBITDA margin the new baseline, and is 10.5-11% the expected range?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain is mainly mix: contract manufacturing and DaaS, which carry higher margins than B2B, rose from about 46% to 63% of revenue; management expects this to sustain for the next few quarters. Directionally, 11% next year was agreed as fair.

qa_highlights.question: How much utilisation headroom is left in contract manufacturing and how will capacity grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 65-70% on about 9 million tonnes; 2-3 million tonnes to be added in the next two quarters by recycling existing deposits, taking capacity to about 11 million tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 35-40% guidance be raised, given Q1 and Q2 are seasonally lean?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is sticking to 35-40% annual growth; first six months about 40% of sales and second half about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the credit losses and loss given default?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative ECL about INR 22 crore on about INR 3,800-4,000 crore lifetime revenue. Recoveries after legal process range from 25% to over 80%, and most new receivables are insured.

qa_highlights.question: How does supply chain financing work and does it cost interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Financiers pay vendors on day one and the company gets about 90 days to pay; interest is sometimes borne by vendors and is negotiated. Management said it accepts the interest cost to reduce working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Does DaaS expose the company to real estate risk and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a RERA promoter and does not lend or commit capital; income is a fixed monthly fee, a percentage of construction and a percentage of sales, with financial closure and bank loans in place on day one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt path and what drives the rise to INR 75-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Current net debt INR 14.5 crore, net debt-to-equity 0.02x; the rise is to fund working capital for 35-40% growth, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be stronger on cash flows. Long-term net debt-to-equity to stay at 0.5-0.6x.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the customer base and what is the DaaS sales commission benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers are 45-50% of revenue, spread across projects and regions. Management cited sales-only channels charging 2-3% and some 4-5% of GDV, arguing DaaS covers far more than sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asphalt outlook and when is the subsidiary merger completed?
qa_highlights.answer: Asphalt is about six months old, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be meaningfully higher; management expects a meaningful FY27 contribution without giving numbers. Subsidiary merger: three of four regulators have cleared it and it is at the last stage, timeline not committed.

544419|2026-09.headline: ArisInfra Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR 308 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 11.6%, with PAT up 50% to INR 23 crore.
544419|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 308 crore (+28% YoY, +6% QoQ), with EBITDA up 58% YoY to INR 36 crore and PAT up 50% to INR 23 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 32% to INR 599 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR 43 crore. Contract manufacturing and DaaS reached 66% of Q2 revenue versus 53% a year earlier. Management reiterated FY30 guidance of about INR 3,000 crore revenue and 12-13% EBITDA margin, and said growth will not need new equity.

segments.name: DaaS (Developer as a Service)
segments.commentary: GDV under execution rose to INR 2,750 crore-plus from INR 1,839 crore at end-Q1 and INR 1,267 crore at end-FY26, across 15 active projects (up from 10). Fees are 10-14% of GDV, with EBITDA margin about 59% on DaaS per management.

segments.name: Materials (B2B supply)
segments.commentary: Management is moving away from lower-value trading in select categories and redirecting repeat demand to contract-manufactured supply. No segment-level revenue figure was given for this quarter.

demand_pricing: Top-10 customer contribution is about 45-47%, spread across multiple projects and regions; no single customer is said to be concentrated.

Debtors are about 33-34% of revenue, with receivable days around 150 per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity additions and utilisation be read, given 2.6 million tons added this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the Q1 plant count (10 was partner entities; about 15 plants at 30 June) and said capacity is 9.1 to 11.7 million tons, with utilisation at 42-45%. It gives no capacity guidance and says capacity will run ahead of demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DaaS revenue benchmark and recognition method?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross fees are 10-14% of GDV. Revenue is recognised across a fixed time-based fee, a share of sales achieved and construction milestones. Projects run 6 to 30 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the path to 12-13% EBITDA margin by FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, which together are expected to reach close to 75% of sales, plus operating leverage and geographic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are working capital and investment needs changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital is at 54 days and should settle at 60-70 days at steady state. The only planned investment this year is INR 60 crore, with none planned next year; the main use of cash is material purchase funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin sustainable, and what is the DaaS competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 11.5-12% for FY27 and 12-13% by FY30 and said the margin is sustainable. It sees no direct DaaS competitor, as its end-to-end service consolidates outsourced real estate functions.

qa_highlights.question: How exposed is the business in a real estate downturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60-65% of the DaaS portfolio is plotted development, which holds up better in a slowdown. Projects are 10-14 storey towers with 13-18 month cycles, and no five-year-plus projects are taken.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vendor deposits fall, and is contingent liability a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposits fell from about INR 200 crore to INR 162 crore. Management said the INR 114 crore fixed-deposit pledge lets partners borrow from their banks against Aris's FDs, so cash stays on balance sheet and earns interest.

544420|2026-03.headline: Raymond Realty FY26 total income rose 29% to INR3,039 crores; Q4 income up 53% to INR1,176 crores with 139% YoY bookings surge.

Q4 EBITDA margin was 21.5% as stated in the opening remarks and about 21% per the Q&A. JDA share of pre-sales reached 54% in FY26, a 50:50 own-land-to-JDA mix target achieved a year ahead of FY27 schedule. Management guided FY27 blended EBITDA margin of 16% to 18%, minimum 20% growth in pre-sales and top-line, and cash-negative operations for the next two years.

Pokhran Road pre-sales were close to INR1,400 crores in FY27 to date.

segments.commentary: Seven JDA projects with combined revenue potential of about INR17,000 crores, including Kandivali (GDV INR3,000 crores, 70% revenue share to Raymond). JDAs were 22% of booking values in FY25 and 54% of pre-sales in FY26 from non-Thane land.

segments.commentary: Address by GS Wadala and Address by GS Sion together released combined GDV of almost INR6,400 crores. Sion launched on 24 March 2026, so had only about one week of selling; Park Street (retail, Thane) and TenX District 9 were also launched in Thane.

segments.commentary: First project launched by the company, about 3,100 homes, fully sold out and has received full OC during the year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Thane sales depend on each year's product mix; competition has been intense for 20 years. Average Thane sales of INR1,300-1,500 crores a year are achievable; no cause for concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why do JDA launch timelines vary so much (e.g., Mahim signed in CY23 still not launched)?
qa_highlights.answer: Each deal differs by maturity and counterparty speed. BKC took about 9 months from start; Mahim has taken about 2.5 years due to society governance issues. Average is 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook and how is it booked?

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No: management expects cash-negative operations for the next two years; internal accruals of INR600-650 crores to keep growing and be reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of commodity and Morbi gas-supply disruption on costs?
qa_highlights.answer: 3-4% cost impact possible if prolonged; no material impact if resolved in 2-3 months. Suppliers continue at contracted rates; no supply disruption; management sees no EBITDA impact.

544420|2026-06.headline: Raymond Realty Q1 FY27 booking value rose 129% YoY to INR700 crore; FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reiterated.
544420|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 booking value of INR700 crore (up 129% YoY), customer collections of INR550 crore (up 47%) and total income of INR536 crore (up 37%). EBITDA rose 70% YoY to INR70 crore, with margin expanding from 11% to 13%, which management attributed to upfront costs from four projects launched in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth, 20%+ revenue growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin and 20%+ ROCE. JDAs now account for about 52% of INR52,000 crore total GDV, and a new Parel JDA with INR8,500 crore GDV was signed.

financial_highlights.change: Gross debt INR1,095 crore; cash INR271 crore
management said FY27 interest INR100-120 crore

segments.name: JDA (asset-light) portfolio
segments.commentary: Eight JDA projects with combined GDV of INR27,000 crore (52% of total GDV); 64% of Q1 presales came from JDAs. Four launched projects (Bandra East, BKC, Wadala, Sion) carry INR11,500 crore revenue potential, INR2,900 crore cumulative sales and about INR692 crore collections.

segments.name: Owned land (Thane, 100 acres)
segments.commentary: 65 acres under active development with 6.7 million sq ft RERA carpet area and INR16,500 crore revenue potential; INR9,400 crore sold and INR7,460 crore collected to date. Contributed 36% of Q1 booking value; 11 towers (about 4,000 homes) delivered. Management expects own-land margins of 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is execution of Q4 FY26 launches; demand 'pleasantly' above expectations; cost pressures from global wars seen as temporary, with contingencies budgeted over 5-6 year project cycles; policy stable with DCR 2034 and supportive Maharashtra government.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocation and funding aligned with the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-to-equity 0.7x versus internal 1x ceiling; AIFs offering SPV-level capital as an option; equity seen as last resort; cost of debt has only declined.

qa_highlights.question: Parel project ticket size, saleable area, launch timing and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch about 18 months away; ticket sizes INR6-20 crore; total GDV INR8,500 crore; realisation not disclosed beyond GDV.

qa_highlights.question: Mahim launch timing and GDV, and H2 launch calendar?
qa_highlights.answer: Two Mahim projects: first ~Nov-Dec 2026 (~INR2,500 crore GDV), second Feb-Mar 2027 (~INR2,100-2,200 crore); six of eight JDAs to be launched by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose of TenX Mahalakshmi Limited incorporation?
qa_highlights.answer: Incorporated as an SPV in anticipation of new projects; no deal signed yet, to be disclosed when signed.

qa_highlights.question: JDA vs owned-land economics, margins and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: JDA capital need INR300-350 crore per project, peak INR450-500 crore for Parel; own land margin 25-26%, JDA ~20% scaling up in FY28; ROCE guided at 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost trajectory and debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt INR824 crore, gross debt INR1,095 crore, cash INR271 crore; FY27 interest INR100-120 crore; Q1 ~INR47 crore; government dues interest at 8-9% explained as part of finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why no PAT guidance and what about cash profit and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: No net profit or operating cash flow guidance given; management will revert on PAT growth impact of higher interest.

qa_highlights.question: Demand softness and Home Fest purpose?
qa_highlights.answer: No softness seen; Home Fest is an annual monsoon event for top-of-funnel; response described as good.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion beyond MMR and JDA control terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains MMR and Maharashtra; Pune studied but returns did not meet criteria. Company insists on 100% development control in JDAs with step-in rights.

544420|2026-09.headline: Raymond Realty Q2 FY27 total income rose 7% YoY to INR757 crore, EBITDA margin 15%, booking value up 111% YoY in H1 to INR1,602 crore.
544420|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income grew 7% YoY to INR757 crore and EBITDA rose to INR115 crore at a 15% margin versus 14% a year earlier. Quarterly pre-sales nearly doubled with no new launches, and H1 booking value reached INR1,602 crore (+111% YoY) while collections rose 67% to INR682 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, 20% ROCE and 9-10% PAT margin, and dropped explicit revenue growth guidance. An ICICI Prudential AIF subsidiary investment of INR210 crore for the Mahim project and a INR400 crore promoter equity infusion were announced, with debt held near INR1,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Stake given to ICICI AIF for INR210 crore and why the promoter preferential issue despite earlier no-fundraise stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Structured via OCPRS with economics of 40% capital, 5% turnover fee plus 50% of residual profit; coupon virtually zero and treated as equity. Promoter equity ~INR410 crore cited; management says equity raising was part of the annual plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue growth guidance still 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue guidance this year due to percentage-of-completion complexity; management said revenue would be in a similar range to 20%, with EBITDA growth of 20% and pre-sales growth of 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year interest cost exceed the INR100-120 crore range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full-year figure will be in line with H1 run-rate (H1 interest cited at INR91 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Expected debt trajectory and use of promoter money?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt will not fall for 1-2 years; expected to stay in INR1,200-1,500 crore range within 1:1 D/E. ICICI OCPRS will not be classed as debt; receipt of entire ICICI sum by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Pre-sales guidance implies ~INR2,000 crore in H2; how much from existing portfolio and Mahim product mix?

qa_highlights.question: Is weakness in luxury/ultra-luxury (Invictus Thane, BKC) structural?

qa_highlights.question: Long-term pre-sales CAGR and capital needs?

qa_highlights.question: How are construction cost increases being managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ongoing projects are fixed-price with no escalation; contingencies absorb fluctuations. Future launches to be priced to pass on part of cost increases, with margin expected to be maintained if inflation is temporary.

risks_watch: Rising construction costs (labour, cement, steel) for future launches under fixed-price contracts with limited escalation.
Debt staying at INR1,200-1,500 crore and interest cost run-rate (H1 INR91 crore); cash flow negative in early JDA years.
BKC Invictus upper-floor sales dependent on pending aviation approval and RERA registration.
Revenue guidance withdrawn for FY27; percentage-of-completion makes turnover less predictable.
Stock valuation roughly 50% below listing levels; institutional coverage limited (one analyst) and index exclusion cited.
Mahim launches (INR4,100 crore GDV) in Q3 and Q4 FY27; inventory opened at launch not yet decided.
Interest-rate sensitivity if rates rise 50-75 bp; management's view that demand is resilient is its own assessment.
544420|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and assertive on execution, pre-sales momentum and the ICICI structure, with direct answers on debt and cost. More guarded on revenue guidance (explicitly withheld) and on near-term cost inflation, which it described as a concern for the industry.

But on the ongoing project, there is no immediate impact that we have today.

It will not come down at least for the next 1 or 2 years for sure, because we are continuing to grow and we are adding new projects and we want to grow and we don't want to raise any kind of significant equity going forward.

544421|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of ~260m (30% margin) included ~46m of one-offs; adjusted ~304m (35%), with gases segment margin 40% in Q4 and 38.4% for FY26.
544421|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA was about 260 million at a roughly 30% margin, but management cited three non-recurring items totalling about 46 million (leave-encashment provision 11m, impairment on a legacy non-core investment, and a 15m settlement with an on-site customer over plant start-up date), taking adjusted EBITDA to about 304 million (about 35%). Core gases segment revenue grew 9% QoQ in Q4, and FY26 core gases revenue grew 14.2% over FY25, with reported growth held back by the delayed start of Uluberia 2. Argon prices recovered from Q3 lows but remain below 1H FY26 levels. Management framed FY27 as an execution year with a stronger capacity base, but gave no numeric guidance beyond a 20% revenue CAGR target over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Three items totalling about 46m: 11m employee leave-encashment provision, impairment on a legacy non-core investment, and a 15m settlement with an on-site customer over plant start-up date. Management said these are non-recurring and the 15-year customer contract continues.

qa_highlights.question: Will project engineering revenue grow significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant growth expected; the team is fully engaged on internal projects, which generate no billing, and external projects are unlikely to fit with planned capacity expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for argon prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 prices recovered from Q3 but are below 1H FY26; management urged viewing argon on an annual average basis and expects it to remain robust with steel-sector demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% CAGR achievable and how do capacity additions translate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% revenue CAGR over the next 2-3 years, with no single-year guidance, supported by the Uluberia 2 and East India on-site plants and further merchant additions.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA margin and power cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term aspiration is 40% EBITDA margin, supported by efficient new plants, renewable and PPA power, argon recovery and operating leverage. Management said power cost will decline as a percentage of revenue but not to about 10%.

qa_highlights.answer: About 18% of merchant capacity is on a renewable PPA; the target is PPAs for all three southern plants, subject to state policy and customer-premises constraints.

544421|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to ₹987 mn and EBITDA margin reached 39%, with PAT up 87% YoY to ₹350 mn.

EBITDA rose to ₹387 mn (+21% YoY, +50% QoQ) at a 39% margin, which management attributed mainly to new power-efficient capacity, cost control and higher production rather than argon pricing. PAT of ₹350 mn was helped by lower finance cost and a lower effective tax rate. Management reaffirmed FY27 capex of ₹250 crore and FY28 capex of ₹200 crore, and said the East India 320 TPD on-site plant should start contributing revenue in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said merchant plants are not pre-contracted; the site is chosen after a micro-market survey, contracting starts 3–4 months before commissioning, and the ramp to 80–90% utilisation takes 18–24 months. Early focus is on customers located near their factories, where the company has a cost advantage, plus new industries in the area.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about argon pricing and whether 38–39% margins are a fair base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects the business to stabilise at 40% or higher EBITDA margin as capacity unfolds, with 39% in Q1 close to that. It said argon pricing had a very limited impact this quarter, and that the margin gain came mainly from newer, more power-efficient capacity and cost control. It described 40% as a longer-term target, not a quarterly guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Which capacities does the ₹450 crore capex relate to, given East India and North India were announced earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹450 crore is for two merchant plants: North India (not yet operational) and West Central India (construction started). Together they are about 450–500 TPD. The entire residual amount of the ₹450 crore goes to these two plants.

qa_highlights.answer: Legacy plants are fully utilised. The plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 has some spare capacity. Apart from that, management said nearly all capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.question: What drove cost discipline and how will costs evolve, particularly power?
qa_highlights.answer: Power is the largest cost. Management cited newer, more efficient plants that use less power per unit of gas, plus one long-term renewable PPA signed, exchange purchases, and ongoing scouting for more long-term PPAs. Other costs such as employee and other expenses were described as having standard annual increases.
